en.name: "Firdausi's Parable of the Ship of Shi'ism"
names: Folio 18v from the Shahnama (Book of Kings) of Shah Tahmasp
description: In the introduction to the Shahnama, God launched seventy ships, bearing adherents to the religions of mankind, into a stormy sea. Clearly depicted on the central ship are the Prophet and his son‑in‑law and successor 'Ali sitting beneath the red canopy, while 'Ali’s sons, Hasan and Husain, stand nearby. Details such as the inlaid stars and figures with very small elliptical pupils are characteristic of works attributed to Mirza 'Ali, the son of the master painter Sultan Muhammad.
materials: Opaque watercolour, ink, silver, and gold on paper
tags: Opaque watercolour, ink, silver, and gold on paper

en.name: Simplon-Orient Express Poster
short_description: The Orient Express, owned by the Wagon-Lits Company, connected Paris and Istanbul between 1883 and 1977. French, German, Austrian and Ottoman diplomats and civil servants were on board for its first journey. In the early years, the travellers stayed in different hotels in Istanbul but starting from 1895, passengers stayed exclusively in Pera Palace, which was bought by the Wagon-Lits Company. The Orient Express did not run during World War I, from 1914 to 1918.
keywords: travelling; orientalism; İstanbul; express
partner: Vehbi Koç Foundation Sadberk Hanim Museum

ar.name: بئر - خزان.
description:
بئر – خزان مستدير الشكل، يقارب عمقه 20 متراً (وهو العمق الذي تم الوصول إليه أثناء الحفريات، لكن من المرجح أن يكون البئر أكثر عمقاً)، ويصل محيطه عند الحافة إلى 3 أمتار. ونظراً لوجود 2.3 متر من الماء المرئي بشكل دائم فيه، يمكن أن يكون قد بُني حسب مستوى الفرشة المائية.  
هذا البئر - الخزان عمل هيدروليكي خاص للغاية، تتكون مواد بنائه من الحجر المحلي – حجر رملي أحمر من سيلفش - مما يزيد من قيمته. من الجانب المعماري، يشكل نموذجاً عن التحكم التقني والتوظيف: يرافق درج لولبي الشكل مقبّب ضمن سرداب انحدار البئر - الخزان حتى المستوى المنخفض الذي يبلغ 16 متراً.  
غُطيَ الدرج بأكمله بدوراته الأربع بقبة رائعة كاملة الاستدارة مفصّصة. تؤمن ثلاث نوافذ في القبة منظرها الجانبي نصف دائري الربطَ مابين السرداب والدرج والبئر بحيث تفتح الطريق للماء حسب المستويات المختلفة للامتلاء، كما تفتح المجال للهواء وللإضاءة الطبيعية للسرداب.  
بُنيتْ هذه المعلمة في نهاية القرن 12 أو في بداية القرن 13 الميلادي، إلى جانب الكسوة الداخلية للسور الذي يحيط بالمدينة والذي بُني في نفس الفترة. ويبدو السور في هذا الموقع أكثر سماكة، كما يتكئ عليه برج ملاصق من الخارج.  
من الأكيد أن هذه البنيات الثلاث (السور والبرج الملاصق والبئر - الخزان) التي بُنيت في نفس الفترة كانت مهيأة لتشكل مجموعة دفاعية شكلانية ووظيفية.  
ليس هناك أدنى شك في أن وظيفة البئر - الخزان كانت تأمينَ المياه للمنطقة الواسعة المنخفضة من المدينة، وعلى الأخص الحمام الذي يبعد عنه بحوالي 100 متر.  
عند وصول المسيحيين في نهاية القرن الثالث عشر الميلادي، رُدم البئر بالتراب والحثالة ونُسيت وظيفته. وفي عام 1979، أُعيدَ اكتشافه عند القيام بأعمال تأهيل المدينة وإعادة ترصيف أرضية الموقع. ولم تكشف الحفريات الأثرية اللاحقة عن بنيته الرائعة فحسب، وإنما أيضاً عن كنز خارق للعادة من الخزفيات، من بينها قطع تعود إلى القرن 9 – 10 وحتى القرن 17 للميلاد، جرى عرضها فيما بعد في المتحف الوطني للآثار.  
يشكل البئر - الخزان اليوم جزءاً لايتجزأ من المتحف البلدي للآثار في سيلفش حيث يُعتبر القطعة الأساسية فيه، ولذلك أقيم معرض دائم حوله.  
صُنّف هذا النموذج الوحيد من نوعه عن بئر - خزان مرتبط بالفرشة المائية الجوفية معلمة وطنية منذ عام 1990.

كان هذا الخزانُ المائي أو الحوضُ الموحدي يُزود انطلاقا من الفرشة المائية لسيلفش. ينزلُ سُلم مقببٌ بشكل حلزوني إلى رواق يتواجد على عمق 16 متر. غطيت كل مساحة هذا السلم المكون من أربع دورات بقبة نصف أسطوانية مفصصة؛ وتقوم ثلاث نوافذ تعلوها قببٌ نصف دائرية بالربط بين رواق السلم والبئر، وتفضي إلى الماء، وتضمن مرور الهواء والضوء الطبيعي داخل الرواق. أحيط الخزان بكل القطع المعروضة، ويشكل اليوم القطعة الرئيسة للمتحف البلدي للآثار.
dynasty: الفترة الموحدية، النصف الثاني من القرن 6 - النصف الأول من القرن 7 الهجري / النصف الأول من القرن 12 – النصف الأول من القرن 13 الميلادي.
keywords: ماء.
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

en.name: Cistern.
description:
A water tank or cistern, circular in cross-section, almost 20 m deep (the depth reached with cleaning and excavation, but thought to be much greater) and 3 m in diameter at the mouth. As 2 to 3 metres of water can always be seen it is possible that the construction is linked to phreatic (underground) waters.  
It is a very rare work of hydraulics, built of local stone – Silves red sandstone – giving it a high quality of construction. Architecturally it is a fine example of technical craftsmanship and functionality: a vaulted spiral staircase descends alongside it for 16 metres in a gallery to the lower level.  
The entire staircase, consisting of four flights, is roofed by a magnificent segmented tunnel vault. Three windows, with semi-circular-shaped vaults, form the link between the gallery of the staircase and the well, allowing access to the water at the different levels of filling, and also provide the gallery with ventilation and natural light.  
This monument was built at the end of the AH 6th / AD 12th century or the beginning of the AH 7th / AD 13th century, close to the inner surface of the wall which runs around the *medina* (town) and which was rebuilt at the same time. In this area the wall is wider and has a watchtower built against the outside.  
Undoubtedly these three structures (wall, watchtower and cistern), built at the same time, functioned as a defensive, structural and architectural whole.  
The function of this monumental cistern was probably to supply water to most of the lower part of the town, namely the *hammam* (public baths) which was very close, some 100 m away.  
The cistern was filled in with earth and rubbish and its function abandoned with the arrival of the Christians at the end of the AH 7th / AD 13th century. It was only rediscovered in 1979, when reconstruction and repaving work was begun in that area. The archaeological excavations which followed brought to light not only the magnificent structure itself but also an extraordinary haul of ceramics, with pieces dating from the AH 3rd–4th / AD 9th–10th centuries to the AH 11th / AD 17th century, now on display in the Silves Municipal Archaeology Museum.  
The cistern is today part of the Silves Municipal Archaeology Museum, where it plays a central role, with the whole permanent exhibition arranged around it.  
This unique example of a cistern linked to phreatic waters has been classified as a National Monument since 1990.

This Almohad water tank or cistern was fed from the Silves water table. A vaulted spiral staircase descends into a gallery to a depth of 16 metres. The entire four-flight staircase is covered by a segmented barrel vault. Three windows with semi-circular vaults link the stairwell to the well, giving access to the water as well as naturally lighting and ventilating the gallery. The cistern is now the centrepiece of the Municipal Museum of Archaeology around which the other exhibits are arranged.
dates: Hegira second half of 6th–first half of 7th century / AD second half of 12th–first half of 13th century.
keywords: water; cistern
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

es.name: Pozo-aljibe.
description:
Pozo-aljibe de sección circular, de tres metros de diámetro en la boca y cerca de 20 metros de profundidad (profundidad a la que se ha llegado limpiándolo y excavando, pero se cree que era mucho más hondo). Tiene de dos a tres metros visibles de agua, lo que hace pensar que se trata de una construcción que llega al nivel freático.  
Es una obra hidráulica inusual, hecha en albañilería de piedra local –gres rojo de Silves– que le da una gran calidad constructiva. Arquitectónicamente, es un ejemplo de maestría técnica y funcionalidad: una escalera helicoidal abovedada, en galería, facilita el descenso hasta una profundidad de 16 m.  
Toda la escalera, de cuatro tramos, está cubierta por una magnífica bóveda de cañón segmentada. Tres ventanas, con bóvedas de perfil semicircular, unen la galería de la escalinata y el pozo para poder acceder al agua dependiendo del nivel de esta, además de airear e iluminar de forma natural la galería.  
Este pozo se construyó a finales del siglo VI / XII o principios del siglo VII / XIII, junto al paramento interno de la muralla que cerca la medina. En este lugar, la muralla es más ancha y tiene adosada en el exterior una torre albarrana. Estas tres estructuras (muralla, torre albarrana y pozo-aljibe), construidas en el mismo periodo, funcionarían como un todo defensivo, estructural y arquitectónico.  
El monumental pozo-aljibe tendría la función de abastecer a gran parte de la zona baja de la ciudad, especialmente el *hammam* (baños públicos) situado a unos 100 m. Hoy está integrado en el Museo Municipal de Arqueología de Silves, del que constituye la pieza central alrededor de la cual se ha organizado la exposición permanente.  
Este ejemplo único de pozo-aljibe que llega hasta la capa freática está clasificado como monumento nacional desde 1990.

Pozo-aljibe almohade que alcanza el nivel freático. Una escalera helicoidal abovedada, en galería, facilita el descenso hasta una profundidad de 16 m. Toda la escalera, de cuatro tramos, está cubierta por una bóveda de cañón segmentada. Tres ventanas, con bóvedas de perfil semicircular, unen la escalera y el pozo para poder acceder al agua y también para airear e iluminar la galería de forma natural.  
El pozo-aljibe está integrado hoy en el Museo Municipal de Arqueología, del que constituye la pieza central alrededor de la cual se organiza la exposición permanente.
dates: Segunda mitad del siglo VI–primera mitad del VII de la Hégira / XII–XIII d. C.
keywords: Agua
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

fr.name: Puits-citerne.
description:
Puits-citerne de forme circulaire d'environ 20 mètres de profondeur (profondeur atteinte lors des fouilles, mais probablement plus importante encore) et 3 mètres de diamètre à la margelle. Avec ses 2,3 mètres d'eau constamment visibles, il est possible qu'il soit bâti par rapport au niveau de la nappe phréatique.  
Il s'agit d'un ouvrage hydraulique assez particulier, construit en maçonnerie de pierre locale – grès rouge de Silves –, ce qui en rehausse la qualité. Du point de vue architectonique, il représente un exemple de maîtrise technique et de fonctionnalité : un escalier hélicoïdal voûté, en galerie, accompagne sa descente jusqu'au niveau inférieur de 16 mètres.  
L'escalier tout entier, avec ses quatre volées, est couvert d'une magnifique voûte en plein cintre segmentée. Trois fenêtres aux voûtes à profil semi-circulaire font le lien entre la galerie de l'escalier et le puits, ouvrant l'accès à l'eau d'après les différents niveaux de remplissage, mais aussi à l'air et au jour naturel de la galerie.  
Ce monument a été construit à la fin du XIIe siècle ou au début du XIIIe siècle, à côté du parement interne de la muraille qui entoure la médina et qui a été reconstruite à la même époque. Ici la muraille est plus épaisse, une tour flanquante y est adossée à l'extérieur.  
Il est certain que ces trois structures (muraille, tour flanquante, puits-citerne), dressées dans la même période, devaient constituer un ensemble défensif, formel et fonctionnel.  
Le puits-citerne avait sans doute pour fonction d'approvisionner en eau la vaste zone basse de la ville, notamment le *hammam* (bains publics), distant d'une centaine de mètres.  
À l'arrivée des chrétiens, à la fin du XIIIe siècle, on l'a bourré de terre et de déchets et sa fonction a été oubliée. Il a été redécouvert en 1979, au moment des travaux de réhabilitation et de repavage du site. Les fouilles archéologiques suivantes ont mis au jour non seulement sa magnifique structure, mais ausssi un extraordinaire trésor de céramique, avec des pièces datant du IXe-Xe siècle jusqu'au XVIIe siècle et qui sont désormais exposées au Musée municipal d'archéologie.  
Le puits-citerne fait aujourd'hui partie intégrante du Musée municipal d'archéologie de Silves, où il a le rôle de pièce capitale et autour duquel toute l'exposition permanente a été organisée.  
Cet exemple unique de puits-citerne relié à la nappe phréatique est classé monument national depuis 1990.

Ce réservoir à eau ou citerne almohade était alimenté par la nappe phréatique de Silves. Un escalier voûté en colimaçon descend dans une galerie à une profondeur de 16 mètres. Toute la surface de cet escalier à quatre volées est couverte par une voûte en berceau segmenté. Trois fenêtres à voûtes semi-circulaires font le lien entre la galerie de l'escalier et le puits, donnant accès à l'eau et assurant la circulation de l'air et de la lumière naturelle dans la galerie. La citerne, autour de laquelle sont disposés tous les autres objets exposés, est aujourd'hui la pièce maîtresse du Musée municipal d'archéologie.
dates: Seconde moitié du VIe siècle-première moitié du VIIe siècle de l’Hégire (seconde moitié du XIIe siècle-première moitié du XIIIe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: eau
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

pt.name: Poço-Cisterna.
description:
Poço-cisterna de secção circular com cerca de 20 m de profundidade (profundidade atingida com a limpeza e escavação, mas que se pensa ser muito maior) e com 3 m de diâmetro de boca. Tem constantemente visíveis 2 a 3 metros de água o que leva a pensar tratar-se de uma construção com ligação ao nível freático.  
  
É uma obra hidráulica muito rara, construída em alvenaria de pedra local – grés vermelho de Silves – que lhe dá grande qualidade construtiva. Arquitetonicamente é um exemplo de mestria técnica e de funcionalidade: uma escadaria helicoidal abobadada, em galeria, acompanha a descida até ao nível inferior de 16 metros.  
  
Toda a escadaria, com quatro lanços, é coberta por uma magnífica e segmentada abóbada de berço. Três janelas, com abóbadas de perfil semicircular, fazem a ligação entre a galeria da escadaria e o poço, permitindo o acesso à água, conforme os diferentes níveis de enchimento, mas também o arejamento e iluminação natural da galeria.  
  
Este monumento foi construído nos finais do século VI AH / XII AD ou inícios do século VII / XIII, perto do paramento interno da muralha que cerca a medina e que foi reconstruída na mesma época. Neste local a muralha é mais larga e tem adossada ao seu exterior uma torre albarrã.  
  
Certamente que estas três estruturas (muralha, torre albarrã e poço-cisterna), erguidas no mesmo período, funcionariam como um todo defensivo, estrutural e arquitectónico.  
  
Este monumental poço-cisterna teria assim como função abastecer grande parte da zona baixa da cidade, nomeadamente o *hammam* (banhos públicos) que se situava muito perto, a cerca de 100 m.  
  
O poço-cisterna foi entulhado com terra e lixo e abandonada a sua função com a chegada dos Cristãos, nos finais do séc. VII / XIII. Foi redescoberto somente em 1979, quando ali se iniciavam obras de reconstrução e de repavimentação. As escavações arqueológicas que se seguiram trouxeram à luz dia não só a magnífica estrutura mas também um espólio cerâmico extraordinário, com peças datadas desde o século III-IV / IX-X ao século XI / XVII, actualmente expostas no Museu Municipal de Arqueologia.  
  
O poço-cisterna integra hoje o Museu Municipal de Arqueologia de Silves, onde funciona como peça central e à volta da qual foi organizada toda a exposição permanente.  
  
Este exemplo único de poço-cisterna ligado ao nível freárico está classificado como Monumento Nacional desde 1990.

Poço-cisterna almóada, ligado ao nível freático de Silves. Uma escadaria helicoidal abobadada, em galeria, acompanha a descida até ao nível inferior de 16 metros. Toda a escadaria, com quatro lanços, é coberta por uma segmentada abóbada de berço. Três janelas, com abóbadas de perfil semicircular, fazem a ligação entre a galeria da escadaria e o poço, permitindo o acesso à água mas também o arejamento e iluminação natural da galeria. O poço-cisterna integra hoje o Museu Municipal de Arqueologia, onde funciona como peça central e à volta da qual foi organizada toda a exposição permanente.
dates: 2ª metade do século VI-1ª metade do século VII AH / 2ª metade do século XII – 1ª metade do século XIII AD.
keywords: poço; cisterna; Silves; almóadas; água
partner: Archaeological Area and Museum of Mertola, Mertola

ar.name: أربعة مقاعد كهنية من موضع الخورس.
description:
مقاعدُ دير القديسة كلارا هي مقاعد من نوع ضخم. كانت الوحدات الأربع التي توجد في المتحف الأثري الوطني تشكل جزءاً من مجموعة تضمُّ في الأصل خمسين مقعداً؛ تتواجد حالياً الستة وأربعون مقعداً المتبقية في بعثة سان دييجو (الولايات المتحدة).  
بنية الخشب والزخرفُ المدهون بارزان؛ فقد جُمِّعت الأجزاء بطريقة جعلت العناصر المُسمَّرة قليلة العدد. كما أن سلسلة الألوان تقليدية؛ مع هيمنة لتدرجات الوردي، والأحمر الداكن، واللون الضارب إلى الخضرة، والأبيض، والأخضر الأصفر، المطلية على طَلية صلبة بيضاء تؤدي إلى نتيجة بصرية باهرة.  
إن المشهد المعماري للعمل، بأعمدته المثمنة وعقوده الصغيرة المفصصة وكنته ذات الحاملات والكورنيش، يمنح المجموعة طابعاً يوحي بالعظمة. فهو النموذج الأقدم في إسبانيا لمقاعد عالية: فقد جرى إنجازها حوالي 1353، التاريخ الذي أسَّست فيه ماريا دي باديلا، عشيقة الملك بيير الأول، الدير، كما تؤكد ذلك الشعارات ذات السباع المنتصبة على قدميها الخلفيتين، والمجرفات الصغيرة الخاصة بالنار، التي هي رمز ماريا دي باديلا.

تعطي هذه المقاعد الأربعة فكرة عن الضخامة الأصلية للمجموعة التي كانت تتكون، في البداية، من خمسين مقعدا، والتي كانت تتواجد بدير سانتا كلارا دي أستوديلو (بالانسيا). تتميز القطع المجمعة فقط بهيئة معمارية جدا؛ وتهيمن عليها زخرفة التوريق ذات الألوان اللامعة.
dynasty: فترة المدجنين، القرن الثاني عشر – الخامس عشر
keywords: أستوديلو؛ تعدد ألوان؛ خشب؛ مدجن؛ مقاعد؛ نقش.

en.name: Four choir stalls.
description:
Monumental choir stalls from the convent of Santa Clara. The four stalls held by the National Archaeological Museum are part of a set originally made up of 50, with the 46 remaining stalls now at the San Diego Mission in the United States.  
The wooden structure and the painted decoration are particularly noteworthy. The construction is made in such a way as to reduce the use of nailed elements to a minimum. The usual range of colours has been used, with a predominance of pinks, dark red, green-black, white and yellow-green applied on a strong base of white primer, producing a visually astounding result.  
The architectonic aspect of the work, with its octagonal columns, curved lobed arches and a roof with corbels and *tabicas* (small boards), give it a grandiose character. It is the oldest example of tall choir stalls in Spain having been made around 1353, the same year that María de Padilla, the lover of King Peter I of Castile, founded the monastery, as proclaimed by the shields with rampant lions and fire shovels, Maria de Padilla's emblem.

These four stalls give an idea of the original monumentality of the complete set of 50 stalls from the Convent of Santa Clara de Astudillo in Palencia. It has an architectural structure and its parts are simply assembled. The decoration is dominated by brightly coloured plant arabesques.
place: Convent of Santa Clara de Astudillo, Palencia, Spain.
keywords: Choir stalls; wood; carving; polichromy; Mudéjar; Astudillo; Peter I; religious furnishing

es.name: Cuatro asientos de sillería de coro
description:
La sillería del convento de Santa Clara es de tipo monumental. Las cuatro sillas del Museo Arqueológico Nacional formaron parte de un conjunto compuesto originalmente por cincuenta. Las 46 sillas restantes se hallan actualmente en la Misión de San Diego (Estados Unidos).  
  
Destacan la estructura de la carpintería y la decoración pintada. Está ensamblada de tal manera que se han reducido al mínimo los elementos clavados. La gama de colores es la habitual, con predominio de los tonos rosa, rojo oscuro, negro verdoso, blanco y verde amarillo, aplicados sobre una recia imprimación blanca, con deslumbrante resultado visual.  
  
El aspecto arquitectónico de la obra, con columnas ochavadas, arcos de lóbulos curvos y tejaroz con canes y tabicas, presta al conjunto un carácter grandioso. Es el ejemplo más antiguo en España de sillería alta: fue realizada en torno a 1353, fecha en que María de Padilla, amante del rey Pedro I de Castilla, fundó el monasterio, como lo pregonan los escudos con leones rampantes y badilas.

Estos cuatro asientos dan idea de la monumentalidad original de la sillería completa, formada por 50 asientos, del convento de Santa Clara de Astudillo (Palencia). De estructura arquitectónica, las piezas van simplemente ensambladas y predomina la decoración de ataurique en brillantes colores.
place: Convento de Santa Clara de Astudillo (Palencia).
keywords: sillería; madera; talla; policromía; mudéjar; Astudillo; Pedro I

fr.name: Quatre stalles de chœur.
description:
Les stalles du couvent de Santa Clara sont de type monumental. Les quatre unités qui se trouvent au Musée archéologique national faisaient partie d'un ensemble qui en comptait cinquante à l'origine. Les quarante-six stalles restantes se trouvent actuellement à la Mission de San Diego (États-Unis).  
La structure de l'ébénisterie et le décor peint sont remarquables. Les parties sont assemblées de telle sorte que les éléments cloués sont très peu nombreux. La gamme de couleurs est traditionnelle, avec prédominance des tons de rose, rouge sombre, verdâtre, blanc et vert jaune, appliqués sur une solide impression blanche, donnant un résultat visuel éblouissant.  
L'aspect architectonique de l'œuvre, avec ses colonnes octogonales, ses petits arcs lobulés, son auvent à modillons et corniche donne à l'ensemble un caractère grandiose. C'est l'exemple le plus ancien en Espagne de stalles hautes: elles furent réalisées autour de 1353, date à laquelle María de Padilla, maîtresse du roi Pierre Ier de Castille, fonda le monastère, comme le proclament les blasons à lions rampants et les petites pelles à feu qui sont l'emblème de María de Padilla.

Ces quatre stalles donnent une idée la monumentalité originelle de l'ensemble, initialement formé de cinquante stalles, du couvent de Santa Clara de Astudillo (Palencia). D'aspect très architectural, les pièces sont simplement assemblées ; la décoration *d'ataurique* à couleurs brillantes prédomine.
keywords: stalles ; bois ; sculpture ; polychromie ; mudéjar ; Astudillo ; Pierre Ier

en.name: Small Pattern Holbein Rug
description:
Early Ottoman carpets with endless geometric designs of the kind found on paintings by the German painter Hans Holbein Jr. (1497/8–1543) are called "Holbein" Rugs. The small pattern version of the Holbein Rug is more common. This rug is one of the Museum’s earliest 19th century acquisitions. The rug is one of those few small pattern Holbein Rugs which have survived almost completely intact.  
A special feature of the Holbein Rug is the red central field, used instead of the usual blue or green. The field contains star-centred Holbein guls on an ivory field strung along two axes in the longitudinal direction. The area between the guls is occupied by blue and green arabesque medallions forming crosses and arranged into an almost continuous lattice. A closed *kufic* band, ivory on a dark red ground, forms the main border with a narrow secondary border of "S" motifs on each side. en.name: Castle-Palace
description:
Commissioned by Rodrigo de Mendoza in 1509 and finished in 1512, the Castle became one of the most outstanding examples of Renaissance architecture in 16th-century Spain. Its construction went against the tendency of the time, imposed by the power of the king, who felt that he needed to destroy the existing fortresses to be able to consolidate his power over all of his subjects, including the ancient feudal nobility. In this sense, the attempt of don Rodrigo was an anachronism, explicable only by the political and strategic interests of the crown, which believed the old feudal and military caste was still needed.  
The exterior of the castle is forbidding and military and in complete contrast to the interior, which is refined and courtly, a reflection of the Italian humanist ideals. This spirit of the Renaissance is evident in the patio with galleries on two levels, where five arches rest on Corinthian columns at each level. The upper columns rest on pedestals and the galleries are closed with a marble balustrade. The monumental staircase that occupies the centre of the west side determines the proportions of the rest of the space; a model copied by most of the Renaissance buildings throughout Spain.  
In terms of decoration, the doors, windows and friezes are outstanding and develop a rich sculptural scheme. The Latin inscriptions, referring to the patron and his wife, alternate with sculptures inspired by classical mythology, obliging the viewer to interpret the building in humanist terms. The wooden ceilings, seen in various rooms, introduce us to a style of woodwork that will be much evident from here on in, in the itinerary.  
Many Spanish and Italian artists worked on this building. Among these, Michele Carlone stands out. He directed the work, first from Genoa and then from inside the palace itself. In Genoa, Carlone supervised the cutting and working of the Carrara marble that arrived by boat at the Port of Almeria. Once he had arrived in La Calahorra the Italian architect made sure that the design of the materials used, whether local or not, was related to the world of Classical Antiquity which the Renaissance was trying to recapture.

es.name: Castillo-palacio
description:
Encargado por Rodrigo de Mendoza en 1509 y concluido en 1512, el castillo se convirtió en uno de los ejemplos más destacados de la arquitectura renacentista del siglo XVI en España. Su construcción iba en contra de la tendencia impuesta en la época por el poder real, que necesitaba destruir las fortalezas existentes para consolidar su poder sobre todos los súbditos, incluida la vieja nobleza feudal. En este sentido, el intento de don Rodrigo era un anacronismo que solo los intereses políticos y estratégicos de la Corona, que todavía creía necesitar a la vieja casta feudal y militar, pueden explicar.  
El exterior del castillo, de carácter cerrado y militar, se contrapone al interior refinado y cortesano, reflejo de los ideales humanistas italianos. El espíritu renacentista se manifiesta en el patio con galerías desarrollado en dos alturas, con cinco arcos sobre columnas corintias en cada nivel. Las superiores descansan sobre pedestales, y las galerías se cierran con una balaustrada de mármol. La escalera monumental que ocupa el centro del lateral oeste condiciona por su amplitud el resto de los espacios, un modelo que siguió una gran parte de las construcciones renacentistas españolas.  
En el aspecto decorativo destacan las portadas, las ventanas y los frisos, en los que se desarrolla un rico programa escultórico. Las inscripciones latinas referentes al mecenas y su esposa alternan con esculturas inspiradas en la mitología grecorromana, y obligan a una lectura en clave humanística del edificio. Los techos de madera de las distintas habitaciones anuncian los trabajos lignarios que a partir de ahora iremos encontrando en nuestro recorrido.  
En el edificio intervinieron numerosos artistas españoles e italianos. Entre ellos destaca Michele Carlone, que dirigió los trabajos, primero desde Génova y después desde el propio palacio. En Génova, Carlone supervisó el corte y la talla de los mármoles de Carrara, que eran enviados por barco hasta el puerto de Almería. Una vez en La Calahorra, el arquitecto italiano se ocupó de que el diseño de los materiales utilizados, por locales que fueran, estuviera relacionado con el mundo de la Antigüedad clásica que el Renacimiento trataba de recuperar.

en.name: *Landscape from Gebze*
short_description: Osman Hamdi focused on dilemmas such as East and West, love and hate, life and death. While stylistically reminiscent of western Orientalist painters, his works reflect a more nuanced appreciation of Ottoman society and culture. In the art of his paintings, he depicted unique details so diligently that he made us recognize our environment and Turkish culture. He illustrated carpets, tile panels, calligraphies, decorative arts, shrines, mosques and human figures in his paintings. He also gave importance to details while reflecting the colourful scenes of Turkish culture, traditional architecture, Ottoman fashion and domestic and social life of the women in the Ottoman Empire. And it’s obvious that he is the first painter who used human figures in the western style.

en.name: Carpet
description:
This superbly preserved carpet is a type known as “animal carpet” variant. It probably dates to somewhere between the late 16th and the first half 17th century. So-called animal carpets comprise a well-known Persian carpet group dating to the 16th century with patterns of flowers/palmettes, cloud bands, and animals including mythical beasts on a background of spiraling tendrils/vines. The place of manufacturing of animal carpets and their variants are not clear, but Herat, Isfahan, and Kashan were given in literature as possible manufacturing centres. The most famous carpets in this group is the pair which once belonged to the Hapsburg Emperors The carpets are called “emperor carpets”; now one is in New York Metropolitan Museum of Art and the other is held by the Vienna Museum Fur Angewandte Kunst.  
  
Fashion for compositions filled with both real and imaginary animals appears to emerge, first in illuminations, in the second quarter of the 15th century in Shiraz and Herat simultaneously. By the early 16th century the style was embraced by the court artists in Tabriz and soon as almost epitomized the decorative arts of the time. Animals on these carpets are drawn in the style favoured at the court of Shah Tahmasp in the mid-16th century and possibly the works of these court artists were the original inspiration for the animal motifs seen on these carpets. With the accession of Shah Abbas I in 1587 a subtle change occurred in the style of decorative arts. Animal style gave way to more abstract designs.  
  
The style of spiraling tendrils and animals on carpets continued to develop, creating variant groups. This carpet fits well with a variant group that can be distinguished by the addition of a medallion, the increase and dominance of animal representation, the retreat of floral elements (palmette) and spiraling tendrils, and the total disappearance of the cloud bands.
holder: The George Washington University Museum and The Textile Museum
keywords: Silk; Safawid; Safavid; wool; floral motifs; imaginary animal
materials: Silk (warp and weft), wool (pile); knotted pile carpet; asymmetrical knot; open left
partner: The George Washington University Museum and The Textile Museum

ar.name: عقد.
description:
كان هذا العقد يشكل جزءاً من سلسلة عقود الرواق الجنوبي لقصر الجعفرية في سرقسطة. تتولَّدُ المجموعةُ انطلاقاً من عقد مكون من ثلاثة عشر فصاً، ترتكز عليه سلسلة من العقودِ الصغيرةِ المقعرةِ والمكونة بتقاطع عقود أخرى أكبر حجماً ومفصصة أيضاً. زُخرف الجزءُ العلوي بتزويق نباتي مُنمنم، مقطوعٍ بأربع قبب صغيرة؛ وجرت تعليةُ المجموعة بعقد كبير، يبدو أنه يستند على أعمدة مع أبدانها وتيجانها.  
تمكننا هذه القطعة من أن نلحظ مرة أخرى الطريقة التي عولجت بها بعض العناصر البنائية (عقود، أعمدة أو قبب صغيرة) على أنها مُجرد عناصر زخرفية؛ وهي ممارسة فنية شائعة في ممالك الطوائف. تخلق هذه التشبيكات الواقعية للعقود الصغيرة، المُحصَّل عليها من التكاثر المتناسق لكل أنواع العقود، جواً متميزاً من الظل والضوء؛ فهو فن يُعطي أهمية أكبر إلى التأثير النظري أكثر مما يعطيها إلى المواد وإلى العمارة نفسها.  
تتبع الأشكال الفنية لهذه الفترة الاتجاهات الخلافية لمسجد قرطبة الكبير، ولكنها تعكس في مملكة الطائفة في سرقسطة ذوقاً خاصاً بالنماذج الباروكية التي سوف تستعمل فيما بعد من طرف الفن الأندلسي والمدجن.

كان الجانب الجنوبي لصحن الجعفرية مزخرفا برواق شكلت به العقود، مثل هذا العقد، عمارة رائعة المنظر، زخرفية ودون وظيفة بنيوية حقيقية، مستمدة من سلسلة العقود المتقاطعة بمسجد قرطبة، لكن معقدة إلى أن وصلت إلى طراز "باروكي" لامثيل له.
dynasty: فترة ممالك الطوائف: دولة بني هود (432 – 503 / 1040 – 1110)
keywords: زخرفة زهرية؛ زخرفة معمارية؛ عمارة بلاطية / قصرية؛ عقد مفصص.

en.name: Arch.
description: This arch was part of the arcade of the southern portico of the Aljafería Palace in Saragossa. The whole consists of a 13-lobed arch supporting a series of small hollow arches formed by the crossing of other larger arches, which are also poly-lobed. The upper part is decorated with plant arabesques interrupted by four small scalloped cupolas. It is completed by a large arch that appears to be supported on columns, with their shafts and capitals. In this arch we can see how certain structural elements (arches, columns or small cupolas) are used as purely decorative elements, a common practice in the art of the Taifa kingdoms. The fretwork in these arcades, created by a series of arches that multiply harmoniously, produces an effect of light and shade. It is an art that places more importance on visual impact than on the materials or even the architecture. The artistic forms of this period follow the caliphal tendencies of the Great Mosque of Córdoba, but in the Taifa kingdom of Saragossa there is a special tendency towards more elaborate designs, which would later be adopted in various Andalusian and Mudéjar buildings.

The south side of the Aljafería courtyard was decorated with an arched portico similar to this one, built for effect and for decoration and with no real structural function. It was inspired by the intertwining arcades of the Great Mosque of Córdoba, but its complexity makes it singularly baroque in style.
dynasty: Taifa kingdoms; Banu Hud dynasty, Abu Yafar Ahmad al-Muqtadir (r. AH 437–73 / AD 1064–81)
keywords: Palatial architecture; floral decoration; lobed arch; architectural decoration; patronage

es.name: Arco
description:
Este arco formó parte de la arquería del pórtico meridional del palacio de la Aljafería de Zaragoza. El conjunto se genera a partir de un arco de trece lóbulos sobre el que se apoya una serie de arquillos huecos formados por el cruzamiento de otros arcos mayores también polilobulados. La parte superior está decorada con ataurique interrumpido por cuatro pequeñas cúpulas de gallones. El conjunto se remata con un gran arco que parece apoyarse sobre unas columnas, con sus fustes y capiteles.  
  
En esta pieza observamos, una vez más, cómo ciertos elementos constructivos (arcos, columnas o pequeñas cúpulas), son usados como elementos puramente decorativos, práctica habitual en el arte de los reinos de taifas. El trabajo de calado en estas arquerías, formadas por una serie de arcos que se multiplican armoniosamente, produce un efecto de luces y sombras. Es un arte que da más importancia al impacto visual que a los materiales o la propia arquitectura.  
  
Las formas artísticas de este periodo siguen las tendencias califales de la Gran Mezquita de Córdoba, pero en el reino taifa de Zaragoza denotan un gusto especial por modelos más barrocos, que posteriormente serían retomados en algunas construcciones del arte andalusí y mudéjar.

El lado sur del patio de la Aljafería se decoró con un pórtico de arcos como este que componían una arquitectura efectista, decorativista y sin verdadera función estructural, inspirada en las arquerías de arcos entrecruzados de la mezquita de Córdoba, pero complicada hasta alcanzar un barroquismo único.
dates: Abu Yafar Ahmad al-Muqtadir (437- 473 H. / 1046-1081 d. C.).
dynasty: Taifas: dinastía de los Banu Hud (432-503 H. / 1040-1110 d. C.)
keywords: arquitectura palatina; decoración floral; arco lobulado; decoración arquitectónica

fr.name: Arc.
description:
Cet arc faisait partie de l'arcature du portique sud du palais de la Aljafería de Saragosse. L'ensemble se génère à partir d'un arc de treize lobes sur lequel s'appuie une série de petits arcs creux formés par le croisement d'autres arcs plus grands, également polylobés. La partie supérieure est décorée par un *ataurique* interrompu par quatre coupolettes à tranches. L'ensemble est surmonté d'un grand arc qui semble s'appuyer sur des colonnes, avec ses fûts et chapiteaux.  
Cette pièce nous permet de remarquer, une fois de plus, la manière dont certains éléments constructifs (arcs, colonnes ou petites coupoles) sont traités comme éléments purement décoratifs, une pratique artistique courante dans les royaumes de Taïfas. Ces véritables dentelles d'arcatures, issues de la multiplication harmonieuse de toutes sortes d'arcs, produisent de remarquables jeux d'ombre et de lumière. C'est un art qui donne plus d'importance à l'effet visuel qu'aux matériaux et à l'architecture elle-même.  
Les formes artistiques de cette période suivent les tendances califales de la Grande Mosquée de Cordoue mais, dans le royaume taïfa de Saragosse, elles manifestent un goût particulier pour des modèles plus baroques qui, plus tard, seront repris par l'art andalou et mudéjar.

Le côté sud du patio de la Aljafería était décoré avec un portique dont les arcs comme celui-ci composaient une architecture spectaculaire, décorative et sans véritable fonction structurelle, inspirée de la série d'arcs entrecroisés de la mosquée de Cordoue, mais compliquée jusqu'à atteindre un “baroquisme” sans équivalent.
dates: Époque d'Abou Djafar Ahmad al-Mouqtadir (r. 437-473 H /1046-1081 J.-C.).
dynasty: Royaumes de Taïfas : dynastie des Banu Hud (432-503 de l’Hégire / 1040-1110 J.-C.)
keywords: architecture palatine ; décoration florale ; arc lobulé ; décoration architectonique

en.name: Sé Catedral de Santarém
names: Jesuit Church and College of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception;  Patriarchal Seminary
description:
The building is situated in Marquês da Bandeira Square. The typically Jesuit facade consists of four levels and five vertical sections separated by wide pilasters. The façade is broken up by windows and four niches that contain the Jesuit saints, St. Ignatius Loyola, St. Francis Xavier, St. Francis Borgia and St. Aloysius Gonzaga.  
The two towers commonly seen in Jesuit church architecture have been replaced by the patron saint of the church, Our Lady of Conception, flanked by large volutes and pinnacles. Several other ornamental features reflect the Flemish and Manueline styles, breaking away from the austerity of Jesuit architecture. Above the principal door is the Jesuit symbol “IHS”.  
The plain, single-nave interior has eight side chapels, five of which have gilt-carved wood retables (Our Lady of Assistance; Chapel of St. Francis Xavier (the Sacred Heart of Jesus Chapel); Chapel of Our Lady of Glory and Chapel of Our Lady of Conception), one is of marble (Chapel of Our Lady of Good Death), another in marbled wood (Chapel of St. Aloysius Gonzaga) and two in stucco imitating marble (St. Anne's Chapel and the Chapel of St. Francis de Borgia). The simple wooden roof of the nave is decorated with *trompe l'œil* paintings: a central *Immaculate Conception* flanked by four Jesuit saints, four female figures from the Old Testament (Jahel, Esther, Deborah and Judith) and the Four Continents (America, Africa, Europe and Asia). It is also worth mentioning the magnificent polychrome stone inlay in the main chapel, surmounted by a frescoed dome depicting the *Coronation of Our Lady*.

Built within the Jesuit College of Santarém, the Church of Our Lady of Conception, now the Cathedral of the Diocese of Santarém, presents an imposing façade rich in the symbolism of the Company of Jesus. Inside, it consists of a single nave and eight side chapels with richly decorated *trompe l'œil* ceiling paintings, carved and altars and, within the Chancel, polychrome stone inlay work that breaks away from the architectural austerity of previous Jesuit projects.
artist: D. Duarte da Costa and King João IV

Court architect: Mateus do Couto (“uncle”, active 1660); design of main altar: Carlos Baptista Garvo; stone carvers: António Pereira, Vicente Soares, Manuel Rodrigues; wood carvers: António Martins Calheiros, António Luís, Claude Laprade, José Pereira Lobo, Manuel Álvares, Matias Rodrigues de Carvalho; sculptor: João António Bellini of Padova; painters: António Machado Sapeiro, Luís Gonçalves de Sena [dates unknown]
history:
In 1609, D. Duarte da Costa, Armeiro Mor of the Kingdom (in charge of the weaponry) and a Jesuit priest, offered to finance the construction of a college for the Company of Jesus in Santarem. In 1647, King João IV gave the Company the estate of the ruined Royal Palace and appointed Mateus do Couto (“uncle”) as architect. The original project contract was signed by the Superior General, John Paul Olivia, in 1653, in Rome, and as with other Company projects, was obliged to follow specific rules. Construction of the church began in 1672 and approval for the facade was given in 1673. An inscription on the facade indicates that the work was probably finished by 1711. The Jesuits were expelled in 1759 and their assets were confiscated. In 1780, Queen Mary I offered the Santarém building to the Patriarchal Cardinal of Lisbon to accommodate the Patriarchal Seminary. Following the French invasions and the Civil War, the Seminary was closed in 1834. It was restored by Cardinal Guilherme Henriques de Carvalho in 1853.  
On 16 July 1975, the Papal Bull Apostolicae Sedis Consuetudine of Pope Paul VI created the Diocese of Santarém and the church became a cathedral.
keywords: Counter-Reformation, Jesuit Order, college, *trompe l'œil,* Santarém

pt.name: *Sé Catedral de Santarém*
names: Igreja e Colégio Jesuíta de Nossa Senhora da Conceição; Seminário Patriarcal.
description:
O edifício impõe-se monumentalmente na Praça do Marquês de Sá da Bandeira. A fachada tipicamente jesuíta desenvolve-se em quatro níveis e cinco corpos verticais, separados por largas pilastras, rasgados por janelas e quatro nichos com os santos jesuítas (Santo Inácio de Loyola, São Francisco Xavier, São Francisco de Borja e São Luís Gonzaga).  
No topo, a padroeira da igreja, Nossa Senhora da Conceição, ladeada por largas aletas e pináculos, em substituição das duas torres.  
Vários elementos ornamentais relembram um estilo flamengo e manuelino e quebram a comum austeridade imposta por Roma. Encima a porta principal o símbolo dos jesuítas.  
O interior, de nave única, de estilo chão, tem oito capelas laterais, à face, cinco das quais em talha dourada (Capela de Nossa Senhora do Socorro; Capela de São Francisco Xavier, actualmente do Sagrado Coração de Jesus; Capela de Nossa Senhora da Glória e Capela de Nossa Senhora da Conceição), uma em mármore (Capela de Nossa Senhora da Boa Morte), outra em madeira marmoreada (Capela de S. Luís Gonzaga) e duas em estuque imitando mármore (Capela de Santa Ana e Capela de S. Francisco de Borja). A nave ostenta um tecto plano em madeira, pintado em perspectiva, onde a Imaculada Conceição ocupa a zona central, ladeada por quatro santos jesuítas, quatro figuras femininas do Antigo Testamento (Jael, Ester, Débora e Judite) e os quatro continentes (América, África, Europa e Ásia). Destaca-se ainda o magnífico trabalho de embutidos policromos em pedra na capela-mor, encimada por abóbada pintada a fresco, com representação da Coroação de Nossa Senhora.

Integrada no conjunto arquitectónico do Colégio dos Jesuítas de Santarém, a Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Conceição, actualmente Sé da Diocese de Santarém, apresenta uma fachada principal imponente, rica em simbologia da Companhia de Jesus. O interior, organizado por uma nave única e oito capelas laterais, quebra a austeridade dos projectos jesuítas pela riqueza decorativa dos tectos pintados em perspectiva, dos altares em talha, em mármore e embutidos em pedra policroma da capela-mor.
artist: D. Duarte da Costa e rei D. João IV.

Arquitecto Régio: Mateus do Couto (tio, activo 1660); projecto do altar-mor: Carlos Baptista Garvo; canteiros: António Pereira, Vicente Soares e Manuel Rodrigues; entalhadores: António Martins Calheiros e António Luís, Claude Laprade; José Pereira Lobo; Manuel Álvares; Matias Rodrigues de Carvalho; escultor: João António Bellini de Pádua, pintores: António Machado Sapeiro, Luís Gonçalves de Sena. Datas desconhecidas.
history:
Em 1609, D. Duarte da Costa, armeiro-mor do Reino e padre jesuíta, ofereceu-se para financiar a construção de um colégio da Companhia de Jesus, em Santarém. Em 1647, D. João IV doou à Companhia o terreno do antigo Paço Real e nomeou o arquitecto Mateus do Couto (tio) para a obra. O superior geral, João Paulo Oliva, assinou em Roma, em 1653, o projecto inicial, que estava obrigado, como as restantes construções da Companhia, a regras específicas. Só em 1672 se iniciou a construção da Igreja, com aprovação da fachada em 1673. A conclusão da obra data, provavelmente, de 1711, tal como indica a inscrição da fachada.  
Após a expulsão dos Jesuítas, em 1759, os bens da Companhia foram confiscados. A rainha D. Maria I, em 1780, doou o edifício de Santarém ao cardeal patriarca de Lisboa, para que nele se instalasse o Seminário Patriarcal. O Seminário acabou por ser extinto, em 1834, após as invasões francesas e a Guerra Civil, tendo sido restaurado pelo Cardeal D. Guilherme Henriques de Carvalho, em 1853.  
A 16 de Julho de 1975, a Bula *Apostolicae Sedis Consuetudinem*, do Papa Paulo VI, criou a Diocese de Santarém, e escolheu esta igreja como Catedral.

en.name: Mellah
description:
The date of when the Jewish community settled in the *Fas Jdid*, in the quarter near the Royal Palace, is very often contested, but the Mellah as we know it today only had its boundaries defined in the 9th/15th century. The actual, physical boundaries in fact date from the time of the ‘Alawite Sultan Mulay Lyazid. The spatial constraints obliged the inhabitants, whose numbers were growing, to build upwards rather than outwards, usually constructing two floors, and to reduce the width of alleyways.  
Delineated today in the north and northwest by the ramparts of the Royal Palace, in the south by the Jewish cemetery, in the east by the commercial and residential quarters, and in the west by the old Jewish cemetery, the Mellah was, during the 9th/15th and 10th/16th centuries, much larger and was divided into two extensive neighbourhoods. The first, situated in the northern part of the Mellah on the surroundings of the Bulakhsissat, housed the rich Jewish merchants, most of whom had been expelled from Spain. Accustomed to a refined way of life from their days in the Iberian Peninsula, these Jewish immigrants from al-Andalus handed down, from generation to generation, the Andalusian legacy as is made apparent by their houses. Their dwellings were luxurious, decorated in *zellij*, like those belonging to the rich living in the *medina*. The second neighbourhood, in the southeast of the Grande Rue (the Main Street), and thus less airy, housed the *toshabim*s, the native Jews. It housed workshops, small shops and poorer housing.  
A dozen synagogues religiously framed the Mellah. The largest was situated in the northern sector of the neighbourhood, the only area that was provided with drinking water ever since the 9th/15th century, whilst other synagogues were spread across the neighbourhood.  
Whilst the Mellah offered the Jewish community the benefit of uniting their talents in the craftsmanship of gold and in the production of precious items, other activities, such as textile production, also featured. A local tradition in the working of silk had already existed in Fez since the Middle Ages, but was refined with the arrival of Sephardic Jews from al-Andalus. Two sorts of workshops were involved in the silk industry: those in charge of its production, and those in charge of the preparation of textiles for Jewish or Muslim religious ceremonies, or indeed of ceremonial dresses for the Royal Palace. The Mellah was also reputed for its shoe workshops. A guild incorporated numerous cobblers from the Mellah. The basic material was bought in the *medina*, but certain Jewish artisans prepared the hides themselves, which they then used or exported out of Fez.  
The Mellah of today still harbours a large amount of these commercial and craftmaking activities. Stalls are to be found not only in the main street, which itself was built after the fire which ravaged the Mellah in 1912, but exist in the little streets which surround this main one. It remains the centre for the production and commercialisation of objects fashioned in gold.

es.name: Mellah
description:
La fecha en la que la comunidad judía se instaló en *Fas-Ydid*, el barrio cercano al Palacio Real, es muy discutida; pero los límites del Mellah propiamente dicho no se definieron hasta el siglo IX/XV. Los actuales se remontan a la época del sultán alauí Mulay Lyazid. Esta constricción espacial obligó a sus habitantes, cada vez más numerosos, a edificar en altura —por lo general dos plantas— y a estrechar las calles.  
Actualmente el Mellah está delimitado al norte y noroeste por la muralla del Palacio Real, al sur por el cementerio judío, al este por los barrios comerciales y de viviendas, y al oeste por el viejo cementerio judío; pero en los siglos IX/XV y X/XVI era bastante más extenso y se dividía en dos grandes zonas. En la primera, la septentrional, bordeada por los vergeles de Bulajsisat, residían los mercaderes más ricos, en su mayoría expulsados de España. Apegados al refinamiento que habían disfrutado en la Península Ibérica, estos hombres se transmitirán de generación en generación el legado andalusí. Buena prueba de ello son sus residencias: lujosas, decoradas con *zelish*, como las más opulentas de la *medina*. En la segunda y más angosta, situada al sureste de la Calle Mayor, vivían los *tochabim*, los judíos autóctonos. Allí se concentraban los talleres, los pequeños comercios y las viviendas de los más pobres.  
El ámbito religioso del Mellah lo constituía una docena de sinagogas. La más grande estaba ubicada en la zona norte —la única con agua potable desde el siglo IX/XV—, y el resto disperso por las callejuelas del barrio.  
En el Mellah, la comunidad judía no solo tenía el monopolio de los oficios relacionados con el oro y los productos preciosos, sino que también desarrollaba otras actividades, como por ejemplo la textil. Ya desde la Edad Media existía en Fez una arraigada tradición local en el trabajo de la seda, pero la llegada de los sefardíes de al-Andalus le dio un impulso definitivo. Había dos tipos de talleres: los encargados de su producción y los que se ocupaban de la confección de tejidos para las ceremonias religiosas, tanto judías como musulmanas, e incluso de los trajes de gala del Palacio Real. Otro gremio importante en el Mellah era el de los zapateros, quienes solían comprar las materias primas en la *medina*, aunque algunos artesanos preparaban por sí mismos las pieles que utilizaban o que exportaban a otros lugares.  
En el Mellah actual se sigue desarrollando buena parte de estas actividades artesanales y comerciales. No solo hay comercios en la Calle Mayor, trazada tras el gran incendio que devastó el barrio en 1912, sino también en las callejuelas que la rodean. Permanece también el centro de producción y venta de objetos de oro.

fr.name: Mellah
description:
La date d’installation de la communauté juive à *Fas Jdid*, dans le quartier proche du Palais Royal, est très souvent contestée, mais le Mellah proprement dit n’a vu ses limites se définir qu’au IXe/XVe siècle. Celles actuelles datent, elles, du sultan alaouite Moulay Lyazid. Cette contrainte spatiale a obligé les habitants, de plus en plus nombreux, à construire en hauteur, en général sur deux étages, et à rétrécir la largeur des ruelles.  
Délimité, aujourd’hui, au nord et au nord-ouest par les remparts du Palais Royal, au sud par le cimetière juif, à l’est par les quartiers de commerce et d’habitation, et à l’ouest par le vieux cimetière juif, le Mellah, était, aux IXe/XVe et Xe/XVIe siècles, plus large et il se divisait en deux grands quartiers. Un premier, situé au nord du Mellah sur les bordures de vergers de *Boulakhsissat*, abritait les riches négociants juifs, pour la plupart expulsés d’Espagne. Attachés au mode de vie raffinée qui avait été le leur dans la Péninsule ibérique, ces juifs expulsés d’al-Andalus se transmirent, de génération en génération, le legs andalou comme l’attestaient leurs habitations. Leurs demeures étaient luxueuses, décorées de *zellige*, comme chez les riches de la médina. Le second quartier, au sud-est de la Grande Rue, moins aéré, abritait les *toshabim*s, les juifs autochtones. Il abritait les ateliers, les petits commerces et les habitations des plus pauvres.  
Une douzaine de synagogues encadraient religieusement le Mellah. La plus grande était située dans la section nord du quartier, seule zone à être alimentée en eau potable dès le IXe/XVe siècle, d’autres étaient parsemées à travers le quartier.  
Si le Mellah offrait à la communauté juive l’avantage de réunir les compétences dans les métiers de l’or et des produits précieux, d’autres activités y étaient représentées, comme le textile. Une tradition locale du travail de la soie existait déjà à Fès dès le Moyen Âge, mais elle a été affinée avec l’arrivée des juifs séfarades d’al-Andalus. Deux genres d’ateliers travaillaient la soie: ceux chargés de sa production, et ceux chargés de la confection de tissus pour les cérémonies religieuses juives ou musulmanes, ou encore des habits d’apparat pour le Palais Royal. Le Mellah était aussi réputé pour ses ateliers de chaussures. Une corporation réunissait les nombreux cordonniers du Mellah. La matière première était achetée en médina mais certains artisans juifs préparaient eux-mêmes les peaux qu’ils utilisaient ou qu’ils exportaient hors de Fès.  
Le Mellah renferme, encore aujourd’hui, une grande partie de ces activités artisanales et commerciales. Les commerces sont présents non seulement dans la Grande Rue, qui, elle, a été construite après l’incendie qui a ravagé le Mellah en 1912, mais aussi dans les ruelles qui entourent cette rue principale. Il reste le centre de production et de commercialisation des objets en or.

en.name: Church of San Pedro and San Pablo
description: Overlooking the River Darro is the Church of San Pedro and San Pablo. Building work began here in the second half of the 16th century and, designed by Juan de Maeda, shows clearly how the organisation of spaces in Mudéjar churches provides a concrete alternative to the classical solutions. Here, we find a nave with transept and side chapels opening off the main area. The result is a rectangular ground plan and an elevation that has different levels, with windows that ensure the illumination of the interior. The various wooden ceilings, created by the carpenter Juan de Vilchez, are outstanding. Among them is the *armadura* of the nave, a great rectangle of *limas moamares* with *almizate* decorated with four bunches of *muqarnas*, while the *armadura* over the transept has 16 sections and rests on four coffered squinches. The Sanctuary ceiling, as the one described previously, develops into a cupola decorated with knots of ten strands. In the side chapels of this church, the various tombs of the principal families of Granada in the 16th century enrich the artistic heritage of the whole. Similarly, the palaces of these same families, such as the Casa de Castril, enrich this lower area of the Albaicín.

es.name: Iglesia de San Pedro y San Pablo
description:
Asomada al Darro, la iglesia de San Pedro y San Pablo, comenzada en la segunda mitad del siglo XVI y trazada por Juan de Maeda, supone una alternativa importante en las formas espaciales de las iglesias mudéjares frente a las soluciones clásicas. En ella encontramos una nave de crucero y capillas laterales abiertas al espacio principal. El resultado en planta es un rectángulo, mientras que en el alzado tiene distintos niveles, con ventanas que aseguran la iluminación interior.  
El conjunto de cubiertas de madera fue realizado por el carpintero Juan de Vílchez. Entre ellas sobresalen la *armadura* de la nave principal, un gran rectángulo de *limas moamares*, decorada en el *almizate* con cuatro racimos de *mocárabe*; la del crucero, de dieciséis paños y apoyada sobre cuatro pechinas con casetones, y la cubierta de la capilla mayor, que, al igual que la anterior, tiende hacia la forma cupular, presentando lazo de diez en la decoración. En las capillas laterales de esta iglesia hay varios enterramientos de las principales familias granadinas del siglo XVI que enriquecen el patrimonio artístico del conjunto, del mismo modo que los palacios de dichas familias, como la anteriormente comentada Casa de Castril, enriquecen esta zona baja del Albaicín.

en.name: Bowl
description:
This ribbed bowl is made of coloured strip mosaic, employing short strips of coloured cane, a technique employed in Italian factories and notably in Rome itself. This masterpiece is possibly the only surviving complete example of the ouput of this city.  
  
The bowl came to the museum in 1868, as part of a large collection of 'Ancient glass' owned by the antique dealer John Webb. The bowl, and the rest of the collection, was first shown in the South Kensington Museum's 1862 'Special Exhibition of Works of Art of the Medieval, Renaissance, & More Recent Periods', which coincided with the large International Exhibition of the same year. The bowl stayed on loan to the museum until acquired six years later.
materials: Mosaic glass, fused and slumped, with applied foot. Clear marks of lathe turning around the outside of the rim and foot and on the interior of the bowl.
tags: Mosaic glass, fused and slumped, with applied foot. Clear marks of lathe turning around the outside of the rim and foot and on the interior of the bowl.

en.name: *Plato and Aristoteles*
description:
This representation is depicted in one of the seven lunettes of the main room. In this room the central theme is the *Ascension to the Mountain of Knowledge*. The allegories of several disciplines (Philosophy, Mathematics, Moral Philosophy, Theology, History and Law) are flanked by pairs of their significant representatives. The lunettes allude to the books held in the bookshelves below.  
In this lunette, illustrating Philosophy, Plato and Aristoteles are sitting on the sides of a central basis. They are supporting a monochrome standing female figure. She is holding in her right hand three circles of different diameter and in her left hand a round vessel with a burning a flame.
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: *Platone e Aristotele*
description:
La raffigurazione si trova in una delle sette lunette della sala centrale dove sono dipinte la salita al monte della virtù e le allegorie delle varie discipline (Filosofia, Matematica, Filosofia Morale, Teologia, Storia e Legge), attraverso la raffigurazione di una coppia di sapienti, e con la funzione di indicare le varie discipline cui afferivano i volumi posti nelle scaffalature sottostanti.  
Nella lunetta che rappresenta la Filosofia, Platone e Aristotele sono posti  ai lati di un piedestallo centrale, su cui poggia una figura femminile eretta, monocroma, che regge nella mano destra tre cerchi di diametro decrescente e, nella sinistra, una base circolare da cui emana una fiamma.

en.name: Holy Trinity Column
description:
An outdoor free-standing spiral column on a triple pedestal in the main square of Sopron, it represents Hungary's first outdoor-column spiral. The bottom level of the pedestal is curved with bevelled edges; its middle part is a curved-sided square with prisms at the edges; the top is decorated with offsets, serving as a pedestal for marginal figures.  
At the front on the second level of the pedestal, the double Löwenburg-Thököly coat of arms inscription in Hungarian reads: “This votive sculpture was erected by Count János Jakab Löwenburg and his wife in 1701, it was restored by the public of Sopron Free Royal City in 1797, 1847, 1883 and 1911”. Standing on the ledges of the mid-level pedestal-columns are ancillary figures of the Thököly-Löwenburg families' patron saints: St. James, St. Stephen King of Hungary and, at the corners, St. John of Nepomuk and St. Anthony of Padua. At each of the four corners are four figures of female saints (Barbara, Regina, Anne and Catherine – also the Thököly-Löwenburg families' patron saints; the *Immaculata* is at the bottom of the column. The patrons at the front are Count János Jakab Löwenburg half-kneeling and Countess Katalin Thököly kneeling on a pillow; both have their arms raised and look upwards towards the Holy Trinity at the top. Between them is an inscription in Latin with the *chronosticon* of the year 1701: *“VnI trInoqVe Deo patrI fILIo spIrItVI sanCto eX Voto posVIMVs sopronll.”* (“We the \[citizens\] of Sopron erected \[it\] in gratitude to the One God Holy Trinity, to the Father, to the Son to the Holy Spirit.”) There are further inscriptions on the other sides of the pedestal about the patrons.  
It is interesting that no other representation of Count Löwenburg remains from this era as far as we know.  
Above the mid-level pedestal there is a spiral column decorated with garlands and *putti* – its shape and garland decoration evoking the baldachin columns in St. Peter's Basilica, Rome – but, finally, the column is crowned with the Holy Trinity above the Corinthian column capital (the Father on the right and the Son on the left; above them the dove of the Holy Spirit among golden rays).

The Holy Trinity column in Sopron is one of Hungary’s most beautiful Baroque monuments with its pedestal decorated with figures of saints and patrons. Erected to commemorate the end of the plague epidemic, it was built between 1697 and 1701, out of a sentiment of plight and gratitude.
artist: Count Lipót Kollonich Archbishop of Esztergom Cardinal and Primate; Countess Katalin Thököly (1655–1701); Count János Jakab Löwenburg [János Jakab Lovorovszky until 1683] (?–1732); Ealdorman of Békés County: 1699–1732
history:
Baroque Holy Trinity columns are sculptures representing the Holy Trinity placed on free-standing columns in public spaces, and are usually erected out of a sentiment of plight and gratitude after great epidemics. The richly sculpted Holy Trinity sculpture in Sopron was erected following a plague epidemic that raged there at the end of the 17th century. In April 1695, after the epidemic had come to an end, Count Lipót Kollonich Archbishop of Esztergom Cardinal and Primate, suggested to the city assembly that a Holy Trinity sculpture be erected out of plight and gratitude that the town had survived, and requested donations from the citizens to realise it. The assembly of a Protestant majority responded positively to the suggestion, and works probably began that year, although there is no written evidence to confirm that assumption. The sculpture is mentioned in 1697 in the protocols of the town council when a carpenter complained about the sculptor, Szervác Leitner, who (as the context suggests) took part in carrying the sculpture into the town.  
Debate is still ongoing as to who was responsible for the design and sculpting of the monument. Since Kollonich himself presented the design, some researchers are of the opinion that Leitner was not sufficiently proficient as an artist to design and sculpt the monument, so Kollonich had the design and the sculpture made in Vienna or Kismarton (Eisenstadt), close to the Esterházy court. Guild legislation did not allow sculptors to act as stonemasons.  
Stylistic and iconographic examinations distinguish between different masters and sessions on the sculpture (the qualities of female saint figures are different; the representation of St. John of Nepomuk is very early). Based on inscriptions and local chronicles the column was erected in 1701. The site was already an important one in Sopron in the 18th century.  
The inscription on the sculpture mentions Countess Katalin Thököly (the sister of Imre Thököly) and her third husband, Count János Jakab Löwenburg as patrons, and a council protocol reveals that Löwenburg established a foundation for its maintenance as well. But when the sculpture needed repairing and people turned to the foundation for finance it was no longer in existence. The city, however, felt duty bound to renovate the monument and in 1796 and 1797, at the city's expense, the sculptor János Mynch restored it.  
The monument was renovated on several occasions subsequently.

en.name: Map of the Ottoman district (mutasariflik) of Jerusalem.
description: The Mutasarrifate of Jerusalem was a late-Ottoman administrative district governed directly from Istanbul; it was not part of the neighbouring vilayets of Beirut or Syria. Listed on the map are its four subordinate kazas: Yafa, Bir al-Sabea, Gaza, and Khalil al-Rahman. The red line crossing the map between Yafa on the Mediterranean coast and Jerusalem represents the Yafa–Jerusalem Railway. Initiated by the Jerusalemite Ottoman entrepreneur Yosef Navon, its concession was transferred to French investors and the line was operated by the Société du Chemin de Fer Ottoman de Jaffa à Jérusalem et Prolongements. The railway line opened in 1892; it was an approximately 87-km narrow-gauge line through the coastal plain, via Lydda and Ramla, before climbing through the hills toward Jerusalem.

en.name: Kilim, *paws*
description: The earliest preserved Pirot kilims date from the late 18th century. Early Pirot kilims were decorated with the so-called *endless pattern*, by repeating the same motif on the whole surface of the kilim. The motif of *paws* (*kostenice*) was used most often for the *endless pattern* creation. Early examples of kilims decorated with the *endless pattern* didn’t have a border. The border on the kilim indicates that it dates from the later period. The colours used are: red, blue, green, violet, yellow, orange and white.

en.name: Throne Room
description: The Throne Room, also known as the Great Room, is the largest of the palace's three state rooms. Construction began in 1768 when the marriage of Dom Pedro to the future Queen Maria I demanded a large area for official audiences. Designed by the architect, Jean-Baptiste Robillion, the new room was built in the Rococo style with carvings by the sculptor and wood carver, Silvestre de Faria Lobo. The paintings on the ceiling represent Faith, Sun, Hope, War, Justice and Charity and were executed under the direction of the painter, João de Freitas Leitão. Manuel da Costa, António Berardi and Manuel do Nascimento assisted him.

Pedro com a sobrinha, futura rainha D. Maria, justificou a criação de um grande espaço destinado às audiências oficiais. Projectada pelo arquitecto Jean-Baptiste Robillion, a nova sala foi concebida ao gosto rococó, sendo a obra de talha da autoria do grande escultor-entalhador Silvestre de Faria Lobo. As pinturas do tecto representam a Fé, o Sol, a Esperança, a Guerra, a Justiça e a Caridade, e foram executadas sob a orientação do pintor João de Freitas Leitão, tendo sido seus colaboradores Manuel da Costa, António Berardi e Manuel do Nascimento.

ar.name: علبة كحل
description: هذه المكحلة تتضمن كحلاً ومرود (وهو أداة تستخدم للاكتحال) والتي كانت تستخدم من قبل كل من النساء والرجال في العديد من البلدان لتكحيل العين.وقد كان استخدام الكحل منتشرا في مصر من العصر الفرعوني فصاعدا وهو مصنوع من حرق نبات الزعفران ومزجه مع النحاس الخام والرصاص. وقد كان الكحل يستخدم كتجميل للعينين وأيضا كعلاج طبي وعلبة الكحل هذه من منتصف القرن العشرين هي مثال رائع على استخدام نموذج الأرابيسك السائد المستخدم في التصميم الإسلامي. فالأرابيسك كعنصر زخرفي يتكون من جذع طويل، تتفرع منه أوراق منفصلة كفية الشكل، ومن جهة أخرى، وبصورة أكبر، تستخدم كلمة ""أرابيسك"" للإشارة إلى مجموعة كاملة، ومكررة من التصاميم المتماثلة، والمتشابهة في النسق، التي تستوحى من الأزهار، وأوراق النباتات، والحيوانات؛ لتضفي بعدا جماليا يتسق مع التنظيم المثالي لواقع الطبيعة.وتستخدم أنماط ""الأرابيسك"" بشكل واسع في الصناعات الحرفية العُمانية؛ حيث ترى في الصناعات الخشبية، والجصية، والمعدنية؛ وقد يستعان بها لتغطية الأسطح بشكل كامل، أو بأشكال محددة ضمن إطار هندسي دقيق.
dates: منتصف القرن الرابع عشر هجري / منتصف القرن العشريت ميلادي

en.name: Kohl Container
description: Cosmetic kits such as this one, comprised of a kohl container and kohl stick, were used by both women and men in many countries to apply eyeliner. The use of kohl was widespread in Egypt from the Pharaonic period onwards, made from burning the saffron plant and combining it with raw copper and lead. Kohl was used to beautify the eyes as well as to medically treat them.  This mid-20th century kohl container is a fine example of use of the predominant Arabesque pattern used in Islamic design.  The Arabesque as a specific decorative element consists of a continuous branching stem with split palmate leaves. The aesthetics of the Arabesque are derived from the imposition of order on the natural world. Arabesque patterns are used extensively in traditional Omani woodwork, plasterwork and metalwork as a means of covering entire surfaces or precise areas within a defined geometric framework.
dates: Mid 14th century AH / Mid 20th century AD
keywords: Kohl Container; Jewellery; Arabesque

en.name: *St. Francis Xavier and St. Ignatius of Loyola*
description:
Saint Ignatius of Loyola was the main founder and the first Superior General of the Society of Jesus, a religious order of the Catholic Church professing directly to the Pope a vow of obedience, as far as missionary duties were concerned. The early Jesuits were sent by Ignatius to pagan lands where they could work on the propagation and strengthening of the Catholic faith. Among them was St. Francis Xavier. He had studied at the same college as St. Ignatius in Paris and helped him plan the foundation of the Society of Jesus. St Francis was sent to Lisbon in 1540 principally because King D. João III wanted him to serve in India.  
In a short period of 10 years (1542–1552) he converted people from Goa, Ceylon, Malacca and Moluccas, where he established several missionary centres; he also established some others in central and southern Japan. He was buried in Goa where is body is still enshrined at the Basilica of Bom Jesus. He continues to be considered the greatest missionary since the Apostles.  
Christianity was expanded by St. Francis Xavier's work as a missionary and by his apostolic zeal. He became a model of holiness and an instrument of evangelisation against other confessional denominations.  
The floral and vegetal motifs that adorn these two sculptures have their origins in oriental art. Commissioned during Portuguese rule in Asia the sculptures are the result of the exchange of knowledge and ideas, techniques and materials from both cultures. The technical expertise reached by both Chinese and Japanese artists allowed their elite cosmopolitan styles to be linked together, and their patrons and the merchants who dealt with their work, to discover new art markets.

According to the austerity of Counter-Reformation rules, the Society of Jesus ordered a simplified interior design for the Church of São Roque, which included the Asian-influenced painted wooden sculptures *St. Ignatius of Loyola* and *St. Francis Xavier*.
holder: Lisbon's Holy House of Mercy / Museum of São Roque
Santa Casa de Misericórdia, Lisbon / Museum of São Roque
keywords: Society of Jesus; Jesuit mission; pilgrimage; miscegenation; Romano-Iberian wooden sculptures

pt.name: *São Francisco Xavier e Santo Inácio de Loyola*
description:
Santo Inácio de Loyola foi o principal fundador e o primeiro Superior Geral da Companhia de Jesus, uma ordem religiosa da Igreja Católica, com voto de obediência directa ao papa, em relação a missões importantes. Os primeiros jesuítas foram enviados por Santo Inácio a terras pagãs para trabalharem na propagação e no fortalecimento da fé católica. Entre eles, contava-se São Francisco Xavier. Este tinha estudado na Universidade de Paris com Inácio e outros companheiros, e ajudou a planear a fundação da Companhia de Jesus. Francisco Xavier foi enviado para Lisboa, em 1540, a convite do rei D. João III, mas com destino às missões na Índia.  
Num curto espaço de 10 anos (1542-1552), converteu gente de Goa, Ceilão, Malaca e Molucas, onde estabeleceu várias missões; posteriormente, fundou missões no Japão. Após a sua morte em Sanchoão, a 3 de Dezembro de 1552, foi o seu corpo levado para Goa, onde se encontra intacto na Basílica do Bom Jesus. É considerado o maior missionário de todos os tempos, desde os Apóstolos. Tornou-se um modelo de santidade e de zelo missionário, bem como um instrumento de evangelização e de diálogo missionário com outras culturas e religiões.  
Os motivos florais e vegetais que ornamentam estas duas esculturas têm a sua origem na arte oriental. Ambas são o resultado do intercâmbio de ideias, técnicas e materiais com as culturas orientais. O nível técnico e artístico a que chegaram os artistas chineses e japoneses permitiu que as suas elites estabelecessem ligações comerciais com mercadores e clientes ocidentais, tornando assim possível a abertura de novos mercados de arte oriental.

De acordo com a austeridade própria da Contra-Reforma, a Companhia de Jesus optou por um modelo simplificado para a construção interior da Igreja de São Roque. As duas esculturas representando Santo Inácio de Loyola e São Francisco Xavier, em madeira, decoradas à maneira oriental, faziam parte do seu acervo.
holder: Santa Casa da Misericórdia de Lisboa / Museu de São Roque
Santa Casa da Misericórdia de Lisboa/ Museu de São Roque.
keywords: Companhia de Jesus; missões jesuítas; peregrinação; miscigenação; escultura em madeira romano-ibérica.

en.name: *A landscape from Eyüp, Istanbul*
short_description: At the beginning of the 19th century, romantic painters who appreciated eastern mysticism brought newly discovered eastern landscapes with their paintings which contained fiery colours and interesting landscapes. One of those painters coming to Istanbul from Malta and affected by eastern mysticism was Amadeo Preziosi. He usually painted scenes from daily life, such as shops between streets, coffeehouses, baths, peddlers passing the street, a woman filling water from a fountain and figures from different ethnic groups. Like many of his contemporaries, Preziosi had been lured to the exotic city of Istanbul. He also tried to reflect the cultural diversity of the city in his paintings. Especially in his watercolour paintings he loved expressing the blue water of the Bosporus with its caïques, pavilions, palaces, boats, mansions, residences, bazaars and cemeteries.

en.name: Monumental Complex of Saint Nicholas
description:
Between 1995 and 1998, as the square hosting the monument complex, Piazza della Repubblica, was being renovated, ancient structures made in opus quadratum were found. Dating to the Roman Republican period, those structures are thought to be the podium of a big three-celled temple that faced the valley, probably a Capitolium or the Temple of Juno mentioned in classical sources. The church of the Assumption of Mary, partially demolished in the seventeenth century, was built on the temple’s walls in the early Christian age and altered in the Middle Ages. The remains of the seventeenth-century walls belonged to the Seminary of the Christian Doctrine Fathers. The parvise’s flooring is partially made of the basalt slabs from the 19th-century pavement of Piazza del Popolo in Rome.  
  
In front of the entrance of the town hall, the Fontana della Bella Flora (Bella Flora Fountain) can be seen. Built in 1886, its feminine figure has become the emblem of Ariccia. However, she does not represent, as tradition dictates, the nymph Aricia or the goddess Flora, since the statue comes from a tomb in the old cemetery of Ariccia.  
  
The Palazzo Municipale (Town Hall) was built in 1997–98 in post-modern forms according to the design of Francesco Petrucci. It stands on the site of the Seminary of the Christian Doctrine Fathers, founded in 1668.  
  
The Church of Saint Nicholas of Bari was built in 1665–66 on the site of the paleo-Christian Church of the Assumption, which was then moved to Piazza di Corte. Gian Lorenzo Bernini designed the Church and then entrusted the execution to his brother Luigi. Only the central nave of the old Church of the Assumption was preserved from the demolition and used as a basis for the centrally planned present church. It is covered with a vaulted ceiling and has two side chapels. The facade has a single order divided by pilasters with a simple tympanum without friezes. Since 2008 the Church of Saint Nicholas has hosted the Bernini Theatre.

it.name: Complesso di San Nicola
description:
La piazza, su cui prospetta la chiesa di San Nicola e il Palazzo Municipale, è stata ristrutturata nel 1995-1998, portando alla luce strutture in opera quadrata di età tardo-repubblicana relative al podio di un imponente tempio a tre celle con fronte verso la valle, probabilmente un *Capitolium* o il *Tempio di Giunone* citato da fonti classiche. Sopra tali murature era stata costruita in età paleocristiana e rimaneggiata nel Medioevo, la chiesa di Santa Maria Assunta, fatta demolire parzialmente nel '600. I resti di muri seicenteschi sono invece relativi al vecchio collegio dei Padri della Dottrina Cristiana. La pavimentazione del sagrato della chiesa riutilizza parte delle lastre in basalto della pavimentazione ottocentesca di Piazza del Popolo a Roma.  
   
Di fronte all'ingresso del municipio è collocata la *Fontana della Bella Flora*, realizzata nel 1886. La figura muliebre, assurta ad emblema di Ariccia, non rappresenta però, come si vorrebbe, la ninfa Aricia o la dea Flora, dato che la statua proviene da una tomba del vecchio cimitero di Ariccia.  
   
Il Palazzo Municipale costruito nel 1997-1998 in forme post-moderne su progetto di Francesco Petrucci, sorge sul sito del collegio dei Padri della Congregazione della Dottrina Cristiana fondato nel 1668.  
   
La Chiesa di San Nicola di Bari è sorta nel 1665-66 in luogo dell'antica chiesa di origini paleocristiane dell'Assunta, spostata nella fastosa sede della Piazza di Corte. L'esecuzione dei lavori fu affidata a Luigi Bernini, fratello del grande maestro. Nel progetto di Gian Lorenzo Bernini fu preservata dall'abbattimento la sola navata centrale della vecchia Chiesa dell'Assunta, dalla quale fu ricavata l'attuale chiesa a pianta centrale a sala, sormontata da volta a vela con due cappelle laterali. La facciata prospiciente la piazza si presenta a ordine unico spartito da paraste con semplice timpano senza fregi. Dal 2008 è sede del Teatro Bernini.
