en.name: Leather binding.
description:
Back-board. Italian format. The red-brown dye of the leather has turned black at the edges.  
The panel is covered with wicker-like strap-work tooled with fringe markings enclosing roundels. The central rope is twisted into three knots. The border consists of four linear frames. The second frame is decorated with a twisted rope motif and a fringe with roundels. The leather covers a panel of what appears to be poplar, on the back of which is glued a piece of parchment.  
The decoration applied to this binding follows the style in fashion at the time in Ifriqiya. Twisted rope, plaiting, curled interlacing and chequer-work are all in fact used in the *minbar* (preacher's chair) of the Great Mosque at Kairouan, which bears the stamp of Syrian Umayyad art, with its heritage of Byzantine themes, and which also evokes Abbasid art with its profound Sassanid influences. However, these arguments do not allow us to conclude that the Kairouan bookbinding was influenced by Syria. Several links in the chain are missing. Furthermore, the books bound at Kairouan seem to borrow their decoration from a repertoire that was familiar to the Christians and which the Copts used to extraordinary effect. In fact, it is likely that the binding is one of the acquisitions through which Christian Egypt contributed to the enrichment the Muslim world.

Brown binding from Kairouan separated from the Qur'an to which it belonged. It is decorated with twists, braids, interlacing loops and squares, also found on the pulpit of the Great Mosque of Kairouan, which was strongly influenced by Syrian Umayyad art.
dates: Hegira, end of the 3rd–beginning of 4th centuries / AD 9th–10th centuries.
keywords: Floral decoration
materials: Poplar-wood press-board covered with decorated leather.
tags: Poplar-wood press-board covered with decorated leather.

es.name: Encuadernación de cuero.
description:
Cubierta posterior de formato italiano. La tonalidad castaña con reflejos cobrizos del cuero está ennegrecida en los bordes. El ornamento consiste en un entrelazo en forma de mimbre decorado con un fleco, formado por una sucesión de rayas interrumpidas por un espacio medio, que adorna los galones y encierra unos círculos dentro de su malla. La parte central exhibe un trenzado de tres nudos. La orla incluye cuatro marcos; el segundo está formado por un trenzado adornado con un fleco, con círculos en su interior. Este cuero recubre una tabla que parece de álamo, en cuyo reverso se encuentra adherida una hoja de pergamino.  
La decoración de esta encuadernación se ajusta al estilo de moda en Ifriqiya. Trenzados, entrelazos con ondulaciones y cuadrículas se emplearon en la decoración del *minbar* de la Mezquita Mayor de Kairuán, que tiene la impronta del arte omeya de Siria, heredero de temas bizantinos, a la vez que evoca el arte abbasí, de influencia sasánida.  
Estas interpretaciones no permiten, sin embargo, deducir que la encuadernación kairuaní haya recibido influencia siria. Quedan aún varios cabos sueltos por dilucidar, ya que las encuadernaciones confeccionadas en Kairuán se asemejarían al repertorio usual entre los decoradores cristianos, desarrollado de manera muy notable por los coptos. En efecto, es indudable que la encuadernación fue una de las mayores contribuciones del Egipto cristiano al enriquecimiento del mundo musulmán.

Encuadernación kairuaní de tonalidad castaña, separada del volumen del Corán que protegía. La decoración está formada por trenzados, entrelazos con ondulaciones y cuadrículas, semejante a la ornamentación del *minbar* de la Mezquita Mayor de Kairuán, que muestra la impronta del arte omeya de Siria.
dates: Finales del siglo III-principios del IV de la Hégira / IX-X d. C.
keywords: Decoración floral
materials: Tabla de madera de álamo, cuero decorado.
tags: Tabla de madera de álamo, cuero decorado.

fr.name: Reliure en cuir.
description: Plat inférieur. Format à l'italienne. La teinte brun roux du cuir a noirci sur les bords. Le panneau est occupé par un entrelacs de vannerie dont une chenille formée par une succession de barres, interrompues par un espace médian, meuble les galons et enserre dans ses mailles des rouelles. La partie médiane présente une torsade constituée par trois nœuds. La bordure comprend quatre encadrements, le deuxième est orné d'une torsade meublée par une chenille qui enserre des rouelles. Ce cuir recouvre une planchette qui semble en peuplier et au verso de laquelle est collée une feuille de parchemin. Le décor appliqué à cette reliure est conforme au style alors en vogue en Ifriqiya. Torsades, tresses, entrelacs à boucles et quadrillages trouvent d'ailleurs leur emploi dans le minbar (chaire) de la Grande Mosquée de Kairouan qui porte la marque de l'art omeyyade de Syrie, héritier des thèmes byzantins, tout en évoquant l'art abbasside, imprégné d'influences sassanides. Toutefois, ces arguments ne permettent pas de conclure que la reliure kairouanaise a subi l'influence de celle de Syrie ; plusieurs anneaux de la chaîne nous échappent encore, d'autant que les reliures réalisées à Kairouan semblent emprunter leur parure au répertoire familier aux décorateurs chrétiens et dont les coptes avaient fait un remarquable usage. En fait, il est vraisemblable que la reliure soit une des acquisitions dont l'égypte chrétienne contribua à enrichir le monde musulman.

Reliure kairouanaise de teinte brune, séparée du volume de coran auquel elle appartenait. Torsades, tresses, entrelacs à boucles et quadrillages en composent le décor, qui se retrouve également sur le *minbar* (chaire) de la Grande Mosquée de Kairouan, fortement imprégnée par l'art omeyyade de Syrie.
dates: Fin IIIe-début IVe siècle de l’Hégire (fin IXe-début Xe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: Décoration florale
materials: Ais en bois de peuplier couvert de cuir décoré.
tags: Ais en bois de peuplier couvert de cuir décoré.
partner: Musée des arts islamiques de Kairouan

ar.name: فأس قتال
description: هذا الفأس مزين بأحرف عربية مطلية على كلا الوجهين . ويسمي النقش السلاطين العثمانيين حتى محمد الثالث ولكن فقط بشكل سريع وغير كامل. وإن مطرقة الفأس تحمل اسم السلطان محمد الثالث مما يعني أن السلاح صنع لعضو من حراس السلطان الشخصيين . والرصيعة المركزية تحتوي ثناء على الله . ونحن لا نعلم كيف دخل هذا الفأس للمجموعة الإمبراطورية.

de.name: Streitbeil
description: Das Beil ist beidseitig mit vergoldeten, arabischen Schriftzeichen geschmückt. In der Beschriftung werden in ungeordneter und unvollständiger Folge die Osmanischen Sultane bis Mohammed III. genannt. Auf dem Hammer des Beiles findet sich der Name Sultan Mohammeds III., für dessen Leibwache die Waffe wahrscheinlich gefertigt wurde. In den Medaillons in der Mitte des Beils wird der Name Allahs angerufen. Wie das Gardebeil in kaiserlichen Besitz gelangte, ist unbekannt.
keywords: Streitbeil; Osmanisches Reich; Mohammed III.

en.name: Battle axe
description: This axe is decorated with gilt Arabic letters on both sides. The inscription names the Ottoman Sultans until Muhammad III but only in a cursory and incomplete way. The hammer of the axe features the name of Sultan Muhammad III, suggesting that the weapon was made for a member of his Life Guards. The central medallion contains an appelation to Allah. We do not know how this axe entered the imperial collection.

description: The enchanting fresco on the ceiling of the Dining Room shows Odysseus’ arrival at the nymph Calypso’s island guarded in heaven by gods. It was painted primarily during the reign of Max III Joseph.

ar.name: بقايا الحجر الأصلي المحفور لياكوب إدوارد بولاك
description: مع ثورة عام 1848  وسقوط ميتيرنيش ، فقد دخلت النمسا في مرحلة جديدة مع الشرق. في عام 1851 قبل الطبيب اليهودي البوهيمي ياكوب إدوارد بولاك (1818- 1891) دعوة لزيارة بلاد فارس. وقد كان يدرس الجراحة في طهران وبقي بولاك لتسع سنوات وتعلم الفارسية وأصبح الطبيب الشخصي للشاه وقد درس البلد والشعب في رحلات طويلة وسريعا بعد عودته لفينا بدأ في نشر دراساته بشكل واسع وقد رغب في التواصل المعرفي بين وحول الثقافات.كما هو وارد في النقش على الضريح فقد اختار بولاك البيت من القرن الثالث عشر من الشعر الفارسي للسعدي وخلال عمره فإن بولاك لم ينس أي فارسي في فينا أن يعبر عن احترامه لحكيم باشي السابق ( الطبيب السابق) للشاه. ومؤخرا قام طبيب إيراني باستبدال الحجر المحفور في مقبرة فينا الوسطى بحجر جديد كرمز للتكريم وبقايا الحجر الأصلي وجدت طريقها للمتحف.

en.name: Remnants of Jakob Eduard Polak's original gravestone
description:
With the revolution of 1848 and the fall of Metternich, Austria entered a new phase of encounters with the Orient. In 1851, the Bohemian-Jewish doctor Jakob Eduard Polak (1818–1891) accepted an invitation to Persia. He was to instruct surgery in Tehran. Polak stayed for nine years, learned Persian, became the personal physician of the Shah, and studied the land and its people on long journeys. Soon after his return to Vienna, he began to publish extensively. He wished to communicate knowledge between and about both cultures.  
As an epitaph for his gravestone, Polak selected a verse by the 13th century Persian poet Saadi. During the lifetime of Polak, no Persian in Vienna neglected to pay his respects to the former Hakim Bashi (personal physician) of the Shah. Recently, an Iranian doctor replaced the original gravestone in the Vienna Central Cemetery with a new one, as a mark of honour. The remains of the original gravestone found their way to the museum.

en.name: Tray; Plate
description: In the entirety of the formation and establishment of Viennese glass culture, no name stands out like that of the company J. & L. Lobmeyr. Setting the standards of technique and execution in 19th century AD Austrian glasswork, the company also collaborated with many famous artists of the time, such as Oscar Strnad, Josef von Storck, Josef Hoffmann and Otto Pruscher. It is thanks to these collaborations that J. & L. Lobmeyr covered a wide range of styles, techniques, ornaments and decorations. A particular design that was popular until the turn of the century is oval colourless glass platters with Renaissance style rim decoration and figurative representations. Several artists were known to have done such designs, and in the example presented here we see the designs of August Eisenmenger and Josef von Storck. Depicting Triton and Nereid in a close embrace, the intaglio-cut figures fill the colourless glass surface, creating a clear composition and contrast.
artist: Eisenmenger, August (design); Storck, Josef von (design); Pietsch, Carl (manufacturer); J. & L. Lobmeyr (client / customer)
partner: MAK – Austrian Museum of Applied Arts / Contemporary Art

en.name: Oratorio della Santissima Trinità
description:
The Oratorio della Santissima Trinità has a square plan and a vaulted ceiling with lunettes. The interior is completely decorated. On the ceiling is depicted the Trinity. Figures of prophets are painted in the lunettes. The walls are decorated with biblical scenes framed by squares and separated by monochrome figures in a sort of frieze.  
The complex iconographic program is centred on the celebration of the Trinity and the Alliance between God and Man. All of the scenes depicted come from the Old Testament with the exception of the *Baptism of Christ*. Lionello Spada planned the general scheme of the cycle and painted it along with Francesco Brizio. Two of the scenes are attributed to Lucio Massari. It is very difficult to distinguish the different painters owing to their great technical and stylistic homogeneity. This testifies about their common will and technical preparation.  
The frescoes in this oratory are a good example of the renovation of painting created by the Carracci and developed by the Academy (Accademia dei desiderosi later the Accademia degli Incamminati), which was founded by the three Bolognese painters in 1582 in order to teach young artists. The perspective in the landscapes in the background of Francesco Brizio's paintings, where figures and landscape are equally important comes from the style of Ludovico Carracci. The painted illusionistic architecture of the ceiling shows Spada's apprenticeship as a Quadraturista (painter of illusionistic architectures).  
The imposing framing of the high altar and the wooden stalls of the choir, where the members of the brotherhood used to sit, carved and inlaid in oak, perfectly complete the decoration.

The Oratory of the Holy Trinity holds one of the most significant decorative cycles painted by the Bolognese school in the early 17th century. At the same time it is important evidence of the work of local brotherhoods assisting pilgrims. Its interior is completely decorated with beautiful frescoes painted by Lionello Spada, Lucio Massari and Francesco Brizio, pupils of the Carracci. The frescoes represent stories from the Old and New Testament. The wooden carved choir is among the finest works of Giacomo da Bergamo, called Venezian, a cabinet maker.
artist: Painted decoration: Lionello Spada, Francesco Brizio and Lucio Massari; wooden choir and altar: Giacomo da Bergamo, known as ‘Veneziano’
history:
The construction of the oratory linked to the the church and dedicated to the Holy Trinity and began in 1603. It was built by the Brotherhood of the Holy Trinity, whose task was to provide assistance for poor pilgrims and convalescent patients at the nearby hospital of St. Mary.  
Three well-known pupils of the Carraccis, Lionello Spada, Francesco Brizio and Lucio Massari began work on the painted decorations. The work began in 1605 and today these are considered one of the most significant fresco cycles of the early 17th century in Bologna. The beautiful carved wooden choir and the framing of the altar were commissioned in 1615 from Giacomo da Bergamo, known as 'Venezian'.  
The brotherhood of the Holy Trinity was suppressed in 1798, after the Napoleonic conquest, and all its properties passed to the Hospital of St. Mary.
keywords: Religious architecture; oratory; fresco; Carracci school; frieze; brotherhood
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Oratorio della Santissima Trinità
description:
L'Oratorio della Santissima Trinità è costituito da un ambiente a pianta rettangolare, con copertura a volta lunettata. L'interno è interamente decorato in ogni sua parte: sulla volta è rappresentata la Trinità, le lunette sono decorate con figure di profeti e sulle pareti sono dipinte scene bibliche in riquadri intervallati da figure a monocromo, che compongono un fregio.  
Il complesso programma iconografico scelto per l'oratorio è incentrato sull'esaltazione della Trinità e dell'alleanza tra Dio e l'uomo. La decorazione, che rappresenta episodi tratti dell'Antico Testamento (con l'eccezione del battesimo di Cristo), fu eseguita da Lionello Spada, al quale si deve la progettazione generale del ciclo pittorico, e da Francesco Brizio, che ha realizzato la maggior parte delle scene narrative, anche se due di esse sono state attribuite a Lucio Massari. La grande omogeneità di tecnica e stile rende comunque difficile identificare nello specifico le diverse mani e conferma l'unità di intenti e di modi di fare pittura dei tre artisti.  
Gli affreschi dell'oratorio sono un esempio del rinnovamento introdotto in pittura dai Carracci e divulgato attraverso l'Accademia dei Desiderosi, chiamata in seguito Accademia degli Incamminati, da loro fondata nel 1582, per formare nuovi artisti. Il gusto prospettico dei paesaggi che fanno da sfondo alle scene dipinte da Francesco Brizio, dove la natura ha un'importanza pari alla figura umana, risente in particolare dell'influenza di Ludovico Carracci, mentre l'architettura dipinta della volta rivela la formazione di Lionello Spada come quadraturista.  
Completano l'apparato decorativo l'imponente ancona dell'altare maggiore e i banchi del coro, dove prendevano posto i membri della Compagnia, realizzati in legno di noce intagliato e intarsiato.

L’Oratorio della Santissima Trinità custodisce uno dei più significativi cicli pittorici del primo Seicento bolognese ed è un'importante testimonianza del ruolo delle Confraternite laicali per l’assistenza ai pellegrini. L'interno è interamente ornato dalle magnifiche decorazioni murali dei pittori Lionello Spada, Lucio Massari e Francesco Brizio, allievi dei Carracci, che raffigurano storie dell'Antico e del Nuovo Testamento. Il coro ligneo intagliato è tra le più raffinate opere dell’ebanista Giacomo da Bergamo, detto il Venezian.
artist: Decorazione: Lionello Spada con Francesco Brizio e Lucio Massari; coro ligneo e ancona: Giacomo da Bergamo detto il Venezian
history:
L'oratorio, collegato alla chiesa dedicata alla Santissima Trinità, fu costruito a partire dal 1603 dalla Compagnia della Santissima Trinità, che aveva tra i suoi compiti l'assistenza ai pellegrini poveri e ai convalescenti dell'ospedale di Santa Maria.  
Nel 1605 ebbe inizio il cantiere di decorazione, che rappresenta uno dei più significativi cicli pittorici del primo Seicento bolognese, al quale parteciparono gli allievi dei Carracci Lionello Spada, Francesco Brizio e Lucio Massari. Il notevole coro ligneo e l'ancona dell'altare furono invece commissionate nel 1615 a Giacomo da Bergamo, detto il Venezian.  
La Compagnia della Santissima Trinità fu soppressa nel 1789, durante la dominazione napoleonica, e tutti i suoi beni furono aggregati a quelli dell'ospedale di Santa Maria.
keywords: Architettura religiosa; oratorio; affresco; scuola dei Carracci; fregio

ar.name: سجادة صلاة معاد تصنيعها
description: في سجادة الصلاة المغربية هذه المعاد تصنيعها تشير مشكاة الصلاة إلى اتجاه المصلي إلى مكة و مصباح المسجد يعطي إشارة مرجعية للنور في القرآن :  الله نور السماوات والأرض . مثل نوره كمشكاة فيها مصباح . ( سورة 24 ، الآية 35) ويوجد يدين بطراز خاص تشيرات لحركات الأيدي في الصلاة حيث اليدين المرفوعتين تبدأ بهما الصلاة تعظيما لله بقول "" الله أكبر"" واليد المفتوحة ترمز للأسس الخمسة للإسلام ( الشهادة ، الصلاة ، الزكاة ، الصوم والحج ) و بنفس الوقت اليد تعطي حماية من التأثيرات السلبية وتدل على السعادة والخصوبة.

en.name: Recycled prayer rug
description: On this recycled Moroccan prayer rug, a prayer niche indicates the direction of prayer towards Mecca. A mosque lamp makes reference to the verse of light in the Qur'an: "God is the light of heaven and of earth. His light [comes] as if from a niche, in which a lamp stands." (Sura 24, Verse 35). Two stylised hands indicate to those praying where their hands should come to rest. Uppermost is the invocation to God: "Allahu akbar" – "God is the greatest". The open hand symbolises the five fundamental obligations of Islam (confession of faith, prayer, charity, fasting, pilgrimage). At the same time, the hand provides protection against negative influences and evoke happiness and fertility.

ar.name: ركاب
description: هذا الزوج من الركابات مصنوعة من حديد محفور مزين بالزجاج وحجر اليشب والتمويه بالذهب. والأعقاب الطويلة والعريضة والمنحنية لهذه السروج الحديدية المطروقة كانت مناسبة بشكل خاص للأحذية بدون كعاب التي يرتديها العثمانيون وإن حوافها الحادة تعمل كمهاميز بديلة.

de.name: Steigbügel
description: Dieser Steigbügel besteht aus graviertem Eisen, das mit Glasfluss, Jade und Goldauflagen verziert ist. Die aus Eisen geschmiedete Steigbügel weist sehr lange, breite und geschwungene Trittstege auf, die besonders für die absatzlosen türkischen Stiefel geeignet waren. Die scharfen Ecken der Stege dienten auch als Sporenersatz.

en.name: Stirrup
description: This pair of stirrups is made of engraved iron decorated with glass, jade and gilding. The long, wide, curved treads of these forged iron stirrups were particularly suited to the heel-less boots worn by the Ottomans. Their sharp edges served as substitute spurs.

en.name: Nejma al-Zahra'
description: *“The construction of Nejma al-Zahra’ over a period of ten years (1912-1922) was not initiated on the back of a whim of a rich layabout but was a kind of a step on the way to recreating an Orient that had been dreamt of passionately”*, wrote Ali Louati. The Baron Rodolphe d’Erlanger, son of a wealthy family of French bankers of German origin, was 16 years old when he discovered Tunisia. He had come for reasons relating to his health, and left with the decision to swap the banking world for painting, for as long as the light and colours of the land exalted themselves as they did. At 26, he married Elizabeth, known as “Bettina”, who had come from a noble Roman family. Right from the start, she shared his love of Tunisia, which they visited regularly. In 1912, they began to create “*Nejma al-Zahra’*” (Resplendent Star). Nothing interrupts the harmony of the village whose mass descends from the *zawiya* down to the sea through marrying together with the slope of the hill. In respect to this “velum”, the baron built an esplanade leaning back against the hill, on which he erected his palace, facing the sea. From the outside, a porch entrance, which could be closed with a modestly studded door, subscribes to the spirit of introverted buildings. The slightly rigid composition of the main facade, featuring a projecting gallery as well as perfect symmetry, provides a contrast to the finesse and element of fantasy displayed by the interior spaces. This later residence provided the occasion to restore some honour to a body of professions that were having the life squeezed out of them by shareholders. It is the embodiment of all that is most noble and most refined within the arts of building and interior decoration of the times, whilst showing a preference for the Hispano-Moresque style. Acquired by the Tunisian State, today Nejma al-Zahra’ is the Centre for Arabic and Mediterranean Music. It has preserved its sumptuous furniture and its rich collection of manuscripts, paintings, rugs and other items, and offers the visitor an insight into the private family life of the Baron d’Erlanger. A museum of Tunisian musical instruments has also been opened here in homage to the baron, who was a great connoisseur of Arabic music.

es.name: Neshma el-Zahra
description: “La construcción de Neshma el-Zahra en 10 años (1912-1922) no fue un capricho de un rico ocioso, sino una especie de primer intento de recreación de un Oriente apasionadamente soñado”, escribía Alí Lousti. Cuando el barón Rodolfo d’Erlanger, hijo de una familia de ricos banqueros franceses de origen alemán, descubrió Túnez, contaba con solo 16 años. La luz y los colores del país le influyeron tanto que, aunque había venido para reponerse de una enfermedad, se fue con la decisión de cambiar el mundo de la banca por la pintura. A los 26 años, se casó con Elisabeth (Bettina), hija de una noble familia romana. Desde un principio, ella compartía con él su amor por Túnez, donde residían regularmente. En 1912, comenzaron la construcción de Neshma el-Zahra (en árabe, “estrella resplandeciente”). Nada debía perturbar la armonía del pueblo, cuyos volúmenes descienden desde la *zawiya* hasta el mar, aprovechando la pendiente de la colina. Para respetar esa pendiente, el barón arregló una explanada adosada a la colina, para edificar allí su palacio frente al mar. Desde el exterior se ve una entrada en porche, cerrada por una puerta sobriamente claveteada, tomando así el espíritu de los edificios que guardan celosamente su interior. La composición de la fachada principal, algo rígida, con una galería en antecuerpos y una perfecta simetría de aperturas, contrasta con la finura y fantasía de los espacios interiores. La construcción de esta vivienda, algo tardía, permitió que los oficios y la artesanía que habían recaído en la zona por falta de peticiones, volvieran a renacer por un tiempo. Este edificio refleja el arte de construir más noble y refinado de su época, con preferencia clara por el estilo hispano-morisco. Adquirido por el Estado tunecino, Neshma el-Zahra es actualmente el Centro de Música Árabe y Mediterránea. Conserva su lujoso mobiliario y sus ricas colecciones de manuscritos, tablas y tapices; se consigue que el visitante se vea transportado a la vida familiar del barón d’Erlanger. En este espacio se ha organizado un museo de instrumentos musicales tunecinos como homenaje al barón, que fue un gran conocedor de la música árabe.

fr.name: Nejma el-Zahra
description: “La construction d’el-Nejma El-Zahra sur une dizaine d’années (1912-1922) ne fut pas le caprice d’un riche oisif mais bien une espèce d’initiation sur la voie de la recréation d’un Orient passionnément rêvé”, écrit Ali Louati. Lorsque le baron Rodolphe d’Erlanger, fils d’une famille de riches banquiers français d’origine allemande, découvrit la Tunisie, il avait 16 ans. Il y était venu se refaire une santé et repartit avec la décision de troquer le monde des banques contre la peinture, tant la lumière et les couleurs du pays l’exaltèrent.A 26 ans, il épousa Elizabeth ou “Bettina” issue d’une noble famille romaine. D’emblée, elle partagea avec lui son amour pour la Tunisie où ils venaient séjourner régulièrement. En 1912, ils commençaient la réalisation de “Nejma el-Zahra” (l’Etoile Resplendissante). Rien ne perturbe l’harmonie du village dont les volumes descendent de la zaouïa vers la mer en épousant la pente de la colline. Pour respecter ce “velum”, le baron aménagea une esplanade s’adossant à la colline pour y implanter son palais, face à la mer. De l’extérieur, une entrée en porche, fermée par une porte, sobrement cloutée, s’inscrit dans l’esprit des bâtiments introvertis. La composition quelque peu rigide de la façade principale, avec une galerie en avant-corps et une parfaite symétrie des ouvertures, contraste avec la finesse et la fantaisie des espaces intérieurs. Cette demeure tardive a été l’occasion de remettre à l’honneur des corps de métiers qui avaient perdu leur souffle, faute de commanditaires. Elle est le reflet de tout ce qui existe de plus noble et de plus raffiné dans l’art de bâtir de l’époque, avec cependant une préférence pour le style hispano-mauresque.Acquis par l’Etat tunisien, Nejma el-Zahra est aujourd’hui le Centre des Musiques Arabes et Méditerranéennes. Il conserve son somptueux mobilier et ses riches collections de manuscrits, de tableaux, tapis et autres, et restitue au visiteur l’intimité de la vie familiale du baron d’Erlanger. Un musée d’instruments de musique tunisiens, est aménagé en hommage à ce grand connaisseur de la musique arabe que fut le baron.

en.name: *Expulsion from Eden*
description:
The painting was until recently ascribed to Giovanni Antoni Pellegrini (1675–1741) but further study of comparative material and references by Visnja Bralic, an art historian from Zagreb, has led to a new attribution of the Venetian painter, Girolamo Brusaferro. Although little biographical information exists about the painter, his work is well known, and this knowledge is supported by other extant pieces by him. Brusaferro, who painted altarpieces for churches in Venice, and historical and mythological scenes for private collections, was a member of the Venetian painters' guild (1702–1722).  
The Expulsion from Eden theme was a popular subject for painters during the Baroque period. Here, the artist expressively shows the drama of Adam and Eve driven out of Paradise for their disobedience to God by an angry angel. The busts of the three actors almost fill up the whole surface of the canvas. The angel stands accented with flaming sword in hand, and according to the iconographic principle, in front of the gates of paradise, thus stopping Adam and Eve returning to their haven. The angel, powerfully illuminated, stands with outspread wings brandishing his sword, while the naked bodies of Adam and the hardly visible Eve are in penumbra. Their faces and movements reveal their fear and despair. While Adam is running from the glare of the flaming sword, Eve raises her hands and face to the sky, begging for Divine forgiveness. The colours are warm with a light hue. The figures, emphatically voluminous and in motion, heighten the dynamic nature of the composition.

*Expulsion from Eden* is the work of the Venetian master, Girolamo Brusaferro, who painted numerous altarpieces for Venetian churches, along with other historical and mythological compositions. The Expulsion from Eden theme was a popular subject for painters during the Baroque period. The picture shows the moment when the angry angel, fiery sword in hand, drives Adam and Eve from their earthly paradise. The terrified and despairing exiles have committed the original sin, the shadow of which has fallen over the whole of mankind. While the powerful, naked Adam in painful spasm is bending over, Eve turns to heaven and begs for Divine assistance. The angel, with robust body and wide outstretched wings, brandishes the fiery sword at Adam. The impressive dynamic composition, marked, bright tonality and emphatic voluminousness of the figures distinguish this painting.
keywords: Italian Baroque painting; movement; religious object

en.name: Carpet
description:
The imagery and the Latin inscription suggest that this carpet might have been intended for use as a tomb cover or as a temporary coffin cover during a funerary service. On a delicate blue and white patterned ground reminiscent of fifteenth-century Renaissance silks, five medallions bear motifs associated with death and resurrection: skull and crossbones, and a phoenix rising from flames. The Latin inscriptions around the phoenix read: EX MEMET I(PS)O RENASCOR (from myself I shall regenerate) and VICTORIA DOCTIS (Victory to the learned). What today appears as a date of 1520 above the phoenix is the result of repair; "1520" probably was IPSO (by itself/myself).  
  
In Greek mythology, a phoenix is a long-lived bird that is cyclically regenerated or reborn. Associated with the sun, a phoenix dies by fire and obtains new life by arising from the ashes of its predecessor. The phoenix was subsequently adopted as a symbol in Early Christianity.  
  
A carpet with funerary iconography is rare. There are only two known examples, this carpet and another one in the Victoria and Albert Museum in London. Both of these carpets are more finely and tightly woven than the most Mudejar carpets. Although the design on this carpet is austere, its colours and delicate lace-like designs on the main field and borders achieve graciousness in one hand, and splendour and dignity on the other.
holder: The George Washington University Museum and The Textile Museum
keywords: Wool; phoenix; Spanish carpet
materials: Wool, goat hair; knotted pile carpet; single-warp knot
partner: The George Washington University Museum and The Textile Museum

en.name: Tile panel
short_description:
The architect of Membland Hall in Devon commissioned this sumptuous design for bathroom tiles from William Morris. Morris had the tiles painted in the studios of William de Morgan (1839-1917). They represent a rare collaboration between these two creative geniuses.  
Edward Charles Baring, 1st Baron Revelstoke, was the builder of Membland Hall. He was a merchant banker. The hall was later demolished.

ar.name: كفة ميزان.
description: كفة ميزان مستديرة قليلة العمق تنتمي إلى مجموعة من الموازين، وهي مزينة من الداخل بست زهيرات ذات ست بتلات مرتبة تحت الحافة مباشرة بشكل منتظم على مسافات متساوية، وتحتها شريط يتضمن ثلاث حليات مستدقة الأطراف داخلها شعار مركب يتضمن رمز المنديل وعلبة القلم والكأس على أرضية ذات زخارف ملتفة مجردة. تتناوب الحليات مع ثلاثة إطارات متطاولة تتضمن نقوش بالخط الثلث، وهي مرتبة على أرضية ذات زخارف ملتفة مجردة مع سعف النخل وعناصر مورقة ضمنها، وتعطي النقوش ألقاب التشريفات لحاكم مجهول. تتصل الحليات الدائرية والإطارات فيما بينها بحليات دائرية ذات حدود بسيطة، مملوءة بزهيرات ذات ست بتلات. وثمة إطارات على شكل سعف النخل مستدقة الأطراف تزينها حليات الشعارات من الأعلى والأسفل، وبين هذه الأخيرة تظهر زهيرات ذات ست تويجات متوضعة على مسافات متساوية. تم تزيين مركز الكفة بنموذج زهري متشابك في منتصفه نجمة بستة رؤوس تم خلقها من أشكال مقلوبة ثلاثية الفصوص، وقد تم ملء الفراغات المتبقية ضمن الشكل المتشابك بأشكال أحادية ثلاثية الفصوص وزخارف ملتفة.

من شأن أسلوب كفّة الميزان هذه، وتصميمها، ووجود شعار مُركَّب، أن يضعها في سياق مملوكي مُتأخِّر. ربما صُنعتْ في دمشق أو القاهرة. من المُؤكِّد أن كفّات الموازين كانت حاجات أساسية في أسواق المدن المملوكية، في طول البلاد وعرضها.
holder: المتحف الملكي، المتحف الوطني في اسكتلندا NMS.
keywords: خط ثلث؛ شعار.

en.name: Weighing scales pan.
description: A shallow circular pan belonging to a set of weighing scales, decorated on the inside only with six six-petalled rosettes arranged below the rim at regular intervals. Below this is a band containing three cusped roundels with composite blazons that incorporate the motifs of napkin, pen case and cup set against a stylised scrolling background. The roundels alternate with three elongated cartouches containing inscriptions in *thuluth* script. These are arranged on a stylised scrolling background with split-palmette and leafy elements incorporated into it. The inscriptions give the honorific titles of an anonymous ruler. The roundels and cartouches are interconnected by roundels with plain borders, filled with six-petalled rosettes. Pointed and cusped split-palmette cartouches further highlight the blazon roundels above and below. In between the latter, six six-petalled rosettes appear placed at regular intervals. The centre of the pan is decorated with an interlaced rosette motif with a central, six-pointed star created from inverted trefoils. The remaining spaces within the interlacing are filled with individual trefoils and scrolling.

The style of this scales pan, its layout and the presence of a composite blazon place this object within a late Mamluk context. It may have been made in Damascus or Cairo. Scales pans would have been essential tools in the markets of Mamluk cities throughout the empire.
keywords: Blazon; thuluth; measuring instrument; calligraphy; inscription; floral decoration

es.name: Platillo de balanza
description: Platillo perteneciente a una balanza. En su cara interna está decorado, junto al borde con seis rosetas de seis pétalos dispuestas a intervalos regulares; por debajo de ellas corre una banda Debajo se aprecia una banda con tres medallones que encierran blasones compuestos en los que se identifican una servilleta, un plumier y una copa sobre un fondo de estilizados roleos. Estos medallones alternan con tres cartuchos alargados con inscripciones en caligrafía *zuluz*, igualmente sobre fondo de roleos estilizados, a los que se añaden medias palmetas y hojas. Las inscripciones recogen los títulos honoríficos de un gobernante que no se menciona. Los medallones y cartuchos están conectados por una cinta que traza círculos entre ellos; en el interior de estos círculos se ven rosetas de seis pétalos. Rematan esta banda, arriba y abajo, cartuchos puntiagudos con composiciones de medias palmetas en su interior. Otra línea de seis rosetas de seis pétalos adorna la última banda hasta el centro del platillo, decorado con un lazo que dibuja una estrella de seis puntas rellenada con tréboles invertidos y roleos.

El estilo, la composición y el blasón compuesto de este platillo de balanza indican que es un objeto de finales del periodo mameluco, fabricado probablemente en Damasco o El Cairo. La balanza era un instrumento esencial en los mercados urbanos de todo el imperio mameluco.
dates: Siglo IX de la Hégira / XV d. C.
keywords: blasón; escritura zuluz

fr.name: Plateau de balance.
description: Plateau circulaire concave ayant appartenu à une balance, au bord intérieur simplement décoré de six rosettes à six pétales disposées à intervalles réguliers. Au-dessous, un bandeau comprend trois rondeaux pointés à blasons composites à motif de serviette, de porte-plume et de coupe sur un fond d'enroulements stylisés. Les rondeaux alternent avec trois cartouches allongés contenant des inscriptions en écriture *thoulouth*, se développant sur un fond d'enroulements stylisés à demi-palmettes et éléments foliés. Les inscriptions donnent les titres honorifiques d'un souverain non nommé. Les rondeaux et les cartouches sont reliés par des rosettes à bordure évidée, dont la partie centrale est occupée par une rosace à six pétales. Au-dessus et au-dessous des rondeaux blasonnés sont disposés, pour les mettre en valeur, des cartouches à demi-palmettes pointés et en coupole. Entre eux, six rosettes à six pétales sont réparties à intervalles réguliers. Le centre du plateau est décoré d'une rosace centrale à entrelacs en étoile à six branches générée par une inversion de fleurons. Les espaces entre les entrelacs sont interrompus par des fleurons et des rinceaux.

Le style de ce plateau de balance, son  dessin et la présence d’un blason composite rattachent cet objet à un contexte mamelouk tardif. Il a sans doute été fabriqué à Damas ou au Caire. Les plateaux de balance furent certainement des outils essentiels sur les marchés des villes mameloukes à travers tout  l’empire.
dates: IXe siècle de l’Hégire (XVe siècle J.-C.).
keywords: blason ; écriture thoulouth

ar.name: زبدية من نيسابور
description: الزبدية لها جسم ثقيل وقاعدة مقعرة بشكل طفيف ومركزها مملوء بنموذج شبكي عليه عصابة منحنية مضفرة تشكل ست دوائر.وهي متصلة بدائرة مركزية المزينة بنقش بخط شبيه بالكوفي والدوائر النباتية مملوءة بشكل متناوب بنفس النقش بالخط شبيه الكوفي ونموذج شبكي ذو نقاط خضراء وصفراء. والجدران الخارجية للزبدية مزينة بخطوط سوداء.والتزيين المصور على هذه الزبدية يرتبط بمجموعة كاملة وجدت في نيسابور حيث ترتيبات من زخارف نباتية بشكل دوائر مرسومة باللون الأسود والأصفر والأخضر تكون الشكل الشائع فيها . واستنادا إلى الحفريات الواسعة التي أجريت من قبل متحف المتروبوليتان للفن في نيويورك في شرق بلاد فارس فقد كانت نيسابور مركزا للفخار متعدد الألوان جيد التصميم المصنوع خلال العصر الإسلامي ولكن يبدو أن الأوعية من هذا النوع ذات النقش الشبيه بالكوفي هي نادرة.

en.name: Bowl from Nishapur
description:
The bowl has a heavy body and a slightly concave base, its centre filled with a grid pattern on which a curved interlacing band forms six circles. They are attached to a central circle that is decorated with a pseudo-*kufic* inscription. The vegetal circles are alternately filled with the same pseudo-*kufic* inscription and a grid pattern with green and yellow dots. The outside walls of the bowl are decorated with black lines.  
The decoration depicted on this bowl relates to a corpus of pottery found in Nishapur where arrangements of the circle-shaped vegetal ornament in black, yellow and green colour are a common motive. Based on the extensive excavations conducted by the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York in Eastern Persia, Nishapur has been a centre of well-designed polychrome pottery made during the Islamic period. However, vessels with this kind of pseudo-*kufic* inscription seem to be rare.
keywords: Nishapur; ceramics
materials: Earthenware; underglaze painted in slip and pigment; buff ware

en.name: Map of the United Principalities of Moldova and Valahia
Bath scraper or pumice stone
description:
This object has been associated with a series of bath scrapers and pumice stones attributed to AH 5th-6th / 11th-12th century Middle East. They are characterised by an animal shape or motif made from a coarse material.  
  
This model represents a rodent or a hedgehog recognisable by its long ears and the spines on its back. The bottom of the piece is incised with a grid that would have accentuated its abrasive quality. Deliberately left unglazed and unrefined, such scrapers were used during hamam rituals to exfoliate and purify the skin.  
  
This bath scraper could be considered an early version of the traditional exfoliating washcloth (ar. *kessa* , tr. *kese*), an emblematic item from the hamam. It is also plausible that they coexisted, given that the *kessa* was made from natural perishable material that would have disappeared in places where ceramic has survived.
keywords: Water; pumice stone; bath scraper; Iran; ceramic; ablution
materials: Unglazed ceramic with molded and incised overlay decoration

ar.name: شاهدة بأربع لغات.
description:
شاهدة سداسية الشكل، مقسمة إلى خمسة أقسام؛ نقشت عليها عبارة بأربع لغات، يحتوي القسم المركزي منها على الحروف الأولى لعبارة لاتينية، هي: (ي ك-خ ك-ن ي-ك)" المسيح سينتصر، وصليب منفذ بطريقة التطعيم المعروفة بالشواهد متعددة الألوان، وكتب فوق الصليب باللغة العبرية وعلى الطرف السفلي منه باللغة العربية وعلى اليسار باللغة اللاتينية وعلى اليمين باللغة اليونانية عبارة تتعلق بوفاة آنّا والدة غريسانتو كاهن الحاكم النورمندي روجييرو التي توفيت في سنة543/ 1148 ودفنت في الجامع الكبير (الذي أصبح فيما بعد كاتدرائية باليرمو). ومن هناك نقل ابنها رفاتها إلى كنيسة القديس ميخائيل أركانجلو إلى المعبد الصغير داخل الكنيسة الذي بني بأمره في سنة543/ 1148 لاتيني: 4904 عبري، 6658 يوناني، 543 عربي، وسمى باسم أمه القديسة آنّا.  
يوجد لوحة تذكارية أخرى (هي شاهدة) في متحف تزيزا (عزيزة) كتبت عباراتها باللغات المذكورة آنفاً ( ماعدا العبرية) تذكر بوفاة دروغو أب الكاهن غريسانتو الذي دفن أيضاً في المعبد الصغير المدعو معبد القديسة آنّا في سنة547/ 1153، وذكرت تواريخ أخرى في كنيسة القديس ميخائيل أركانجلو القريبة من دير اليسوعيين، صارت اليوم مخزناً للمكتبة العامة التابعة للبلدية.

تخلد هذه اللوحة التي تحمل نقيشة كتابية بأربع لغات وفاة آنا، والدة جريسانتو، قسيس العاهل النورمندي، روجي (روجار). وتوافق التواريخ الموجودة في الروايات الأربع، والتي كتبت كل واحدة منها وفق تقويمها الخاص، التاريخ اللاتيني لعام 1148.
keywords: كتابة عبرية؛ كتابة يونانية؛ فن عمارة صقلية نورمندية؛ نقش بأربع لغات؛ شاهدة قبر؛ نقش

en.name: Inscription in four languages.
description: Hexagonal marble tombstone in four languages divided into five panels, of which the centre one bears, inscribed within a circle, a Greek cross in polychrome stone inlay with the initials IC XC NI KA, ‘Jesus Christ conquers’. Above the cross there is an inscription in Hebrew, on the lower side an Arabic inscription, on the left a Latin inscription and to the right an inscription in Greek. The inscriptions refer to the death of Anna, mother of Grisanto, a priest of the Norman sovereign Ruggero (Roger), who died in 1148 and was buried in the great *jami* (subsequently Palermo Cathedral) and from there taken by her son to the Church of San Michele Arcangelo and the chapel known as Sant’Anna, built by Grisanto in 1149. The dates in the four versions, each calculated according to the respective calendar, are 1148 Latin, 4904 Hebrew, 6658 Greek and 543 Arabic. There is another tombstone at the Zisa Museum in just three languages (excluding Hebrew) commemorating the death of Drogo, father of the priest Grisanto, also buried in the Chapel of Sant’Anna in 1153. The inscription comes from the Church of San Michele Arcangelo near to the Casa Professa dei Gesuiti, which had many inscriptions, including Latin ones, and is now stored in the municipal library.

This tombstone, in Arabic, Hebrew, Greek and Latin, commemorates the death of Anna, mother of Grisanto, priest to the Norman King Ruggero (Roger). Each of the dates in the four versions, calculated using the appropriate calendar, corresponds to the Latin year 1148.
place: Church of San Michele Arcangelo (de Indulciis), Palermo.
keywords: Siculo-Norman; funerary inscription; Hebrew inscription; Greek inscription; calligraphy; funerary inscription; funerary stele; gravestone
materials: Marble with decorative mosaic tessera of marble and semi-precious stones.
tags: Marble with decorative mosaic tessera of marble and semi-precious stones.

es.name: Inscripción cuatrilingüe.
description: Lápida de mármol cuatrilingüe hexagonal, dividida en cinco recuadros. El recuadro central presenta una cruz griega encerrada en un círculo, realizada con incrustaciones de piedra policromada y las iniciales IC XC NI KA, “Jesucristo vence”. Encima de la cruz aparece la inscripción en hebreo; debajo, en árabe; a la izquierda, la inscripción latina; y a la derecha, la griega. Las inscripciones se refieren al fallecimiento de Anna, madre de Grisanto, sacerdote del rey normando Ruggero. La muerte le sobrevino en el año 1148 y fue sepultada en la mezquita aljama, que se convertiría después en la catedral de Palermo, para luego ser trasladada por su hijo a la iglesia de San Miguel Arcángel, a la capilla de Santa Ana, que Grisanto ordenó construir en 1149. Las fechas de las cuatro versiones se corresponden con el año latino 1148, cada una según su calendario (4904 en hebreo, 6658 en griego y 543 en árabe). En el Museo de la Zisa se conserva otra lápida multilingüe, aunque en ella no está el hebreo, que conmemora la muerte de Drogo, padre del cura Grisanto, también sepultado en la capilla de Santa Ana en 1153. La inscripción proviene de la iglesia de San Miguel Arcángel, próxima a la casa profesa de los jesuitas, donde se conservaban muchas inscripciones, algunas en latín, y que hoy se ha convertido en almacén de la biblioteca municipal.

La lápida, en cuatro lenguas, conmemora la muerte de Anna, madre de Grisanto, sacerdote el soberano normando Ruggero. Las fechas presentes en las cuatro versiones, cada una correspondiente a su propio calendario, coinciden con la fecha latina de 1148.
place: Palermo, iglesia de San Miguel Arcángel (de Indulciis).
keywords: arquitectura sículo-normanda; inscripción funeraria; inscripción hebrea; inscripción griega; estela funeraria;  lápida funeraria
materials: Mármol decorado con teselas de mosaico de mármol y piedras duras.

fr.name: Inscription en quatre langues.
description: Plaque de marbre en quatre langues, hexagonale, divisée en cinq panneaux ; le panneau central porte, inscrite à l'intérieur d'un cercle, une croix grecque réalisée avec des incrustations de pierre polychrome, et les initiales IC XC NI KA, “Jésus Christ vainqueur”. Au-dessus de la croix se trouve l'inscription en hébreu, sur le côté inférieur celle en arabe, à gauche l'inscription latine, à droite la grecque. Les inscriptions font référence à la mort d'Anna, la mère de Grisanto, prêtre du roi normand Roger, morte en 1148 et ensevelie dans la plus Grande Mosquée(plus tard cathédrale de Palerme), puis transférée sur ordre de son fils dans l'église San Michele Arcangelo, dans la “chapelle Sainte-Anne” construite à l'initiative de Grisanto en 1149. Les dates présentes dans les quatre versions sont, chacune selon le calcul du calendrier respectif correspondant au 1148 latin : 4904 hébreu, 6658 grec, 543 arabe. Le musée de la Zisa conserve une autre plaque, mais en trois langues (l'hébreu n'est pas présent), commémorant la mort de Drogo, père du prêtre Grisanto, lui aussi enseveli dans la chapelle Sainte-Anne en 1153. L'inscription provient de l'église San Michele Arcangelo, non loin de la *casa professa* des Jésuites qui conservait de nombreuses inscriptions, y compris latines ; c'est aujourd'hui le dépôt de la Bibliothèque communale.

Cette plaque, portant une inscription en quatre langues, commémore la mort d'Anna, mère de Grisanto, prêtre du souverain normand Roger. Les dates présentes dans les quatre versions, chacune avec le calcul de son propre calendrier, correspondent toutes à la date latine de 1148.
place: Palerme, église San Michele Arcangelo (de Indulciis).
keywords: architecture arabo-normande ; inscription funéraire ; inscription hébraïque ; inscription grecque; stèle funéraire ; pierre tombale

it.name: Iscrizione quadrilingue.
description: lapide marmorea quadrilingue, esagonale, ripartita in cinque riquadri, di cui quello centrale reca, inscritta entro un cerchio, una croce greca realizzata con intarsi lapidei policromi, e le iniziali IC XC NI KA, "Gesù Cristo vince". Sopra la croce si trova l'iscrizione in ebraico, sul lato inferiore quella araba, a sinistra l'iscrizione latina, a destra la greca. Le iscrizioni fanno riferimento alla morte di Anna, madre di Grisanto, prete del sovrano normanno Ruggero, morta nel 1148 e sepolta nella jâmi maggiore (poi Cattedrale di Palermo), e da lì fatta traslare dal figlio nella chiesa di San Michele Arcangelo, nella cappella detta di Sant'Anna, fatta costruire da Grisanto nel 1149. Le date presenti nelle quattro versioni sono, ciascuna con il computo del proprio calendario, corrispondenti al 1148 latino: 4904 ebraico, 6658 greco, 543 arabo. Nel museo della Zisa esiste un'altra lapide, ma in tre lingue (è escluso l'ebraico), che commemora la morte di Drogo, padre del prete Grisanto, anch'egli sepolto nella cappella di sant'Anna, nel 1153. L'iscrizione proviene dalla chiesa di San Michele Arcangelo, nelle vicinanze della Casa Professa dei Gesuiti, che conservava molte iscrizioni, anche latine, oggi adibita a magazzino della Biblioteca Comunale.

La lapide, in quattro lingue, commemora la morte di Anna, madre di Grisanto, prete del sovrano normanno Ruggero. Le date presenti nelle quattro versioni, ciascuna con il computo del proprio calendario, corrispondono tutte alla data latina del 1148.
place: Palermo, chiesa di San Michele Arcangelo (de Indulciis).
