en.name: Diyarbakır Citadel.
description:
The city known since ancient times as Amida, Kara-Amid, and Diyar Bakr was renamed Diyarbakır in 1938. The largest city in southeast Anatolia, it was founded on a 650-m high plateau on the right bank of the upper Tigris River. The city, which is completely surrounded by walls, covers an area measuring 1700 m from east to west and 1300 m from north to south; the city walls total 5 km in length. The walls rise above steep rocks in the east, and are surrounded in other places by moats approximately 6 m deep and 15 m wide, today mostly filled in with earth. The main wall ranges from 8 m to 12 m in height, and 4 m to 5 m in width. The walls are reinforced with 78 towers and a gate on each of the four cardinal directions. These are known as the Tigris or New Gate (east), Harput or Mountain Gate (north), Urfa (Rum, or Anatolia) Gate (west), and Mardin Gate or Bab al-Tell (south). The inner fortress, the original site of the city, has an additional, hidden gate leading to the bank of the Tigris (the Oğrun Kapı or 'Secret Gate'). Other than the fortress mosque, buildings known to have existed within the inner fortress, such as the Artuqid Palace and the Bıyıklı Mehmed Pasha Mansion, have not survived.  
Three large towers, their decoration known to have been added in the Turkish period, and surviving for the most part in good condition until the present day, are worth noting. The Ulu (or Evli) Beden (literally High Wall), located between the Urfa and Mardin Gates, has a semi-circular plan. The top and bottom parts of the inscription on its façade feature double-headed eagles, two human-headed lions, and two bulls. The Yedi Kardeşler (Seven Brothers) Tower resembles the Ulu Beden (High Wall) in both its plan and façade decorations; the inscription on its exterior is also decorated with a double-headed eagle and two lion figures. The Keçi Burcu (Goat Tower), near the Mardin Gate, is not decorated, although it does have an Arabic inscription in *kufic* script.  
In addition to towers, the four main gates opening into the city are decorated with symbols of power such as double-headed dragons, hunting horsemen, lions, and scenes of combat between lions and bulls.  
The walls of the fortress are mostly built of dark basalt cut stone with white limestone here and there.

The fortified walls encircling the old city of Diyarbakır are approximately 5 km long and have survived in good condition to a great extent. The fortifications, renowned for the decoration on the bastions and gates, underwent alterations during Roman, Byzantine, Abbasid, Marwanid, Artuqid and Seljuq periods. The Artuqid palace and Bıyıklı Mehmed Pasha mansion known to have been located within the citadel have not survived.
dates: Harput Gate: Hegira 297 / AD 910; Mardin Gate: Hegira 297 / AD 910; Melikshah Tower: Hegira 464–85 / AD 1072–92; Urfa Gate: Hegira 579 / AD 1183; Ulu Beden (High Wall): Hegira 605 / 1209; Yedi Kardeşler (Seven Brothers) Tower: Hegira 596–619 / AD 1200–22.
dynasty: Originally built during the reign of the Roman Emperor Constantine in AD 349. Additions and repairs made in the Byzantine, Abbasid, Marwanid, Artuqid and Seljuq periods.
artist: Harput Gate: Caliph Muqtadir (r. AH 295–319/ AD 908–32); Mardin Gate: Caliph Muqtadir (r. AH 295–319/ AD 908–32) and Nisanoğlu al-Muayyad (al-Muayyad, son of Nisan, AH ?–540 / AD ?–1145); Melikşah Tower: Sultan Malik Shah of the Great Seljuqs (r. AH 465–85 / AD 1073–92); Urfa Gate: Muhammad, son of the Artuqid ruler Qara Arslan (AH 562–81 / AD 1167–85); Ulu Beden (High Wall) and Yedi Kardeşler (Seven Brothers) Tower: Artuqid ruler al-Malik al-Salih Mahmud (r. 597–619 / 1201–22).

Harput Gate and Mardin Gate: Ahmed bin Cemil el-Amidi (Ahmad bin Jamil al-‘Amidi); Ulu Beden (High Wall): Ibrahim Caferoğlu (Ibrahim, son of Ja‘far); Yedi Kardeşler (Seven Brothers) Tower: Yahya, son of İbrahim aş-Şarafi (Yahya, son of Ibrahim al-Sharafi); Keçi Burcu (Goat Tower): Nasır bin Habib; Melikşah Tower: Ebi Nasr Muhammed bin Abd-ül-Vahid (Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahid).
keywords: Diyarbakır; Diyar Bakr; fortress; walls; figurative decoration

es.name: Ciudadela de Diyarbakır.
description:
Esta ciudad, conocida desde la antigüedad como Amida, Kara-Amid y Diyar Bakr, fue rebautizada en 1938 con el nombre de Diyarbakir. Fue fundada sobre un altiplano a 650 metros de altura en la orilla derecha del alto Tigris y es la ciudad más grande del sudeste de Anatolia. Abarca una superficie de 1.700 m de este a oeste y de 1.300 m de norte a sur, y está completamente rodeada por unas murallas de 5 km de perímetro. Las murallas orientales se levantan sobre escarpadas rocas; hay varios puntos del resto de las murallas que están rodeados de fosos defensivos, de unos 6 m de profundidad y 15 m de ancho. Actualmente, casi todos estos fosos están llenos de tierra. La muralla principal mide entre 8 y 12 m de alto y 4-5 m de ancho. Las murallas están reforzadas con 78 torres y tienen una puerta orientada a cada uno de los cuatro puntos cardinales. La puerta del este se conoce como puerta del Tigris o Puerta Nueva; la del norte, puerta Harput o de la Montaña; la del oeste, puerta de Urfa (Rum o Anatolia); y la del sur, puerta de Mardin o Bab al-Tall. La fortaleza interior, emplazamiento originario de la ciudad, tiene una puerta adicional oculta (Oğrun Kapı o 'puerta secreta') que conduce a la orilla del Tigris. Además de la mezquita fortificada, se sabe que existieron edificios en el interior de la ciudadela, como el palacio artuquí y la mansión de Bıyıklı Mehmed Paşa, que no han perdurado.  
Cabe mencionar tres torres grandes, decoradas durante el periodo turco, que se conservan en buen estado. El Ulu (o Evli) Beden (literalmente 'el muro alto'), situado entre las puertas Urfa y Mardin, tiene la planta semicircular. Las partes superior e inferior de la inscripción de la fachada presentan águilas bicéfalas, dos leones con cabeza humana y dos toros. La torre Yedi Kardeşler ('siete hermanos') se parece al Ulu Beden tanto en por su planta como por la decoración de su fachada; la inscripción del exterior está ornada también con un águila bicéfala y dos leones. La torre Keçi Burcu ('torre de la cabra'), cercana a la puerta de Mardin, no está decorada, aunque sí tiene una inscripción arábiga en letra cúfica.  
Además de las torres, las cuatro puertas principales que dan paso a la ciudad están adornadas con símbolos de poder como dragones bicéfalos, jinetes cazadores, leones y escenas de combate entre leones y toros.  
Las murallas de la fortaleza están construidas en su mayor parte con mampuestos de basalto oscuro y piedra caliza blanca en algunos lugares.

La muralla que rodea la antigua ciudad de Diyarbakır tienen una longitud aproximada de 5 km y gran parte de ella se conserva en buenas condiciones. Esta fortificación, célebre por la ornamentación de sus bastiones y puertas, sufrió diversas alteraciones durante los periodos romano, bizantino, abbasí, marwaní, artuquí y selyuquí. No se conservan ni el palacio artuquí ni la mansión de Bıyıklı Mehmed Paşa que en otro tiempo estuvieron en su interior.
dates: Puerta de Harput: 297 de la Hégira / 910 d. C.; puerta de Mardin: 297 / 910; torre Melikshah: 464-485 / 1072-1092; puerta de Urfa: 579 / 1183; Ulu Beden ('muro alto'): 605 / 1209; Yedi Kardeşler ('siete hermanos'): 596-619 / 1200-1222.
dynasty: La construcción original data de tiempos del emperador romano Constantino, en 349 d. C.; en los periodos bizantino, abbasí, marwaní, artuquí y selyuquí fue objeto de ampliaciones y restauraciones.
artist: Puerta de Harput: califa Muqtadir (r. 295-319 / 908-932); puerta de Mardin: califa Muqtadir (r. 295-319 / 908-932) y Nisanoğlu al-Muayyad (al-Muayyad, hijo de Nisan, ?-540 / ?-1145); torre Melikshah: sultán Malik Shah de los grandes selyuquíes (r. 465-485 / 1073-1092); puerta de Urfa: Muhammad, hijo del soberano artuquí Qara Arslan (562-581 / 1167-1185); Ulu Beden y torre de Yedi Kardeşler: gobernador artuquí al-Malik al-Salih Mahmud (r. 597-619 / 1201-1222).

Puertas Harput y Mardin: Ahmed bin Cemil el-Amidi (Ahmad ibn Yamil al-Amidi); Ulu Beden: Ibrahim Caferoğlu (Ibrahim, hijo de Yafar); torre Yedi Kardeşler: Yahya, hijo de İbrahim aş-Şarafi (Ibrahim al-Sharafi); Keçi Burcu ('torre de la cabra'): Nasir ibn Habib; torre Melikshah: Ebi Nasr Muhammed bin Abd-ül-Vahid (Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahid).
keywords: Diyarbakır; Diyar Bakr; alcazaba; murallas; decoración figurativa.

fr.name: Citadelle de Diyarbakır.
description:
Connue depuis l'Antiquité sous les noms de Amida, de Kara-Ami et de Diyar Bakr, la cité a reçu son nouveau nom de Diyarbakir en 1938. Plus grande ville du sud-est de l'Anatolie, elle est située sur un haut-plateau à 650 m d'altitude sur le cours supérieur du Tigre. Entièrement entourée de 5 km de murailles, elle mesure environ 1 700 m d'est en ouest et 1300 m du nord au sud. Ses remparts s'élèvent sur des escarpements rocheux à l'est et sont entourés pour le reste de douves d'environ 6 m de profondeur et 15 m de large, la plupart étant comblées aujourd'hui. Le rempart principal mesure de 4 à 5 m de large pour 8 à 12 m de haut. Il est renforcé par 78 tours et percé d'une porte à chacun des quatre points cardinaux : la porte du Tigre ou porte Nouvelle à l'est, la porte d'Harput ou porte de la Montagne au nord, la porte d'Urfa (Rum ou d'Anatolie) à l'ouest et la porte de Mardin ou Bab al-Tell au sud. La forteresse qui se dresse à l'intérieur, sur le site d'origine de la ville, possède une porte supplémentaire dissimulée dont sur la rive du Tigre (la Oğrun Kapı ou “porte secrète”). Dans cette enceinte, outre la mosquée, ont existé jadis un palais artukide et la résidence de Bıyıklı Mehmed Pacha.  
Trois importantes tours dont la décoration date de la période turque sont restées pour leur plus grande part en bon état. La tour de Ulu (ou Evli) Beden (littéralement du haut mur), située entre les portes d'Urfa et de Mardin, est de plan semi-circulaire. L'inscription de sa façade est encadrée par des aigles bicéphales, deux lions à tête humaine et deux taureaux. La tour Yedi Kardeşler (des Sept Frères) ressemble à la précédente aussi bien dans son plan que dans son décor de façade. Son inscription est également encadrée d'un aigle bicéphale et de deux lions. La Keçi Burcu (tour de la Chèvre), près de la porte de Mardin, ne comporte aucun décor si ce n'est une inscription arabe en coufique.  
Les autres portes d'entrée principales sont décorées de divers symboles du pouvoir, parmi lesquels des dragons bicéphales, des chasseurs à cheval, des lions et des scènes de combat entre des lions et des taureaux.  
Les murailles de la forteresse sont pour l'essentiel en basalte taillé ponctué de quelques moellons calcaires.

La muraille qui encercle la vieille ville de Diyarbakır mesure approximativement 5 km de long et est en grande partie conservée. Les fortifications, fameuses pour la décoration des bastions et des portes, subirent des altérations durant les périodes romaine, byzantine, abbasside, marwanide, artukide et seldjoukide. Un palais artukide et la résidence de Bıyıklı Mehmed Pacha, jadis à l’intérieur de la citadelle, n’ont pas résisté au temps.
dates: Porte d’Harput : 297 de l’Hégire / 910 J.-C. ; porte de Mardin : 297 H / 910 J.-C. ; tour de Melikchah : 464-485 H / 1072-1092 J.-C. ; porte d’Urfa : 579 H / 1183 J.-C. ; Ullu Beden (le Haut Mur) : 605 H / 1209 J.-C. ; Yedi Kardeşler (tour des Sept Frères) : 596-619 H / 1200-1222.
dynasty: La construction d’origine date du règne de l’empereur romain Constantin en 349. Des adjonctions et des réparations ont été réalisées aux époques byzantine, abbasside, marwanide, artukide et seldjoukide.
artist: Porte d’Harput : calife Mouqtadir (r. 295-319 H / 908-932 J.-C.) ; porte de Mardin : calife Mouqtadir (r. 295-319 H / 908-932 J.-C.) et Nisanoğlu al-Mouayyad (al-Mouayyad, fils de Nisan, ?-540 H / ?-1145 J.-C.) ; Tour de Melikchah : sultan Malik Chah des Grands Seldjoukides (r. 465-485 H / 1073-1092 J.-C.) ; porte d’Urfa : Muhammad, fils du souverain artukide Qara Arslan (562-581 H / 1167-1185) ; Ulu Beden (le Haut Mur) et tour Yedi Kardeşler (tour des Sept Frères) : souverain artukide al-Malik al-Salih Mahmoud (r. 597-619 H / 1201-1222 J.-C.).

Portes d’Harput et de Mardin : Ahmed bin Cemil el-Amidi (Ahmad bin Jamil al-Amidi) ; Ulu Beden (le Haut Mur) : Ibrahim Caferoğlu (Ibrahim, fils de Ja’far) ; tour Yedi Kardeşler (porte des Sept Frères) : Yahya, fils de Ibrahim al-Charafi ; tour Keçi Burcu (tour de la Chèvre) : Nasır bin Habib ; tour Melikchah : Ebi Nasr Muhammed bin Abd-ül-Vahid (Abou Nasr Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahid).
keywords: Diyarbakir ; Diyar Bakr ; forteresse ; remparts ; décoration figurative

tr.name: Diyarbakır Kalesi.
description:
Antik çağlardan beri, *Amida*, *Kara-Amid*, *Diyar Bakr* adlarıyla anılan kent, 1938 yılında *Diyarbakır* olarak isimlendirilmiştir. Güneydoğu Anadolu Bölgesi'nin en büyük kenti olan Diyarbakır, Dicle'nin yukarı havzasında, nehrin sağ kıyısına hakim, 650 metre yükseklikte bir plato üzerinde kurulmuştur. çevresi tamamen surlarla kuşatılmış olan kentin, doğu-batı yönünde 1700 metre, kuzey-güney yönünde 1300 metrelik bir alanı çevreleyen surları toplam 5 km. uzunluğundadır. Doğuda sarp kayalar üzerinde yükselen surlar diğer yönlerde, yaklaşık 6 metre derinliğinde 15 metre genişliğinde, bugün büyük bir kısmı toprakla dolmuş olan hendeklerle çevrilmiştir. Ana duvarın yerden yüksekliği 8-12 metre, kalınlığı ise 4-5 metre arasında değişmektedir. Surların üzerinde 78 burç ve dört ana yönde dört kapı yer almaktadır. *Doğudaki Dicle* (Yeni) *Kapı*, kuzeydeki *Harput* (Dağ) *Kapı*, batıdaki *Urfa* (Rum=Anadolu) *Kapı* ve güneydeki *Mardin Kapı* (Bab-el Tell) adıyla anılmaktadır. Şehrin ilk kurulduğu yer olan iç kalenin, Dicle nehri kıyısına ulaşan gizli bir kapısı daha vardır (Oğrun Kapı). İç kalede, Kale Camisi dışında, varlığı bilinen Artukoğulları Sarayı ve Bıyıklı Mehmed Paşa Konağı günümüze ulaşamamıştır.  
  
Türk döneminde eklendiği bilinen ve günümüze büyük ölçüde sağlam olarak ulaşan üç büyük burç süslemeleriyle dikkat çekmektedir. Urfa Kapı ile Mardin Kapı arasındaki **Ulu (Evli) Beden**, yarım daire kesitli bir plan şemasına sahiptir. Cephesindeki kitabenin alt ve üst kesimlerinde, çift başlı kartal, insan başlı iki aslan, ve iki boğa tasviri yer almaktadır. Plan şeması ve cephe süslemeleri açısından Ulu Beden'e benzeyen **Yedi Kardeş Burcu**'nun cephesini ortalayan kitabenin çevresinde de, çift başlı bir kartal ile iki aslan figürü dikkati çekmektedir. Mardin Kapı yakınındaki **Keçi Burcu**, süslemesiz olmakla birlikte, Kufi yazılı bir Arapça kitabeye sahiptir.  
  
Yukarıdaki burçlar dışında, kente açılan dört ana kapının çevresinde de, güç simgesi olarak çift başlı ejder, atlı avcı, aslan ve aslan-boğa mücadelesi gibi figürlü süslemeler görülmektedir.  
  
Kale surlarının büyük bir kısmı koyu renkli bazalt kesme taşlarla ve yer yer beyaz kireç taşı ile inşa edilmiştir.

Kenti çevreleyen yaklaşık 5 kilometre uzunluğundaki surların büyük bir kısmı günümüze sağlam olarak ulaşmıştır. Roma, Bizans, Abbasi, Mervani, Artuklu ve Selçuklu dönemlerinde önemli değişiklikler geçirmiş olan kale, burçları ve kapıları üzerinde yer alan süslemeleriyle ünlüdür. Kale içinde varlığı bilinen, Artuklu Sarayı ve Bıyıklı Mehmet Paşa Konağı günümüze ulaşamamıştır.
dates: Harput Kapı: 297/910; Mardin Kapı: 297/910; Melikşah Burcu: 464-485 / 1072-1092; Urfa Kapı: 579/1183; Ulu Beden: 605/1209; Yedi Kardeş Burcu: 596-619 / 1200-1222.
dynasty: 349 tarihinde, Roma İmparatoru Constantinus zamanında ilk kez inşa edilmiştir. Bizans, Abbasi, Mervani, Artuklu ve Selçuklu dönemlerinde çeşitli eklemeler ve onarımlar yapılmıştır.
artist: Harput Kapı: Halife Muktedir; Mardin Kapı: Halife Muktedir ve 540/1145, Nisanoğlu El-Muayyed; Melikşah Burcu: Büyük Selçuklu Sultanı Melikşah; Urfa Kapı: Artuklu Hükümdarı Kara Arslan’ın oğlu Muhammed; Ulu Beden ve Yedi Kardeş Burcu: Artuklu Hükümdarı El Melik as-Salih Mahmud.

Mardin Kapı ve Harput Kapı: Ahmed bin Cemil el-Amidi; Ulu Beden: Cafer oğlu İbrahim; Yedi Kardeş Burcu: İbrahim as-Şarafi’nin oğlu Yahya; Keçi Burcu: Nasır bin Habib; Melikşah Burcu: Ebi Nasr Muhammed bin Abd-ül-Vahid.
keywords: Diyarbakır; Diyar Bakr; kale; sur; figürlü süsleme

de.name: Stiftskirche, Stuck
description: Die überaus reiche Stuckausstattung ist ein bedeutendes Beispiel der frühbarocken Stukkatorenschule von München mit Feldergliederung in klassischen Formen, im Chor auch durch figurale Reliefs bereichert. Unter der Leitung des Bildhauers Onofrius Weigl arbeiteten wohl auch Stukkatoren aus Wessobrunn.

en.name: Collegiate church, stucco
description: The exceedingly rich stuccowork is an important example of the Early Baroque Munich school of stucco with panels structured in classical forms, which in the choir are also enriched with figurative reliefs. The work, under the direction of the sculptor Onofrius Weigl, was also executed by stucco masons of the Wessobrunn school.

en.name: The stand of the Italian Community in Tunisia at the International Exhibition held in Turin in 1911
short_description:
The picture shows how, on the occasion of the 1911 international exhibition in Turin the Italian community in Tunisia chose to represent itself by blending elements taken from the Italian and from the Tunisian material culture.  
One can read the sign E. & A. Coen, Tunisi, Susa, Sfax. Eugenio and Alfredo Coen were the owners of a furniture factory and of the imposing furniture shop, “Au Palais Arabe”, in downtown Tunis.

en.name: Ceiling paintings
description: In the central field of the painting surrounded by angels sits a winged woman dressed in a white robe and blue cloak. Her attributes – a crown on her head, a triangle on her breast symbolising the Holy Trinity, a rope and a ring in her hands, flames around her head and a mirror (without stain) – match the iconography of the Immaculate Conception and the Blessed Virgin Mary, being here also a symbol of the Church.

en.name: Mansura
description:
This former fortified camp, later a city, was destroyed by its besieged residents and rebuilt. Today it is nothing but ruins. The building remnants were exploited by the Abdalwadids, who found slabs, onyx capitals, marble and columns that were repurposed in later Tlemcen monuments.  
  
Temporarily the official capital of the Marinids after the fall of Tlemcen in 735 / 1335, Mansura was protected by a rampart 12 metres high, with 80 towers, enclosing an area of 100 hectares in the shape of a trapezoid. Apart from a few sections of rampart walls, only ruins of the old mosque and the *mosalla* (prayer area) remain.  
  
Of the mosque built by Abu Yacoub in 701 / 1302, remnants include pieces of the wall, traces of the *mihrab* and three facades of the magnificent 40-metre-high minaret. Site excavations have helped reconstruct the original plan. Several doors provided access to the mosque, the main one located at the base of the minaret. This door opened on a square courtyard measuring 30 metres per side, framed by three naves. The courtyard preceded the prayer room, 30 metres long and divided into 13 naves by onyx columns.  
  
The minaret’s main doorway, 2.50 metres wide, is topped by decorated arcs within a rectangular frame with inscriptions and two spandrels. The entry arch rests on two onyx columns. On the facade above the doorway is a vault in low relief ornamented with *muqarnas* (honeycomb vaults). Higher up is a vertical diamond-patterned rectangular section, and at the top of the facade is a blind gallery of pointed arches on narrow columns. The minaret, a much-admired masterpiece of Maghreb and Andalusian art, evokes the Qal’at Bani Hammad, the Giralda of Seville, the Kutubiya Mosque of Marrakesh, the Hassan tower in Rabat and the Puerta del Vino in Granada.  
  
Legend has it that globes of gold adorned the summit. They say that the sultan commissioned a Jew to build the minaret, and once his task was completed the sultan forbade him to descend by the interior staircase, which was reserved for Muslims. The unfortunate man had to jump from the top of the minaret, but the legend is vague about the outcome of the story. Some say the unfortunate mason was killed by the fall; others say he was saved miraculously by a whirlwind that carried him to the top of a hill a few kilometres away, to a place still known today as the Jewish Pass.

fr.name: Mansourah
description:
De cet ancien camp fortifié devenu une ville détruite par les assiégés et reconstruite en 735/1335 ne subsistent aujourd’hui que des ruines. Ces vestiges ont été exploités, notamment, par les Abdalwadides qui trouvèrent là dalles, chapiteaux d’onyx, marbres et colonnes remployés pour l’ornementation des monuments tlemcéniens construits par la suite.  
  
Temporairement capitale officielle des Mérinides après la chute de Tlemcen en 735/1335, Mansourah était protégée par un rempart de 12 mètres de haut comportant 80 tours et entourant une superficie de 100 hectares en forme de trapèze. À part quelques pans de rempart, il n’en subsiste actuellement que les ruines de la vieille mosquée et la *moçalla*, la grande aire consacrée à la prière. Il ne reste de la mosquée construite par Abou Yacoub en 701/1302 que des parties du mur, la trace du *mihrab* et une partie du magnifique minaret de 40 m de haut, dont trois façades ont été conservées. Les fouilles sur le site ont permis d’en reconstituer le plan. Plusieurs portes livraient accès à la mosquée, dont la principale est située à la base du minaret. L’arc de cette porte, de 2,50 mètres d’ouverture, s’inscrit dans un encadrement formé de défoncements successifs, avec une bordure rectangulaire comprenant des inscriptions et deux écoinçons chargés d’arabesques. L’arc repose sur deux colonnes en onyx. Au-dessus se trouvaient un encorbellement porté par des *mouqarnas*, un panneau réticulé et, au sommet du minaret, une fausse galerie d’arcatures brisées et de fines colonnettes. Cette porte s’ouvrait sur une cour carrée de 30 mètres de côté, encadrée par trois nefs et qui précédait la salle de prière, longue de 30 mètres et divisée en treize nefs par des colonnes d’onyx.  
  
Ce minaret, qui figure parmi les plus admirables chefs-d’oeuvre de l’art maghrébin et andalou, rappelle tout autant la Qalaa des Beni Hammad, la Giralda de Séville, la Koutoubiya de Marrakech, la tour Hassan à Rabat que la Puerta del Vino à Grenade. Il est auréolé de la légende selon laquelle des globes d’or auraient orné son sommet. On raconte qu’il a été construit par un juif à qui le sultan, une fois sa tâche achevée, interdit de redescendre par l’escalier intérieur de l’édifice, réservé aux musulmans. Le malheureux dut sauter du sommet du minaret, mais la légende est hésitante sur l’issue de l’histoire : pour les uns, l’infortuné maçon se tua en tombant, pour les autres il fut miraculeusement sauvé par un tourbillon de vent qui l’emporta à quelques kilomètres de là, au sommet d’une colline, à l’endroit même que l’on nomme aujourd’hui encore le col du Juif.

ar.name: زجاجة لاعب البولو .
description:
إن زجاجة لاعب البولو هذه هي النموذج الوحيد المحفوظ بشكل كامل من أيام المماليك وتمثل فن الزجاج المملوكي، ولها إفريز يمثل فرساناً يقفزون إلى اليمين يحمل أحدهم مضرب البولو. وقد كانت لعبة البولو محبوبة جداً لدى حكام المماليك من حيث أنها تجمع بين التدريب العسكري واللعب. وقد صنعت هذه الزجاجة على الأغلب في سورية أو مصر بتكليف من أحد الحكام الرسوليين في اليمن بدليل وجود زهور حمراء خماسية الأوراق في إفريز الكتف على أرضية بيضاء، التي توجد كذلك على الأعمال المعدنية التي طلب هؤلاء الحكام أيضاَ تصنيعها.  
الزجاجة مصنوعة من زجاج ذي لون أصفر فاتح ويكاد يكون عديم اللون. وتتكون هذه الزجاجة من جسم مكوّر على قاعدة حلقية وهو مصنوع من زجاج منفوخ ذي أضلاع عمودية ينتهي في الأعلى برقبة أسطوانية عالية. أما الرسوم ذات الحدود الحمراء، وهي عبارة عن رسوم مطلية بالميناء أو مذهبة، فإنها محفوظة بشكل غير واضح تماماً. ويتكون الإفريز الرئيسي لهذه الزجاجة من اثني عشر لاعباً (خيّالاً) يتجهون نحو اليمين وفوق ذلك هناك إفريز أمام غصن تجري فيه حيوانات إلى اليسار (أرانب وغزال ودب وكلاب صيد). وتتقاطع مع هذا الإفريز ثلاث زهور. كما تزين ثلاثة عصافير إفريز الكتف، ويلتف حول الرقبة إفريز ملون من الكتابة على أرضية ذهبية. وتتضمن الكتابة بشكل عام مديحاً عاماً ولذلك لا يمكن الاستفادة منها لتأريخ هذه القطعة.  
إن الحفظ الجيد والكامل لهذه الزجاجة يثير الإعجاب. كما يقال إنها كانت في الصين ووصلت إلى ملكية غراف ف. فون بورتاليس في القرن التاسع عشر. وكما يظهر على زجاجات أخرى مماثلة أن السبب في حفظها الجيد يكمن في أنها كانت مملوءة بتربة مقدسة أو بقايا آثار تذكارية، وحفظت مع كنوز بعض الكنائس الأوروبية. ويعتقد أن هذا النوع من الأوعية المنقوشة كانت تصنع بأعداد كبيرة، بدليل وجود الكثير من بقاياها المكسرة في مجموعات متعددة وجدت كلها تقريباً في تلال أنقاض القاهرة القديمة. ومن المرجح أن الفنانين المهرة كانوا ينتجون هذه القطع الفنية الصغيرة في أوقات قصيرة.

كانت المشاغل المملوكية تنتج أوانٍ زجاجية رشيقة، مثل هذه القارورة التي زيَّنها أحد رسَّامي الزجاج بإفريز بفرسان يحمل أحدهم مضرب بولو. ولعبة البولو كانت بالغة الشيوع في بلاطات المماليك الأميرية. والأواني الزجاجية المُرصَّعة المُزيَّنة بالرسوم، كانت تحظى بقدرٍ كبير من الإعجاب في أوروبا.
keywords: زجاج مطلي بالميناء؛ سوريا؛ مصر؛ عهد مملوكي.
partner: متحف الفن الإسلامي في متحف بيرغامون ، المتاحف الحكومية

de.name: Poloreiterflasche.
description: Die Poloreiterflasche ist das einzige vollständig erhaltene Beispiel der mamlukischen Glaskunst mit einem Fries nach rechts sprengender Reiter, von denen einer einen Poloschläger hält. Das Polospiel war bei den Mamluken-Herrschern sehr beliebt, vereinte es doch militärische Übung und Spiel. Die Flasche wurde in Syrien oder in Ägypten wahrscheinlich als Auftrag für einen Rasulidenherrscher im Jemen hergestellt, da die in dem Schulterfries sitzenden roten, fünfblättrigen Rosetten auf weißem Grund auf Metallarbeiten vorkommen, die ebenfalls Auftragsarbeiten für diese Herrscher waren. Die Fasche ist aus fast farblosem, hellgelben Glas gearbeitet. Der bauchige, auf einem Fußring stehende Flaschenkörper aus optisch geblasenem, vertikal geripptem Glas hat einen hohen zylindrischen Hals. Zurückhaltend ist die rotkonturierte, entweder mit Emailfarben oder nur in Gold ausgeführte Malerei. Der Hauptfries dieser Flasche besteht aus zwölf nach rechts sprengenden Reitern. Darüber befindet sich vor einer Ranke ein Fries nach links laufender Tiere (Hasen, eine Gazelle und ein Bär sowie Jagdhunde). Der Fries wird von drei Rosetten unterbrochen. Die Schulterpartie zieren drei Vögel. Um den Hals legt sich ein farbiger Schriftfries auf goldenem Grund. Die Inschrift enthält allgemeine Lobpreisungen und kann daher nicht als Anhaltungspunkt für eine Datierung gelten. Die perfekte Erhaltung der Flasche erregt immer wieder Erstaunen. Angeblich soll sie sich in China befunden haben und gelangte im 19. Jh. in die Slg. Graf F. v. Pourtalès. Wie andere Flaschen zeigen, haben sie sich vielfach dadurch erhalten, dass sie gefüllt mit heiliger Erde oder ähnlichen Reliquien in europäische Kirchenschätze gelangten. Wie zahlreiche Fragmente in verscheidenen Sammlungen zeigen, die fast alle aus den Schutthügeln von Alt-Kairo stammen, müssen derartige bemalte Gefäße in großer Anzahl hergestellt worden sein. Offensichtlich haben die versierten Künstler in kurzer Zeit diese kleinen Kunstwerke produziert.

Mamlukische Werkstätten produzierten elegante Glasgefäße so wie diese Flasche. Ein Glasmaler hatte hier ein Fries mit Reitern hinzugefügt, von denen einer einen Poloschläger trägt. Emaillierte Glasgefäße waren sind Europa sehr beliebt.
keywords: Emailliertes Glas; Mamluken; Syrien; Ägypten
partner: Museum für Islamische Kunst, Pergamon Museum

en.name: Bottle with polo-playing riders.
description:
This bottle depicting polo players is the only complete example of Mamluk glasswork featuring a frieze of riders galloping to the right-hand side, one of whom is holding a polo stick. Polo was much-loved by the Mamluk rulers, uniting both military exercise and game. The bottle was made in Egypt or Syria, probably on commission for a Rasulid ruler in Yemen, as the red five-leaved rosettes on a white background on the frieze around the shoulder of the bottle appear also on metalwork which was produced on commission for these rulers.  
The bottle is made of nearly colourless, light-yellow glass. Its bulbous body, with its long cylindrical neck, is made of optically blown glass with vertical grooves and it sits on a circular base. The paint work, which is contoured in red and uses either the colours of enamel or just plain gold, is restrained. The principal frieze on this bottle consists of 12 riders galloping to the right. Above this frieze, over a tendril, there is another frieze in which animals (hares, a gazelle, a bear and hunting dogs) are running to the left. Three rosettes break up this frieze. The bottle’s shoulder part is adorned with three birds. The neck is covered by a colourful inscription over a gold background. The inscription consists of general words of praise, and cannot be used as a starting point from which to date the object.  
The bottle’s perfect condition never fails to provoke astonishment. Allegedly, the bottle made its way to China, and in the 19th century became part of the collection of Count F. von Pourtalès. Bottles, as other examples demonstrate, were often preserved because, filled with holy soil or other such relics, they became part of European church treasuries. This sort of painted receptacle must have been produced in large quantities, as the great number of fragments from different collections demonstrate – most of which were found in the rubble of Cairo’s old city. Obviously experienced artists created these small works of art in a short space of time.  
  
Click [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=py7pVIzmSuk&t=24s) to **watch a video presentation** of this artefact.

Mamluk workshops produced elegant glass vessels such as this bottle, to which a glass painter has added a frieze with horsemen, one of whom has a polo mallet. The game of polo was extremely popular at the princely courts of the Mamluks. Enamel-painted glass vessels were much admired in Europe.
holder: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum
keywords: Enamelled glass; Mamluk; Syria; Egypt
partner: Museum of Islamic Art at the Pergamon Museum, State Museums

es.name: Botella con jugadores de polo.
description:
Esta botella es el único ejemplo íntegro que se conserva del trabajo mameluco en vidrio. Presenta un friso con doce jinetes galopando hacia la derecha, uno de ellos con una maza de polo. El polo era una de las actividades preferidas de los gobernantes mamelucos, ya que combinaba el ejercicio militar con el juego. La botella, fabricada en Egipto o Siria, fue encargada, probablemente, por un gobernante rasulí de Yemen, pues las rosetas rojas de cinco hojas sobre fondo blanco del cuello son las mismas que solían decorar las obras de metalistería hechas para estos gobernantes.  
La botella está hecha en vidrio soplado amarillo claro, casi incoloro, con surcos verticales; tiene cuerpo bulboso, cuello alargado cilíndrico y pie circular. La sobria decoración pictórica se delineó en rojo y se pintó con esmaltes o un sencillo dorado. Por encima de los doce jinetes hay otra franja con tres rosetas y animales (liebres, una gacela, un oso y perros de caza) que corren hacia la izquierda, todo sobre fondo de tallos. Los hombros de la botella están decorados con tres pájaros y el cuello presenta una inscripción de varios colores sobre fondo dorado con palabras de elogio y que no sirve para datar la pieza.  
Llama la atención el perfecto estado en que se ha conservado esta botella que, supuestamente, acabó en China antes de que, en el siglo XIX, pasara a formar parte de la colección del Conde F. von Pourtales. Las botellas, tal como demuestran algunos ejemplos, se conservaron con frecuencia debido a que pertenecieron a tesoros de iglesias europeas, donde se utilizaban para guardar tierra sagrada u otras reliquias. En vista de los numerosos fragmentos hallados –la mayoría de ellos en ruina de la ciudad antigua de El Cairo–, los recipientes pintados debieron de fabricarse en grandes cantidades. Obviamente, los artesanos hacían estas pequeñas obras de arte en muy poco tiempo.

Los talleres mamelucos producían elegantes recipientes de vidrio como esta botella, que un pintor decoró con jinetes, uno de ellos con un palo de polo, juego popular en la corte mameluca. En Europa eran muy admirados estos vidrios decorados con esmalte.
holder: Museo de Arte Islámico del Museo Pergamon
dates: Alrededor del año 700 de la Hégira / 1300 d. C.
keywords: Vidrio esmaltado; mameluco; Siria; Egipto
partner: Museo de Arte Islámico en el Museo de Pérgamo, Museos Estatales

fr.name: Bouteille aux joueurs de polo.
description:
Cette bouteille est le seul exemplaire conservé intact de verrerie mamelouke qui présente une frise de cavaliers s'élançant vers la droite, l'un d'eux tenant un maillet de polo. Le jeu de polo était très prisé à la cour des souverains mamelouks, il unissait l'aspect ludique et l'exercice militaire. L'objet a sans doute été fabriqué en Syrie ou en Égypte sur commande d'un souverain rasoulide du Yémen, les rosettes rouges à cinq lobes sur fond blanc dans la frise de l'épaulement rappelant le même motif sur des métaux exécutés pour ces souverains.  
La bouteille est faite d'un verre presque incolore, d'un jaune très clair. Le corps est en forme de panse sur une base annulaire, en verre soufflé optiquement à côtes verticales, le col est haut et cylindrique. Le décor peint est discret, en contours rouges, exécuté en couleurs émaillées ou simplement à l'or. La frise principale figure douze cavaliers s'élançant vers la droite. Au-dessus court sur fond de rinceaux une frise d'animaux s'élançant vers la gauche (des lièvres, une gazelle, un ours et des chiens de chasse). La frise est interrompue par des rosettes. L'épaulement est agrémenté de trois oiseaux. Le départ du col est enserré dans une frise épigraphique colorée sur fond d'or. L'inscription comporte des vœux d'ordre général et ne peut donc servir à la datation de l'objet.  
Le parfait état de conservation de cette bouteille est toujours un objet d'étonnement. Elle semble s'être trouvée en Chine et, de là, être parvenue dans la collection du comte de Pourtalès au XIXe siècle. D'autres exemples montrent que la conservation est due au fait que ces bouteilles sont parvenues remplies de terre sainte ou d'autres reliques dans les trésors des églises européennes. D'après les nombreux fragments conservés dans différentes collections, presque tous issus des monticules-dépotoirs du Vieux-Caire, les récipients peints de ce type ont dû être fabriqués en très grandes quantités. Les artisans expérimentés ont manifestement réalisé ces petites œuvres très rapidement.

Les ateliers mamelouks produisaient d'élégants récipients en verre comme cette bouteille, à laquelle un peintre sur verre a ajouté une frise de cavaliers, dont l'un tient un maillet de polo, un sport très prisé à la cour des souverains mamelouks. Les récipients en verre décorés d'émail étaient très appréciés en Europe.
keywords: Verre émaillé ; mamelouk ; Syrie ; Égypte
partner: Musée d’art islamique du Pergamon Museum (Museum für Islamische Kunst)

en.name: *Madonna and Child with St. John Nepomuk*
description:
The painting is a *bozzetto* (study) for the altar piece commissioned by Benedict XIII for the canonisation of John Nepomuk on 11 March 1729, and intended for the Basilica di San Giovanni in Laterano. The canvas shows John Nepomuk (named after his place of birth: Pomuk, the ancient name for the city of Nepomuk) kneeling before the Madonna and Child, surrounded by *putti* and angels.  
One in the foreground is showing the palm leaf of the martyr and has raised his finger to his mouth, a gesture that alludes to the virtue of the saint, renowned not only as protector of Bohemia, but also as the patron saint of confessors. John, confessor of the queen, aligned himself with the Archbishop of Prague against the claims of King Wenceslaus IV who imprisoned him for refusing to divulge the secrets of the confessional. He was tortured by the King before being flung from the Charles Bridge and drowned in the Vltava.  
The martyrdom is reproduced in the background behind the saint, who is dressed in his priestly robes and canonical cape. Beside Mary, another angel is giving the martyr the crown of stars that, according to tradition, surrounded his head as he floated in the river. The study, usually dated to the 1720s, was acquired by the Italian State in 1921, and is therefore not a part of the Borghese family collection.  
The painting is from Conca's early period when he was one of Rome's most fashionable artists. His painting style of grandiose and exuberant lines, similar to the style of Carlo Maratta, is characteristic of a later phase of Baroque painting, by then infused with the appealing and exuberant language of Rococo culture. As proof of the altarpiece's renown and the devotion of the Bohemian saint, prints were made of it, one of which was engraved by Gottlib Heiss in 1735 and is part of the Borghese collection.

The *bozzetto* (study) was made by Sebastiano Conca for an altarpiece in St. Giovanni in Laterano (now lost). Conca, from Naples, arrived in Rome in 1706 at which time his style was similar to that of Carlo Maratta.  
This is a typical example of a Baroque altarpiece, the *sacrum* appearing in a monumental internal space providing a clear perspective.  
Conca's painting, with its exuberant, grandiose lines, is characteristic of late Baroque art and its captivating and magniloquent language is taken from Rococo culture.
keywords: Bozzetto; Neapolitan painters; altarpiece; perspective; cult of martyrdom

it.name: *La Madonna col Bambino e san Giovanni Nepomuceno*
description: Il dipinto costituisce il modello per la pala commissionata da Benedetto XIII per la canonizzazione di Giovanni Nepomuceno avvenuta l'11 marzo del 1729 e destinata alla basilica di san Giovanni in Laterano. Nella tela è raffigurato san Giovanni Nepomuceno - così chiamato dal luogo di nascita Pomuk, antico nome della città di Nepomuk – inginocchiato davanti alla Madonna col Bambino, attorniati da putti ed angeli. Quello in primo piano mostra la palma del martirio e porta il dito sulle labbra, gesto che allude alla virtù del santo, noto non solo come protettore della Boemia, ma anche come patrono dei confessori. Giovanni infatti, schieratosi al fianco dell'arcivescovo di Praga contro le pretese del re Venceslao IV e confessore della regina, imprigionato dal sovrano si rifiutò di violare il segreto della confessione; torturato dallo stesso re venne poi scaraventato dal ponte Carlo IV, morendo annegato nella Moldava. L' episodio del martirio è riprodotto sullo sfondo alle spalle del santo, in abito sacerdotale e con la cappa dei canonici. Si noti accanto a Maria l' altro angelo che porge al martire la corona di stelle, quella che secondo la tradizione gli circondava la testa mentre il suo corpo galleggiava sul fiume. Il bozzetto, genericamente riferito agli anni '20 del Settecento, è stato acquistato dallo Stato Italiano nel 1921, non è dunque parte della collezione della famiglia Borghese. Il dipinto si colloca nella fase giovanile del Conca, uno degli esponenti più in voga nella Roma del tempo; le sua pittura, dalle linee esuberanti e grandiose vicine allo stile di Carlo Maratta, definisce la fase più tarda della pittura barocca, ormai impregnata da quel linguaggio accattivante e magniloquente, proprio della cultura rococò. A riprova della celebrità della pala, ma anche della devozione del santo boemo, vennero realizzate stampe di traduzione, di cui una incisa da Gottlib Heiss nel 1735, è nella collezione Borghese.

Modello di Sebastiano Conca per una pala d'altare per San Giovanni in Laterano (ora perduta). Conca, giunse da Napoli a Roma nel 1706, epoca in cui si avvicinò allo stile di Carlo Maratta.  
Quest'opera è un tipico esempio di pala d'altare barocca, con un'apparizione del *sacrum* in uno spazio monumentale interno posto in relazione con una vista aperta.  
La pittura di Conca, dalle linee esuberanti e grandiose, definisce la fase più tarda della pittura barocca, ormai caratterizzata da un linguaggio accattivante e magniloquente, proprio della cultura rococò.
keywords: Bozzetto; pittori napoletani; pala d'altare; prospettiva; culto del martirio

en.name: Palazzo Pepoli Campogrande
description: The façade overlooking via Castiglione opens in the middle, with a rich diamond portal. The ceiling of the staircase was decorated by Domenico Maria Canuti (1665) with two important episodes of the life of Taddeo Pepoli, inside oval frames. Taddeo is shown becoming the ruler of Bologna in 1337 and when he was appointed apostolic vicar by Pope Benedict XII in 1340. The ballroom ceiling is one of the most significant examples of Bolognese baroque. Canuti was aided by Mengazzino for the perspective painting. The middle of an opened ceiling with strong scenographic light shows the *Glorification of Hercules* (1669-1671). The eye of the viewer is attracted by the dynamic tension of the figures moving upwards and by the illusionistic architecture. In the following room the Rolli brothers painted the *Triumph of the Bolognese Aristocracy* which depicts the twinning of Bologna and Venice (1686). In the next rooms the anti-classical painter Giuseppe Maria Crespi painted between 1699 and 1700 *The Four Seasons* and *The Olympus*. The figures stand directly on the framing of the ceiling without employing an illusory perspective. The beautiful foreshortening seems to anticipate Tiepolo, Piazzetta and Goya. Donato Creti made the last room decoration in 1710 collaborating with Ercole Graziani senior who painted the quadratura. The representation of *Alexander Cutting the Gordian Knot* is whirling inside an impressing verticality culminating in a dome. The paintings housed in these rooms come from the Zambeccari collection. The palace is now property of the Council and houses a beautiful painting collection donated by Mons. Francesco Zambeccari, owned by the Italian State.

This building, from the architectural point of view one of the most significant senatorial residences between seventeenth and eighteenth-century, was built starting from 1653. The rooms on the first floor were decorated from 1665 to 1710, by some of the main artists working in Bologna (Domenico Maria Canuti, Domenico Santi called Mengazzino, Giuseppe and Antonio Rolli, Giuseppe Maria Crespi, Donato Creti and Ercole Graziani senior). The pictures hanging to the walls date from the sixteenth- to the eighteenth-century.
artist: Odoardo Pepoli; Ercole Pepoli; Alessandro Pepoli

Architects: Giovanni Battista Albertoni and Giuseppe Antonio Torri; painters: Domenico Maria Canuti (1626-1684), Giuseppe Maria Crespi (1665-1747), Donato Creti (1671-1749), Giuseppe (1652-1727) and Antonio Rolli (1643-1695), Domenico Santi known as Mengazzino (1621-1694)
history: In 1653 Odoardo Pepoli was a freshly appointed Senator. He built a huge residence over former houses on his property to promote the elevated social prestige he and his family had recently gained in town. The work continued until 1665, when Domenico Maria Canuti took up the fresco decoration of the staircase. Fifty years later, in 1710, Odoardo and other members of the family, namely Ercole and Alessandro, commissioned the decorations of five rooms. Around 1710 the architect Giuseppe Antonio Torri built the façade overlooking via Clavature. The second name of the building, “Campogrande”, derives from its last owners.

partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Palazzo Pepoli Campogrande
description: La facciata su via Castiglione si apre al centro in un ricco portale a bugnato. I soffitti dello scalone furono decorati da Domenico Maria Canuti (1665) con due importanti episodi della vita di Taddeo Pepoli entro cornici ovali. Taddeo è mostrato quando divenne signore di Bologna nel 1337 e quando fu nominato vicario apostolico da papa Benedetto  XII nel 1340. Nella sala da ballo, uno degli esempi pià significativi del barocco bolognese, Canuti, in collaborazione con Mengazzino per la quadratura, rappresenta la *Glorificazione di Ercole* (1669-1671) al centro di un cielo illusivamente aperto da una forte luce scenografica. L'occhio del visitatore è attratto dalla tensione dinamica delle figure che si muovono verso l'alto e dall'architettura illusionistica. Nella stanza successiva i fratelli Rolli dipinsero *Il Trionfo dell'Aristocrazia Bolognese,*  mostrando il gemellaggio tra Bologna e Venezia (1686). Nelle stanze successive il pittore anticlassicista Giuseppe Maria Crespi dipinse, tra il 1699 e il 1700, la *Stanza delle Quattro Stagioni* e quella dell'*Olimpo*. In quest'ultima stanza le figure stanno in piedi direttamente sull'incorniciatura del soffitto, senza l'utilizzo di una prospettiva illusionistica. I begli scorci sembrano anticipare Tiepolo, Piazzetta e Goya. Donato Creti decorò l'ultima stanza nel 1710 in collaborazione con Ercole Graziani senior che dipinse la quadratura. La rappresentazione di *Alessandro che taglia il nodo gordiano* si attorciglia in una stupefacente verticalità culminante in una cupola. Oggi il palazzo appartiene al Comune e ospita una bella collezione di dipinti donati da  mons. Francesco Zambeccari e di proprietà dello Stato Italiano.

Questo edificio, dal punto di vista architettonico, è uno dei più importanti palazzi senatori costruiti tra il XVII e il XVIII secolo. Le stanze del primo piano furono decorate, tra il 1665 e il 1710, da alcuni degli artisti principali attivi a Bologna (Domenico Maria Canuti, Domenico Santi detto il Mengazzino, Giuseppe e Antonio Rolli, Giuseppe Maria Crespi, Donato Creti e Ercole Graziani senior). I dipinti appesi alle pareti risalgono ai secoli XVI-XVIII.
artist: Odoardo Pepoli; Ercole Pepoli; Alessandro Pepoli
Giovanni Battista Albertoni e Giuseppe Antonio Torri (architetti); Domenico Maria Canuti, Giuseppe Maria Crespi, Donato Creti, Giuseppe e Antonio Rolli (pittori)
history: Odoardo Pepoli, fatto senatore nel 1653, costruì una immensa residenza su case di sua proprietà, per esibire il prestigio sociale che lui e la sua famiglia avevano recentemente conquistato in città. I lavori proseguirono nel 1665, quando Domenico Maria Canuti iniziò la decorazione ad affresco dello scalone. Cinquanta anni dopo, nel 1710, Odoardo e altri membri della famiglia, in particolare Ercole e Alessandro, commissionarono le decorazioni di cinque stanze. Attorno al  1710 l'architetto Giuseppe Antonio Torri costruì la facciata che affaccia su via Clavature. Il  secondo nome dell'edificio, “Campogrande”, deriva dai suoi ultimi proprietari.
keywords: Architettura residenziale; Affresco; Collezione Zambeccari; Domenico Maria Canuti; Domenico Santi detto Mengazzino; Giuseppe e Antonio Rolli; Giuseppe Maria Crespi; Donato Creti; Ercole Graziani senior; Giovanni Battista Albertoni; Giuseppe Antonio Torri; Taddeo Pepoli; Odoardo Pepoli; Ercole Pepoli; Alessandro Pepoli; Taddeo Pepoli; Benedetto XII; Sala da Ballo; Venezia; Quattro Stagioni; *Ercole; Scalone monumentale*; decorazione figurata; Autocelebrazione dell'aristocrazia; Gonfaloniere.

ar.name: منبر.
description:
يتكون هذا المنبر المتحرك من ثماني درجات، مدعومة بسطوح داخلية عمودية. تنتهي هذه الأخيرة بزخارف تتكون من قويسات جانبية كان يجمعها درابزين. زين المنبر في أجزائه الداخلية والخارجية، ووظف فيه كل الرصيد الزخرفي الأندلسي المعروف خلال تلك الفترة، سواء تعلق الأمر بالأشكال النباتية والزهرية والهندسية والكتابية. أحيطت الجوانب والمقعد بنقائش كتابية بأحرف كوفية (نصوص قرآنية وعبارات دينية وثلاث نصوص عن تأسيس المنبر). كتبت الحروف بشكل بارز، وهي منقوشة أو مرصعة. وجرى على الجوانب استخدام التطعيم والترصيعات الذهبية والعاجية بالنسبة لزخارف التشبيكات الهندسية وللعناصر الزخرفية الزهرية التي اتخذت شكل شجرات الحياة المتوجة بقويسات تزين المقعد وواجهات الدرجات.  
وجرى نحت وترصيع اللوحات الصغيرة المضلعة الخشبية ذات الأشكال المتنوعة والتي كانت تملأ عيون التشبيكات الهندسية، بعناصر نباتية وزهرية برقة ودقة كبيرتين تذكران بعمل العلب العاجية الأموية، بل فاقتها تماماً. يضاف إلى هذه النحتيات والترصيعات، استغلال ألوان وتدرجات الخشب الثمين، مما جعل من هذا الأثاث الديني تحفة فنية فريدة من نوعها. وتبين واحدة من النقائش الكتابية أن أمير المسلمين، علي بن يوسف، قد أوصى بهذا المنبر لورشة في قرطبة في عام 532 هجري/1137 ميلادي لصالح جامع مراكش الكبير. وقد قام الخليفة عبد المومن الموحدي الذي دك جامع علي بن يوسف في عام 542 هجري/1147 ميلادي بالمحافظة على المنبر حيث وضعه في مسجده، جامع الكتبية الأولى، ثم نقله إلى الثاني، أي جامع الكتبية الحالي، حيث بقي مستخدماً حتى عام 1950.

صنع هذا المنبر في قرطبة من أجل المسجد الكبير لعلي ابن يوسف في مراكش. وقد حوفظ عليه، وجرى وضعه من طرف عبد المومن في مسجده، الكتبية. الصنعة ناعمة ومضبوطة ودقيقة، وتجعل من هذا الأثاث المنبر الوحيد الذي وصلنا من تلك الفترة، وهو تحفة فريدة من نوعها.
keywords: قطعة دينية طقوسية؛ أثاث؛ زخرفة هندسية؛ زخرفة زهرية؛ كتابات زخرفية؛ منبر؛ ترصيعات خشبية، تذهيب.
materials: أنواع من أخشاب متنوعة (الأرز، الأكاسيا، شمشاد، عناب) وعظم طبيعي ومطلي باللون الأخضر، وعاجيات (منحوتة ومنقوشة ومخرمة، ومجمعة ومرصعة ومذهبة).

en.name: *Minbar*.
description: This *minbar* is a mobile pulpit with eight steps supported by vertical walls ending with lateral arcatures linked by a ramp. Both the internal and external sides are decorated. The entire Andalusian decorative repertoire – vegetal, floral, geometric and epigraphic – has been employed. The sides and the back are framed with *kufic* inscriptions (Qur'anic text, pious formulas and three foundation texts). The characters are embossed, sculpted or inlaid. Marquetry and bone and ivory inlay have been used on the sides for chequered geometrical knotwork and the floral designs, in the shape of trees of life, crowned by arcatures that decorate the back and the risers. The variously shaped small polygonal wooden panels that fill the interstices of the geometrical knotwork are sculpted and carved with floral and vegetal motifs with an outstanding level of delicacy and precision that is reminiscent of and even surpasses the work on Umayyad ivory boxes. In addition to the sculptures and carving, the palette of colours and shades of the valuable woods make this liturgical object a masterpiece of the genre. One of the inscriptions says that 'Ali ibn Yusuf commissioned it from a workshop in Córdoba in AH 532 / AD 1137 for the Great Mosque of Marrakesh. The Almohad 'Abd al-Mu'min spared the *minbar* when he razed 'Ali's mosque in AH 542 / AD 1147. He put it in his mosque, the original Kutubiya and then transferred it to his second, current Kutubiya, where it was used until the 1950s.

Made in Córdoba for the Great Mosque of 'Ali ibn Yusuf in Marrakesh, it was spared by the Abbasid 'Abd al-Mu'min and placed in his mosque, the Kutubiya. The meticulous, precise and subtle crafting of this item make it the only *minbar* to have survived to our times, a masterpiece of its type.
artist: Workshop in Córdoba and the craftsman Aziz.
keywords: Liturgical object; geometric decoration; floral decoration; epigraphic decoration; mosque interior decoration
materials: Different woods (cedar, acacia, box, jujube), natural bone painted green, ivory (sculpted, carved, openwork, assembled, inlaid and gilded).
tags: Different woods (cedar, acacia, box, jujube), natural bone painted green, ivory (sculpted, carved, openwork, assembled, inlaid and gilded).

es.name: *Minbar*.
description:
Este *minbar* es un púlpito móvil con 8 escalones sustentado por paredes verticales terminadas en arquerías laterales que se unen en un montante. En su decoración interior y exterior se ha empleado todo el repertorio andalusí de la época: vegetal, floral, geométrico y epigráfico.  
Los lados y la trasera están bordeados con inscripciones cúficas (textos coránicos, fórmulas votivas, tres textos fundacionales). Los caracteres están en relieve, esculpidos o engastados. La marquetería y las incrustaciones de hueso y de marfil se han empleado en los laterales para formar lacería geométrica en cuadros y para los motivos florales en forma de árboles de la vida rematados con arquerías que decoran el respaldo y las tabicas.  
Los pequeños tableros poligonales de madera con diversas formas que cubren los espacios entre los entrelazos geométricos están esculpidos y cincelados con motivos vegetales y florales; la finura y precisión de su ejecución rememoran, e incluso superan, las la de las cajas omeyas de marfil.  
Estos labrados y cinceladuras, junto con la gama de colores y tonos de las valiosas maderas, convierten este mueble litúrgico en una obra de arte en su género. Una de las inscripciones precisa que, en 532/1137, Ali Ibn Yusuf lo mandó fabricar a un taller de Córdoba para la Mezquita Mayor de Marrakech. En 542/1147, cuando el almohade Abd al-Mumin saqueó la mezquita de Ali, conservó este *minbar*, que fue emplazado en su mezquita, la primera Kutubiya, para después ser transferido a la segunda, la actual, donde se utilizó hasta los años 1950.

Fabricado en Córdoba para la Mezquita Mayor de Marrakech de Ali Ibn Yusuf, Abd al-Mumin lo salvó del saqueo y lo colocó en su mezquita, la Kutubiya. La finura, precisión y minuciosidad de una ejecución llena de matices convierten este mueble, único *minbar* conservado de la época, en una obra de arte en su género.
dates: 532 de la Hégira/1137 d. C. (inicio de fabricación).
artist: Un artesano llamado Aziz en un taller de Córdoba..
materials: Esencias de maderas (cedro, acacia, boj, azufaifo), hueso natural pintado de verde, marfiles; esculpido, cincelado, calado, ensamblado, incrustado, dorado.
