en.name: The Combat of Khusraw Parviz and Bahram Chubina (Page from a Manuscript of the Shahnama (Book of Kings))
description: The illustrated page from a manuscript of the Iranian national epic, the Shahnama, depicts a contest between the Sasanian monarch Shah Khusraw Parviz (Khusraw II, r. AD 590–628) and a would-be usurper, Bahram Chubina. The protagonists, who competed for the Iranian throne, are both crowned. Bahram, the superior warrior, advances on foot toward a group of archers directed by Khusraw. This depiction of an epic battle cheekily includes, at the center of the page, a figure who has fallen, leaving his buttocks exposed. The humiliated man perhaps can be understood as representing an out-of-favor courtier, thereby drawing the centuries-old battle into the contemporary world of the manuscript’s creation.
holder: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)
keywords: Manuscript; ink; watercolour; gold; silver; Iran; Safavid; illustration; painting; figural motifs
materials: Ink, opaque watercolor, gold and silver on paper
tags: Ink, opaque watercolor, gold and silver on paper
partner: Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA)

en.name: Staircase
description: Monti designed a so-called “macchina per salire” (machine to  ascend) that transformed the loggia into a theatrical stage, with stuccos by Carlo Nessi. The staircase consist of two symmetrical and opposite flights where the windows are open on illusionistic perspectives.
place: Hall, ground floor, Palazzo Marescotti Brazzetti
partner: Musei Civici d’Arte Antica di Bologna in cooperation with the Province of Bologna

it.name: Scalone monumentale
description: Monti costruì la cosiddetta “macchina per salire” che trasformò la loggia in un palcoscenico teatrale, con stucchi di  Carlo Nessi. Lo scalone consiste in due rampe simmetriche che si fronteggiano, le finestre si aprono su prospettive illusionistiche.
place: Ingresso, piano terreno, Palazzo Marescotti Brazzetti

ar.name: شاهدة تزيينية (قطعة).
description:
قطعة من شاهدة محفورة من جانبيها، شكلها شبه مستطيل، ولونها أبيض صوفي مُزنْجر بالكستنائي الفاتح. تحوي الجهة الداخلية المتبقية منها فتحةً دائرية تشهد على شكل الربط أو التثبيت الذي كان يجمعها بالبنية الأصلية (يبدو أنها تنتمي إلى غطاء صندوق حلي).  
  
يقدم السطحان زخارف محفورة بعناية، ومحددة بإطار دقيق مع بعض التحزيزات على الجانب الأدنى. وتمثل الزخارف على أحد الجوانب نسراً ملكياً يبسط جناحيه، لكنه يقف على الأرض ورأسه يستدير إلى جهة اليسار، وبالجانب الآخر حيوان من فصيلة الأيائل يمسك بفمه عنصراً نباتي الشكل. كما يمثل الشكلان المحاطان بعناصر نباتية واللذان يوحيان بالحركة نحو مركز الصفيحة مشهد صيد، ويرد هذا الموضوع الزخرفي، في قطع أخرى من العاج والخشب والمعدن من نفس الفترة. ونظراً لنوعية الزخارف وللعناصر الممثلة، يمكن أن تشكل القطعة جزءاً من تحفة فنية كمالية، تشبه لحد كبير قطعاً أخرى مصنوعة في قرطبة، وعلى الخصوص في مشاغل خلف.  
  
نوعية الزخارف على السطحين، توحي بأن هذه القطعة كانت تشكل جزءاً من بنية يظهر جانباها للعيان.

يبرزُ أحد جوانب هذه الشاهدة نسرا ملكيا بجناحيه المبسوطين، بينما يمثل الآخر حيوانا من فصيلة الأيائل؛ وهو موضوع زخرفي مشترك مع قطع أخرى من العاج أو من المعدن ترجع إلى نفس الفترة. ومن الممكن أن تكون هذه الشاهدة قد صنعت في ورشة بقرطبة.
dynasty: الفترة الأموية، مرحلة الخلافة، القرن 4 الهجري / القرن 10 الميلادي
keywords: زخارف تصويرية؛ منقولات.

en.name: Ornamental plaque (fragment).
description:
Fragment of an ornamental plate sculpted on both sides. It is sub-rectangular in shape, beige in colour with a light brown patina. The bottom corner has a round hole which suggests the probable manner of attachment to the structure to which it belonged (it was probably part of the lid of a small chest).  
Both sides have detailed sculpted decoration and are bordered by a fine moulding with some incisions on the lower part.  
One side shows a golden eagle with its wings open, but standing on the ground, with its head turned towards the left. The other side shows a deer holding in its mouth a plant motif. Both creatures, surrounded by plant decorations and giving a sense of movement towards the centre of the plate, suggest the theme of hunting. This type of thematic decoration is similar to other pieces in ivory, wood and metal from the same period. Given the type of decoration and the figurative elements, this may have been part of a work of sumptuary art and is very similar to those produced in Córdoba (Spain), specifically in the Halaf workshop.  
The quality of the decoration on both sides suggests that this fragment would have been part of a structure in which both were clearly visible.

One of the sides of this plaque shows a golden eagle with its wings outstretched, while the other depicts a deer. This decoration is common in other ivory, wood and metal items from the same period. The plaque would have been made in a Córdoban workshop.
keywords: figurative decoration; furnishing

es.name: Fragmento de placa ornamental.
description:
Fragmento de placa ornamental esculpida por ambos lados. Tiene forma rectangular y es de color beige con una pátina de castaño claro.  
En el ángulo inferior hay un orificio redondo, que hace pensar en alguna forma de encaje o fijación en la estructura a la que perteneció (posiblemente la tapa de una arqueta).  
Ambas superficies tienen una decoración tallada con minucia y delimitada por una fina moldura con algunas incisiones en la parte inferior.  
Decora uno de los lados un águila real posada en el suelo, con las alas abiertas y la cabeza girada hacia la izquierda; en el otro lado, un cérvido lleva en la boca un elemento fitomórfico. Ambas figuras, envueltas en elementos vegetales y en movimiento hacia el centro de la placa, tienen un patente carácter cinegético.  
Este tipo de temas es común a otras piezas de marfil, madera y metal de la misma época. Atendiendo a su decoración y los elementos representados, la placa pudo formar parte de un objeto de arte suntuario muy semejante a los producidos en Córdoba, especialmente en el taller de Halaf.  
La calidad de la decoración de las dos superficies sugiere que este fragmento era parte de una estructura donde ambos lados se veían y destacaban.

Fragmento de placa de marfil en una de cuyas caras está representada un águila real con las alas abiertas, mientras que en la otra se ve un cérvido. La decoración es común a otras piezas de marfil, madera o metal de la misma época. Seguramente se fabricó en un taller cordobés.
dates: Siglo IV de la Hégira / X d. C.
keywords: Decoración figurativa; mobiliario.
partner: Museo Municipal de Arqueología de Silves

fr.name: Stèle ornementale (fragment).
description:
Fragment de stèle gravée de chaque côté, de forme sous-rectangulaire, de couleur beige patinée de châtain clair. Le coin inférieur préservé présente un orifice circulaire qui suggère la probable forme d'assemblage ou de fixation sur la structure d'origine (appartenant sans doute au couvercle d'un coffret).  
Les deux surfaces présentent un décor gravé avec minutie et délimité par un fin cadre avec quelques incisions sur la partie inférieure.  
Le décor montre sur un des côtés un aigle royal aux ailes éployées mais appuyé sur le sol, la tête tournée sur sa gauche, et de l'autre côté un cervidé qui maintient dans sa gueule un élément phytomorphe. Les deux figures, entourées d'éléments végétaux et suggérant un mouvement vers le centre de la plaque présentent un caractère cynégétique. Cette thématique ornementale est commune à d'autres pièces d'ivoire, de bois ou de métal de la même époque. Vu le type de décor et des éléments représentés, le fragment pourrait appartenir à un objet d'art somptuaire très similaire à ceux produits à Cordoue, notamment dans les ateliers de Khalaf.  
La qualité du décor des deux surfaces suggère que ce fragment faisait partie d'une structure dont les deux côtés pouvaient être vus.

Un des côtés de ce fragment de stèle montre un aigle royal aux ailes éployées, alors que l'autre représente un cervidé. Cette thématique ornementale est commune à d'autres pièces d'ivoire, de bois ou de métal de la même époque. Cette stèle a dû être fabriquée dans un atelier de Cordoue.
dates: IVe siècle de l’Hégire (Xe siècle J.-C.)
keywords: décoration figurative ; mobilier

pt.name: Placa ornamental (fragmento).
description:
Fragmento de placa ornamental gravada de ambos os lados. Tem forma sub-rectangular de cor beje com patine de cor castanha clara.  
  
O canto inferior preservado apresenta um orifício redondo que sugere a provável forma de encaixe ou fixação na estrutura à qual pertenceu (provavelmente fazendo parte da tampa de uma arqueta).  
  
Ambas as superfícies têm a decoração gravada com minúcia e delimitada por fina moldura com algumas incisões na parte inferior.  
  
A decoração mostra de um dos lados uma águia real com as suas asas abertas, mas assente no chão, com cabeça flectida para a esquerda e do outro um cervídeo que sustenta na boca um elemento fitomórfico. Ambas as figuras, envolvidas em elementos vegetalistas e indiciando movimentos em direcção ao centro da placa, têm grande carácter cinegético. Este tipo de decoração temático é comum a outras peças de marfim, de madeira e de metal da mesma época. Dado o tipo de decoração e elementos representados, poderá ter feito parte de um objecto de arte sumptuária muito semelhante aos produzidos em Córdova nomeadamente na oficina de Halaf.  
  
A qualidade da decoração das duas superfícies sugere que este fragmento integraria uma estrutura onde ambas eram destacadas e visualizadas.

Fragmento de uma placa em marfim. Numa das faces está representada uma águia real de asas abertas, ao passo que na outra se vê um um cervídeo. A decoração é comum a outras peças de marfim, de madeira e de metal da mesma época (séc. IV H./séc. X d.C.). A placa deve ter origem numa oficina cordovesa.
holder: Museu Municipal de Arqueologia de Silves.
dates: Séc. IV AH / Séc. X AD.
keywords: placa; Silves; omíadas; decoração figurativa; mobiliário; marfim esculpido; relevo
partner: Museu Municipal de Arqueologia de Silves

en.name: Dar al-Longu
description:
The traditional Gafsian house, like everywhere else in Tunisia, has a central courtyard. It is accessed via a simple or elbow-shaped hallway. The kitchen, the cellar-vaults which in Gafsa are called *makhzen*, and the bedrooms all open out onto the courtyard, which has no porticoes. The bedrooms are long and narrow, as they are adapted to the length of palm-tree wood and to cross vaults. Each room is furnished at both ends with two masoned rostrums which serve as beds; one surmounts a storeroom full of provisions, the other, which is higher, surmounts a smaller chamber.  
It was essentially under the Husaynites, i.e. in the 12th/18th century, with its administrative and military elite, and often with the help of Sfaxian Master-Masons like Mohamed Kammun, that the Gafsian house adopted the look of a bourgeois residence, imitating those of Tunis and of the large coastal towns. T-shaped rooms, courtyards with porticoes, painted ceilings and *kadhal* frames are all embraced.  
Houses such as Dar al-Smawi and Dar al-Qarwi are exact copies of Sfaxian houses, right down to the last detail.  
Dar al-Longu is an intermediary house. The government, having bought it from its previous owners, the Bakirs, gave it to its Gafsa representative, the Chief Ahmed Ibn Hassan Ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Longu. His family, who were of Turkish origin, had set up and secured the town’s military and government functions. The first owners of Dar al-Longu had sufficient means to allow themselves to have a relatively sumptuous house, which they chose to place right at the centre of town, close to the Roman pools. A portico endowed with benches, onto which a large room opens, which perhaps once served as stables, leads to a elbow-shaped hallway. The kitchen and outhouses, as well as a reception room and three *qbu* rooms flanked by smaller ones, *maqsura*, all covered in intersecting vaults, are positioned all around the courtyard. Each room surmounts a cellar, which has its own entrance situated inside the courtyard, and acts as a storeroom, *makhzen*. Stairs placed in the hallway lead to the first floor. In terms of typical Gafsian architecture, Dar al-Longu has retained the courtyard without a portico, the intersecting vaults, and the cellars. From Tunis and the coastal towns, it has borrowed the rooms with *qbu*s and the painted ceilings. The latter were to be found on the first floor and imitate the Italian-style painted ceilings of Tunis, and thus the house distinguishes itself from Dar al-Smawi whose ceilings, imitating those of Sfax, are of Andalusian production. Mohamed Kammun, who, according to the inscription fixed onto the vault of one of the rooms, oversaw the building works in 1233/1818, had to abandon some architectural dispositions from his hometown in order to satisfy the landowners’ attachment to certain forms of traditional Gafsian architecture, and also had to accommodate their weakness for the architecture of Tunis, the thought of which titillated their bourgeois pride. The oratory, *masjed*, integrated into the main part of the house whilst opening out onto the street, was perhaps conceived with this thought in mind.  
It seems that Ahmad al-Longu’s contribution is limited to purely decorative aspects.

es.name: Dar el-Longu
description:
La casa tradicional de Gafsa tiene un patio central, característica general en Túnez. Un vestíbulo simple y acodado permite acceder a ella. Sobre el patio, desprovisto de pórticos, se abren la cocina, los sótanos (en Gafsa llamados *majzen*) y los dormitorios. Éstos son largos y estrechos, y se adaptan así al ancho de la madera de palmera y a las bóvedas cruzadas. Cada habitación está equipada en sus extremidades por dos estrados de albañilería, uno de los cuales corona una despensa de provisiones y el otro, más alto, una pequeña habitación.  
Fue esencialmente bajo los husseiníes, es decir en el siglo XII/XVIII, con la instalación de una elite administrativa y militar, y frecuentemente con la ayuda de los arquitectos de Sfax, que la casa de Gafsa pudo tomar la forma típica de las casas burguesas, imitando las de Túnez y las grandes ciudades costeras. Habitaciones en forma de T, patio con pórticos, techos pintados, marcos en *kadhal* empiezan a ser adoptados en ellas. Las casas como la Dar el-Smawi y Dar el-Qarwi calcan, incluso en los detalles, las casas de Sfax.  
Dar el-Longu es una casa de tamaño mediano. El gobierno, que la compró a sus antiguos propietarios, los Bakir, la cedió en 1881 a su representante en Gafsa, el caíd Ahmad ibn Hassan ibn Abd el-Rahman el-Longu. Su familia, de origen turco, se había asegurado las funciones militares y de gobierno en esta ciudad. Los primeros propietarios de Dar el-Longu tenían suficientes medios para permitirse una casa relativamente suntuosa, cuyo emplazamiento en medio de la ciudad habían elegido. Un pórtico equipado con banquetas se abre hacia una gran sala, que había servido quizá como establo y que da acceso a un vestíbulo en zigzag. Alrededor de todo el patio se ordenan la cocina y sus dependencias, una pieza de recepción y tres habitaciones en *qbu*. Éstas están, a su vez, flanqueadas por pequeñas habitaciones cubiertas por bóvedas cruzadas. Cada habitación tiene una entrada independiente, situada en el patio. Las escaleras del vestíbulo llevan al primer piso.  
De la arquitectura típicamente gafsí, Dar el-Longu ha tomado el patio desprovisto de pórticos, las bóvedas cruzadas y los sótanos; de Túnez y las ciudades costeras, ha tomado las habitaciones *qbu* y los techos pintados. Éstos se encuentran en el primer piso e imitan los techos pintados italianizantes de Túnez, apartándose así de Dar el-Smawi, cuyos techos imitan los de Sfax, de factura andalusí. Mohamed Kammun, que supervisó los trabajos en 1233/1818 según la inspiración fijada sobre la bóveda de una de las habitaciones, debió renunciar a algunas disposiciones arquitectónicas de su ciudad para satisfacer el apego de los propietarios a ciertas formas de la arquitectura tradicional de Gafsa, aunque unida a una cierta dependencia de la arquitectura de Túnez, cuyo reflejo impresiona el orgullo de los burgueses. Quizá es en esta perspectiva en la que se sitúa el oratorio (*masyad*), integrado en el conjunto de esta casa, aunque abierto sobre la calle.  
Parece que la aportación de Ahmad el-Longu se hubiera limitado a aspectos puramente decorativos.

fr.name: Dar el-Longu
description:
La maison traditionnelle de Gafsa, comme partout ailleurs en Tunisie, est à cour centrale. Un vestibule simple ou coudé permet d’y accéder. Sur la cour, dépourvue de portiques, ouvrent la cuisine, les caves appelées *makhzen* à Gafsa, et les chambres d’habitation. Celles-ci, longues et étroites, sont ainsi adaptées à la longueur du bois de palmier et aux voûtes croisées. Chaque chambre est équipée à ses extrémités de deux estrades maçonnées servant de lit, surmontant, l’une une resserre à provisions, l’autre, la plus haute, une chambrette.  
C’est essentiellement sous les Husseinites c’est-à-dire au XIIe/XVIIIe, avec l’élite administrative et militaire et souvent à l’aide de maîtres maçons sfaxiens, dont Mohamed Kammoun, que la maison gafsienne va prendre l’allure d’une demeure bourgeoise, imitant celles de Tunis et des grandes villes côtières. Chambres en T, cours à portiques, plafonds peints, encadrements en *kadhal* y sont adoptés.  
Des maisons comme Dar el-Smaoui et Dar el-Qaroui calquent, même dans les détails, les maisons sfaxiennes.  
Dar el-Longu est une maison intermédiaire. Le gouvernement, l’ayant achetée à ses anciens propriétaires, les Bakir, l’a cédée en 1881 à son représentant à Gafsa, le caïd Ahmed Ben Hassan Ben Abderrahman el-Longu. Sa famille, d’origine turque, avait assuré des fonctions militaires et caïdales dans cette ville. Les premiers propriétaires de Dar el-Longu avaient suffisamment de moyens pour se permettre une maison relativement somptueuse dont ils ont choisi l’emplacement au coeur de la ville, à proximité des piscines romaines. Un portique équipé de banquettes, sur lequel ouvre une grande salle, ayant peut-être servi d’écuries, donne accès à un vestibule en chicane. Tout autour de la cour s’ordonnent la cuisine et des dépendances, une pièce de réception et trois chambres à *qbou*, flanquées de chambrettes, *maqsoura*, toutes couvertes en voûtes croisées. Chaque chambre surmonte une cave à entrée indépendante située dans la cour, jouant le rôle de resserre, *makhzen*. Des escaliers placés dans le vestibule mènent à l’étage. De l’architecture typiquement gafsienne, Dar el-Longu a retenu le patio dépourvu de portiques, les voûtes croisées, et les caves. À Tunis et aux villes côtières, elle a emprunté les chambres à *qbou* et les plafonds peints. Ceux-ci se trouvaient à l’étage et imitent les plafonds peints italianisants de Tunis, s’écartant ainsi de Dar Smaoui dont les plafonds, imitant ceux de Sfax, sont de facture andalouse. Mohamed Kammoun, qui a assuré les travaux en 1233/1818 selon l’inscription fixée sur la voûte de l’une des chambres, a dû renoncer à certaines dispositions architecturales de sa ville pour satisfaire l’attachement des propriétaires à certaines formes de l’architecture traditionnelle de Gafsa et aussi un certain penchant pour l’architecture tunisoise, dont le miroitement chatouillait leur orgueil bourgeois. C’est peut-être dans cette perspective que se place l’oratoire, *masjed*, intégré à la masse de cette maison, mais ouvrant sur la rue.  
Il semble que l’apport d’Ahmad el-Longu se soit limité à des aspects purement décoratifs.

en.name: Panoramic view of the church interior
description: Commissioned by the wealthy merchant, Manuel Álvares Azeitado, this is the first *scarto* known in Portugal, forming part of the International Baroque program. The panoramic view of the interior shows the *trompe l'œil* architecture of the barrel-vaulted ceiling, which appears to be a continuation of the walls. The *trompe l'œil,* centred towards one focal point, creates the illusion of deep recession, heavenly sphere or even an open sky.
artist: Woodcarvers: João de Touro Freitas, António de Oliveira (1675–n.d.), Manuel João da Fonseca and Francisco da Silva (1684-n.d.); painters: António de Oliveira Bernardes (1662–1732) and Pedro Figueira; azulejos painters: Gabriel del Barco (1649–c.1703)
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: Vista panorâmica do interior da igreja
description: Resultante de uma encomenda do rico mercador Manuel Álvares Azeitado, este é o primeiro *scarto* conhecido em Portugal que está associado a um programa do Barroco Internacional. A vista panorâmica do interior evidencia a arquitectura em *trompe l’œil* da abóbada que, centrada num ponto focal, cria a ilusão de uma abertura em direcção ao céu.
artist: Entalhadores: João de Touro Freitas, António de Oliveira (1675–n.d.), Manuel João da Fonseca e Francisco da Silva (1684-n.d.); pintores: António de Oliveira Bernardes (1662–1732) e Pedro Figueira; pintores de azulejos: Gabriel del Barco (1649–c.1703)

en.name: *Bei der Kupplerin (The Procuress)*
description: A large area of this painting is taken up by a carpet. Owing to the clearly recognisable pattern, it is possible to identify this carpet as coming from Uşak, a town in western Anatolia with a long and rich history of carpet production. On account of the dark blue ground and the red, onion-shaped central medallion, it is possible to date this carpet to the first half of the 16th century. Vermeer presents a seemingly light-hearted, quiet scene in which the objectionable aspect of the situation is not immediately apparent. Nevertheless, he leaves us in no doubt that this is a scene of procuration: the fashionably dressed suitor is paying money while with his left hand he touches the breast of the young woman.
holder: Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister (Old Masters Picture Gallery), Dresden State Art Collections
keywords: Painting; Carpet; Genre painting
partner: Dresden State Art Collections, Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister (Old Masters Picture Gallery)

en.name: The Austrian ship on which Emperor Franz Joseph participated at the opening ceremony of the Suez Canal in 1869
short_description: Emperor Franz Joseph visited the Suez Canal on board the Austrian ship, *Elisabeth*. He reached the Egyptian port of Ismilia on 14 Nov 1869 and stayed in Egypt until the 26 Nov 1869. During this trip, he also visited Cairo and Alexandria.
holder: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History
partner: Austrian Military Museum / Institute of Military History

en.name: Untitled
description:
Sculpture of two blocks, designed for assembly and composed of horizontally-overlapping glass sheets. A signature of “TE85” appears on the upper part of the piece. Torres Esteban’s work is often characterized by this use of green, cut and cold-glued industrial plate glass. The form of the piece is also typical of the artist’s style. Here we see an interest in volume, with luminescent and kinetic effects that show the influence of Eusebio Sempere.  
  
The work of Joaquín Torres Esteban is associated with the Studio Glass Movement, which originated in the United States and spread internationally. Torres Esteban is one of the pioneers of laminated glass sculpture in Spain. Throughout his glassmaking career, he participated in numerous international events and organized VICOINTER’83, an international contemporary glass exhibition in Valencia.  
  
In 1986, the National Museum of Decorative Arts dedicated a monographic exhibition to Torres Esteban, after which the artist donated this piece.
keywords: Laminated glass; sculpture; Studio Glass Movement

es.name: Sin título
description:
Escultura realizada mediante láminas de vidrio superpuestas en sentido horizontal que componen dos bloques diseñados para ser ensamblados. Presenta la firma “TE85” en la parte superior. El uso de planchas de vidrio industrial de color verde, cortadas y pegadas en frío, es habitual en las obras de Torres Esteban. Desde el punto de vista formal, la pieza también puede considerarse característica de la producción de este autor. En ella se aprecia un interés por el volumen y los efectos lumínicos y cinéticos que manifiesta la influencia de Eusebio Sempere.  
  
La obra de Joaquín Torres Esteban se inscribe en la órbita del “Studio Glass Movement”, originado en Estados Unidos y con amplia difusión internacional. Torres Esteban es uno de los pioneros de la escultura en vidrio laminado en España. Participó en numerosos encuentros internacionales a lo largo de su trayectoria como vidriero y se encargó de organizar la muestra de vidrio contemporáneo internacional VICOINTER’83, celebrada en Valencia.  
  
En 1986 el Museo Nacional de Artes Decorativas dedicó una exposición monográfica a Torres Esteban, tras la cual el artista donó esta obra.
keywords: Vidrio laminado; escultura; Studio Glass Movement
materials: Vidrio laminado; cortado, pulido, pegado en frío

en.name: Jug and basin set (*aftafa-layan*)
description:
The *aftafa-layan* is a jug and basin set with a separating lid used for washing, usually made of copper and richly decorated. It was widely distributed in the Near and Middle East and used during large feasts. The lid was used as an esthetic cover for the basin. It is decorated with inscriptions and floral elements. One or two lines from Hafez’s ghazal poem were written on the upper border of *aftafa*. The edge borders of the *layan* are decorated with inscriptions. The inscription in the cartouches on the border read as follows:  
"It's time to enjoy the flowers and life.  
Sagi! Give the water of life.  
In the meadow, wine and jam \[bowl\] are pleasant.  
Along with crimson tulips.  
Wasted youth is a pity, it can't be considered a life."
keywords: jug; basin; copper; aftafa-layan; tableware; Azerbaijan

en.name: Nave
description: An oval-shaped nave with four altars.
partner: Institute for the Administration of Architectural and Archaeological Heritage -  IGESPAR

pt.name: Nave
description: Nave ovalada, de grandes dimensões, com paredes encurvadas e quatro altares de pedra.

en.name: Noria at the Mohammed VI Museum for the Civilisation of Water in Morocco
dates: This reconstructed noria is displayed in the museum to highlight traditional urban water engineering. As a functional exhibit, it demonstrates historical methods of lifting and distributing water and engages visitors directly. In doing so, it illustrates how water infrastructure has shaped urban life while connecting engineering, public education and cultural heritage in a modern museum context.
partner: Mohammed VI Museum for the Civilisation of Water in Morocco

en.name: Villa Raïs Hamidou (villa des Arcades)
names: Villa Raïs Hamidou (Villa of the Arcades)
description:
The villa’s name derives from the arcades that support the private aqueduct that once provided water to the gardens and the villa, and that we can still see next to the house. It also evokes the raïs Hamidou, a wealthy privateer and owner of the house, who revitalised the local corsair (pirate) trade with several lucrative seizures early in the 13th / 19th century. At the time it was customary to name houses for their owners.  
  
The Villa of the Arcades is located halfway down the hill, overlooking the sea and facing the medina. Its luxury testifies to the social status that privateers achieved from piracy, and to their personal wealth and prestige in Algerian society, which also benefited from it.  
  
When compared to paintings of the villa from around 1830, it seems to be reduced in size – building elements have disappeared.  
  
The house is preceded by a courtyard with a fountain immediately in front, in an atypical position. This vestibule area defines a porch in the form of a portico under a pointed horseshoe arch supported by groups of three narrow twisted columns at each corner. This portico corresponds to the protruding *qbou*, or anteroom, on the floor above. These houses of the Fahs often have imposing porches that look like square rooms. They lack this quality in the medina because of limited space. This porch lends the entrance an imposing quality, perhaps to distinguish it from houses in the medina whose entrances align with the walls of the street.  
  
The rest of the layout is traditional. We even find that the *sqifa*, or entryway, is rendered unnecessary by the garden that serves as a buffer in these country houses. The patio, of beautiful dimensions, has three pointed horseshoe arches supported by a fine marble colonnade.  
  
The upstairs has a double portico with columns on one side that probably served as a hall of honour to reflect the social rank of its owner. The galleries are lined with richly carved railings. The shafts of the white marble columns are hexagonal in the lower part and twisted at the top. The walls are decorated with colourful ceramic tiles.  
  
We have here a fine example of a residence identical to those in the medina, with the exception of the monumental entrance characteristic of these summer residences, or private palaces. The palaces of Achir and those of the Qal‘at of Bani Hammad also had these anteroom entryways.  
  
One can easily imagine the raïs Hamidou watching his ships entering or leaving the Bay of al-Djazair (Algiers) from the vantage point of his now-vanished terrace.

fr.name: Villa Raïs Hamidou (villa des Arcades)
description:
Son nom lui vient des arcades supportant l’aqueduc privé qui alimentait jadis les jardins et la villa et que l’on voit encore sur le côté de la maison. Il évoque aussi le raïs Hamidou, riche corsaire et propriétaire de la maison, qui redonna son intensité à la Course par quelques belles prises au début du XIIIe/XIXe siècle. Il était habituel à l’époque d’appeler les maisons par le nom de leurs propriétaires.  
La villa des Arcades est située à mi-pente sur la colline dominant la mer et face à la médina. Sa richesse témoigne du statut social atteint par les corsaires grâce à leur investissement dans la Course et aux bénéfices substantiels qu’ils en retiraient en termes de richesse personnelle et de prestige aux yeux de la société algéroise, qui en bénéficiait par ricochet.  
D’après les peintures qui la représentent vers 1830, elle semble avoir perdu en surface : des corps de bâtiment ont disparu.  
La maison est précédée d’une cour abritant une vasque précédant immédiatement ce qui fait sa particularité, à savoir son entrée en avant-corps. Cette dernière délimite une avancée formant un portique à un arc brisé outrepassé supporté par des trios de fines colonnes torsadées placés aux quatre angles. Ce portique correspond, au rez-de-chaussée, à l’avancée, relativement importante, du *qbou* du premier étage. Ces maisons du Fahs présentent en effet des renfoncements aux dimensions imposantes, leur donnant l’allure de véritables pièces carrées qu’elles ne peuvent avoir dans la médina en raison du manque d’espace. Cet avantcorps donne à l’entrée de la maison un caractère solennel, peut-être symbolique, la distinguant en cela des maisons de la médina dont les entrées sont plaquées aux murs de la rue.  
Le reste de l’agencement est traditionnel. On y trouve même la *sqifa*, ou entrée en chicane, pourtant rendue inutile par le jardin qui fait office de tampon dans ces maisons de campagne. Le patio, de belles dimensions, présente trois arcs brisés outrepassés soutenus par une fine colonnade de marbre.  
Le premier étage abrite, sur un des côtés, un double portique à colonnes, tenant lieu de salon d’honneur, sûrement en relation avec le rang social de son propriétaire. Les galeries sont bordées de balustrades richement sculptées. Les fûts des colonnes en marbre blanc sont hexagonaux en partie basse et torsadés en haut. Les murs sont décorés de parements de céramiques colorées.  
Nous avons là un bel exemple de demeure identique à celle de la médina, à l’exception de l’entrée monumentale, caractéristique de ces résidences d’été que l’on peut qualifier de palais privés. Il est à noter que les palais d’Achir comme ceux de la Qalaa des Beni Hammad présentaient aussi ces entrées en avant-corps.  
On imagine aisément le raïs Hamidou surveillant, depuis le belvédère de sa terrasse, disparu aujourd’hui, mais que l’on voit sur les peintures anciennes, l’activité de ses navires entrant ou sortant de la rade d’al-Djazaïr.

en.name: Cisitalia 202 SMM Nuvolari
description: The model on display is the second of two cars that arrived at the Museum from the exchange with Brian Brunkhorst in 1995. Brunkhorst bought it in 1988 from a Ferrari dealer, and it came from South America. It had belonged to the same owner from 1948 to 1980, The previous owner, notary Federico Andreini from Buenos Aires, kept this car from 1948 to 1980 and raced with several times in Argentina. Andreini was a member of the Argentine CAS (Club de Automóviles Sport), a club set up just after the Second World War and dedicated to racing sports cars in Argentina. The four-cylinder in-line engine, derived from the Fiat 1100, displaces 1,089 cubic centimetres to provide 60–65 horsepower at 5,500 revolutions per minute; with it, this model can attain speeds of up to 180km/h.
keywords: Historic Car; Engine; Mille Miglia
materials: Steel, copper, leather, paint; assembling, casting, forging, welding, modelling, painting
tags: assembling, casting, forging, welding, modelling, painting

en.name: Museum of Sacred Art
description:
"The Museum of Sacred Art contains some highly important pieces of Manueline gold- and silverwork, almost all from a posthumous donation made by D. Manuel I to Funchal Cathedral of 21 religious objects in silver. The donation was made in 1528, seven years after the death of D. Manuel I.  
The collection includes a huge processional cross, the largest of its kind in Portugal and belonging to yet another donation from the king.  
As is the case with the famous Monstrance of Belém, now housed in the National Museum of Ancient Art in Lisbon, the king’s device, or the armillary sphere, is very clearly highlighted, so that the donor’s memory is not forgotten.  
Another of the king’s offerings is a small but lovely *porta-pax*, undeniably one of the most remarkable pieces of its kind amongst the whole of Portuguese goldand silverware. The *porta-pax* reproduces a Renaissance portico supported by Corinthian columns, with the arms of Portugal flanked by two winged figures under the entablature. The freestanding, albeit very badly damaged figure of the Eternal Father crowns the composition, finished on both sides by fantastic creatures. In the centre is a chased relief of the *Adoration of the Magi*, and five precious stones (hyacinths) complete the decoration.  
Another unique although small Manueline image is that of Our Lady, originating from the Fraternity of Our Lady of the Rosary from Funchal Cathedral and executed by a workshop in Lisbon. It represents a freestanding figure of the Virgin, her hands in an attitude of prayer and her face raised to Heaven. Both the face and hands have been painted. The modelling of her costume, the almost musical rhythm of the pleats in her mantle, resting on the base of the image shaped like a rose, all help to make this a unique piece amongst Manueline silver sculptures.  
No less remarkable is the Manueline chalice also from Funchal Cathedral, which still retains its original highly decorative enamel on the stem and knot.  
The collection of paintings, which come from various religious institutions on the Island, again underlines the importance of Flemish painting in Manueline times. With few exceptions, the collection is made up of large panels indicating that they were mostly specific commissions and not bought on the open market. In fact, the importation of painting was largely due to royal donations and private commissions by the local nobility; not forgetting that ample funds were available from sugar production and the flourishing trade with Flanders. Whilst the existing documentation provides some information about the private commissioning of works by the powerful land-owning nobility, namely through clauses contained in wills, the paintings themselves also testify to the direct involvement of this social sector.  
The magnificent triptych of the *Descent from the Cross*, attributed to the Flemish painter Gérard David and his collaborators, is an example of this patronage. The triptych depicts Portraits of the donors accompanied by St James the Greater, on the left-hand side, and St Bernardino on the right. In another triptych of St James the Less and St Philip, attributed to Pieter Coeck van Aeist, the third and fourth patrons of Funchal, Simão Gonçalves da Câmara and his son João, are depicted on the outer panels with their wives and families.  
The importance of each picture in this fascinating museum means that it is not possible to pinpoint any single piece from it for particular observation, but the triptych of *St Peter, St Paul and St Andrew*, attributed to the painter Joos van Cleve, enables the visitor to see the expressive strategies and resources used by the so-called Flemish “primitives”. In the foreground, the apostles in opulently coloured, flowing robes are outlined against an extraordinary landscape, with the pleats and folds effectively suggesting anatomical volume. The landscape is treated with impressive tactile realism, gradually changing colour from browns to blues, as the figurative elements lose definition and scale. With a remarkable ability to handle perspective, the painter suggests enormous spatial depth, which he uses in the central panel to represent St Peter on the Sea of Galilee.  
The landscapes and the objects depicted in these paintings, used as scenarios or accessories to religious themes, later acquired an autonomous value in new types of paintings, specifically still-life and landscape painting. These apparently profane secondary objects and figures of mere decorative value had a symbolic significance that needs to be decoded. On the reverse of the side panels, and only visible when the triptych is closed are paintings of *The Virgin* and the *Angel of the Annunciation*.  
The importance of Madeira during the Manueline period is also reflected in sculptures that ranges from miniature pieces made in specialised workshops in Malines, to commissions from workshops in the Antwerp area, and which include complete retables, such as the *Reis Magos* (Three Kings) from a chapel of the Estreito da Calheta. The Museum has a number of high quality paintings most notably those that represent the *Virgin and Child* from places such as the Parish Churches of Ponta do Sol, Machico or Ribeira Brava. There are also some exemplary expressive examples of *The Deposition of Christ* in the Museum. Isolated images, such as that of *St Sebastian*, also arrived on the island. Although this latter figure is now housed in the Museum, it belonged to the chapel of the same name. There is also another *Virgin and Child*, originating from the Capela of Nossa Senhora da Ajuda."

en.name: Dawud Pasha’s bedroom
short_description: This bedroom belonged to the first *mutasarrif* (ruler) of the Mount Lebanon *mutasarrifiyya*, Dawud Pasha, who governed from 1861–68). The room is furnished with one double bed, one baldachin bed, two curtains, one rug, two embroidery panels, two bedside tables and a coffer. A thin off-white mattress covered in silk and embroidered in gold thread rests on each bed, and both frames are covered with light blue silk draperies. Three small, rectangular off-white silk pillows rest against the baldachin bed's adjustable headboard. Two square pillows rest on the double bed. The blue silk drapery on the bed frames was also used for the identical silk curtains. The curtains served a purely decorative function and could not be closed, as they were sewn to the valances, which are made with off-white silk and gold embroidery. The curtains are held back with golden tiebacks hooked on golden metal knobs. The embroidery panels on the walls are also made with the same off-white silk, and feature a variety of floral designs. The two dark, wooden bedside tables resemble classical columns and the coffer is made with a lighter wood and decorated with floral bas-reliefs.
keywords: Needlework; Furniture; Floral decoration; Embroidery

en.name: *Commercial port. Marseille*
short_description: Frédéric Alexianu (aka F. Hugo d'Alesi) was a painter who quickly became specialised in advertisement posters for different kinds of transports, and in educational maps. This poster, aimed at primary school children, uses the example of Marseille to illustrate a trading port. The artist draws attention to the different commercial activities undertaken here, in addition to the transport of passengers on an ocean liner. The port of Marseille was the most important Mediterranean port in France, as it facilitated a great number of commercial exchanges with the French colonies in North Africa.
keywords: Commerce; transports; ports; colonies; enseignement

fr.name: *Port marchand. Marseille*
short_description: Frédéric Alexianu (F. Hugo d'Alesi) est un peintre qui s'est rapidement spécialisé dans les affiches publicitaires pour les différents moyens de transport et les cartes murales à destination pédagogique. Ce support prévu pour les enfants des écoles primaires donne à voir un port marchand avec l'exemple de Marseille. Le peintre a prévu de montrer les différentes activités de commerce ainsi que le transport de personnes avec un paquebot. Le port de Marseille était en effet le principal port méditerranéen de la France, et permettait en particulier d'assurer les échanges très denses de marchandises avec les colonies françaises d'Afrique du Nord.
keywords: Commerce; transports; ports; colonies; enseignement

ar.name: كاميو
description: يُصوِّر هذا الكاميو البيضاوي الشكل الإمبراطور المغولي شاه جهان (حكم من ١٠٣٧ إلى ١٠٦٨ هـ/١٦٢٨ إلى ١٦٥٨ م)، حيث يظهر بصورة جانبية، وهو يتحلى بالكثير من الجواهر. يُرجح أن هذا النموذج مأخوذ من اللوحات المغولية. توجد مجموعة صغيرة من الكاميو المُؤرَّخة بدقة من عهد شاه جهان، تُنسب جميعها إلى صائغي أحجار كريمة أوروبيين عملوا في بلاط الإمبراطور. استمرَّت صناعة صور الكاميو الشبيهة بهذه في القرون اللاحقة، بيد صائغي أحجار كريمة هنود في الغالب، وكانت تُثبَّت في قلادات مرصعة بالجواهر.
dates: القرن الثالث عشر الهجري / القرن التاسع عشر الميلادي
keywords: كاميو؛ مجوهرات؛ مغول؛ شاه جهان؛ الهند

en.name: Cameo
description: This oval shaped cameo depicts the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan (r. AH 1037-1068 / AD 1628-1658). He is shown in profile, richly jewelled, a model most likely taken from Mughal paintings. A small group of securely dated cameos exist from the period of Shah Jahan, all of which have been attributed to European lapidaries who worked at the court of the emperor. Cameos like this one continued to be made in later centuries, often by Indian lapidaries, and set into jewelled pendants to be worn.
keywords: Cameo; Jewellery; Mughal; Shah Jahan; India

ar.name: سوق القطانين.
description:
يمتد سوق القطانين من الشرق إلى الغرب 95 م. ويحتوي هذا السوق التجاري على خان وحمامين وصفين من الحوانيت يضم كل صف منهما ثلاثين حانوتاً. السوق ذو تخطيط مستطيل، وسقفه معقود بقبو برميلي تقسّمه سلسلة من العقود إلى ثلاثين جزءاً، فُتح في كل جزء منها فتحة إنارة سقفيّةلإدخال الهواء والضوء إلى داخل السوق. بُني السوق من حجارة مهذبة بيضاء تحولت إلى رمادية بمرور الزمن. وزوّد كل حانوت بمصراع خشبي.  
  
السوق له مدخلان: شرقي وغربي. المدخل الشرقي هو باب القطانين الذي يفتح على الجهة الغربية من الحرم. وقد بُني هذا المدخل بعناية فائقة، وهو يعتبر تحفة معمارية. يتكون المدخل من حنية ذات عقد ثلاثي الفصوص محاطة بحنية أخرى كبيرة يتوجها عقد مدبب سُقف بنصف قبة ترتكز على خمسة صفوف من المقرنصات الحجرية. بُني المدخل من الحجر بالألوان الأسود والأحمر والرمادي، وصُفَّت الحجارة بعناية فائقة وبأسلوب الأبلق. هذا التوافق في الألوان مألوف في عمارة القدس الإسلامية، خاصة في المباني التي تعود للفترة المملوكية. أما المدخل الغربي للسوق، فهو أبسط في تكوينه المعماري من المدخل الشرقي، حيث يتكون من فتحة باب مستطيلة يعلوها عتب كبير. ويتكوّن العتب من سبع صنج معشقة، ويعلوه عقد تخفيف فُتحت فوقه نافذة دائرية. وتقع عناصر المدخل هذه في حائط مرتد يحيط به عقد مدبّب كبير.  
  
يُعتبر سوق القطانين من أكمل وأجمل الأسواق في فلسطين، بل في بلاد الشام. وتمتع السوق بدخل وفير خُصِّص للنفقة على الحرم الشريف وعلى مشاريع الأمير تنكز الناصري التي أقامها في القدس مثل المدرسة التنكزية.

أحد أجمل أسواق مدينة القدس على الإطلاق، لم تجرِ عليه تغييرات جوهرية، منذ أن تمَّ إنشاؤه. وهذا السوق عبارة عن قاعة سوق مستطيلة الشكل، بطول حوالي 95 م، يحيط به على الجانبين صفَّان من الدكاكين، يبلغ عددها 60 دكاناً، بالإضافة إلى وجود خان وحمَّامين. يتَّصل السوق بالحرم الشريف من جهة الشرق، حيث أنه متعامد مع الجدار الغربي له، وذلك عبر بوابة فخمة، تُعتبر من أجمل المباني المملوكية في المدينة.
artist: السلطان الملك الناصر محمد بن قلاوون (حكم ثلاث مرات في الأعوام 693 – 694 / 1294 – 1295، و 698 – 708 / 1299 – 1309، و 709 – 741 / 1309 – 1340)، والأمير تنكز الناصري (توفي عام 741 / 1340) الذي  كان نائب السلطان في الشام في الفترة 712 – 740 / 1312 – 1340.
هناك توقيع لأحد الحرفيين الذين اشتغلوا في تنفيذ المبنى حُفر في وجه مقرنص يقع عند فتحه إنارة سقفية في وسط السوق.  كُتب التوقيع بخط النسخ المملوكي، ونصّه
keywords: أبلق؛ أبواب الحرم؛ باب؛ باب القطانين؛ حانوت؛ حمام؛ خان؛ سوق؛ سوق القطانين؛ صنج؛ صنجات معشقة؛ عقد تخفيف؛ مقرنص.

en.name: Suq al-Qattanin (Market of the Cotton Merchants).
description:
The Suq al-Qattanin extends from east to west measuring approximately 95 m. This commercial *suq* contains a *caravanserai*, two *hammams*, and two rows of 30 shops, totalling 60 shops in all. The *suq* is designed on a rectangular plan, and has a ceiling that is arched with a barrel-shaped vault divided into a series of arches totalling 30 sections. Each section opens up into a skylight to allow light and air into the interior. The *suq* was built of white dressed stone that has turned ashen grey over time. Each shop has a wooden door.  
The *suq* has two entrances, one on the east and the other on the west. The east entrance is called Bab al-Qattanin (Gate of the Cotton Merchants), which opens on to the west side of the Haram. This entrance was built with meticulous care and is considered an architectural rarity. The entrance consists of a recess with a tri-lobed arch, encircled by another large recess. This recess is crowned by a tapered arch and topped by a semi-dome that is supported by five tiers of stone *muqarnas*. The entrance was built from black, grey and red stone and arranged with meticulous attention in the *ablaq* style, whose correspondence of colour is well known in the Islamic architecture of Jerusalem, especially in those buildings that date to the Mamluk period.  
The west entrance to the *suq* is simpler in both design and architectural composition and consists of a rectangular portal, above which is a large lintel. The lintel consists of seven joggled stones, on top of which rests a relieving arch. A circular window opens out above it. The elements of this entrance are located within a recessed wall surrounded by a large pointed arch.  
The Suq al-Qattanin is considered to be one of the most complete and beautiful *suqs* not only in Palestine, but in the whole of Bilad al-Sham (Greater Syria). Income from the *suq* was allocated to the Haram al-Sharif, and towards projects in Jerusalem undertaken by Amir Tankaz al-Nasiri, such as the Madrasa Tankaziyya.

This suq is the most beautiful market in the city. It has not undergone fundamental changes since it was built. The *suq* is characterised by a rectangular market hall approximately 95 m long. It is surrounded on two sides by two rows of shops, 60 in total, in addition to a *khan* (inn) and two bathhouses. On the east side of the suq an imposing portal, considered to be one of the most beautiful Mamluk monuments in the city, opens onto the west side of al-Haram al-Sharif.
artist: Mamluk sultan, al-Nasir Muhammad bin Qalawun (who ruled three times: AH 693–4, 698–708 and 709–41 / AD 1294–5, 1299–1309 and 1309–40), and Amir Tankaz al-Nasiri (d. AH 741 / AD 1340), who was deputy to the sultanate in Bilad al-Sham (Greater Syria) during the period AH 712–40 / AD 1312–40.

Carved on a *muqarnas* façade on the opening of a skylight in the middle of the *suq* there is a signature of one of the craftsmen who worked on the construction of the *suq*. Written in Mamluk *naskhi* script, the inscription reads: “May God have mercy on him, the work of Muhammad bin Ahmad bin ‘Alish”.
keywords: Ablaq; Bab al-Qattanin; shop; carvanserai; Suq; interjoined voussoir; relieving arch; muqarnas

es.name: Zoco al-Qattanin (de los comerciantes de algodón).
description:
El zoco al-Qattanin se extiende de este a oeste y mide de aproximadamente 95 m. Dispone de un caravasar, dos baños y dos filas de treinta tiendas, es decir, sesenta tiendas en total. Es de planta rectangular y está cubierto por una bóveda de cañón dividida en treinta tramos por una serie de arcos. En cada tramo hay un tragaluz que ilumina y airea el espacio. El zoco se construyó con sillares blancos que se han vuelto grises con el tiempo. Cada tienda tiene una puerta de madera.  
El zoco tiene dos entradas, una al este y otra al oeste. La entrada oriental se llama Bab al-Qattanin (puerta de los comerciantes de algodón) y da al lado oeste del Haram. Esta entrada es arquitectónicamente singular y se construyó con verdadero esmero. Presenta una zona rehundida con un arco trilobulado, inscrito en otra zona rehundida mayor coronada con un arco apuntado y una semicúpula que reposa sobre cinco hileras de mocárabes de piedra. La entrada está construida con piedras negras, grises y rojas dispuestas en estilo *ablaq* con precisión, un estilo popular en la arquitectura islámica de Jerusalén, sobre todo en la época mameluca.  
La entrada occidental del zoco es más sencilla tanto en diseño como en composición arquitectónica. Presenta un portal rectangular sobre el que se aprecia un gran dintel de siete piedras sobre el que se abren un arco de descarga y una ventana circular. Todos los elementos de esta entrada están retranqueados dentro de un vano de arco apuntado del muro.  
El zoco al-Qattanin se considera uno de los más completos y bellos no sólo de Palestina, sino de todo el Bilad al-Sham (la Gran Siria). Los ingresos de este zoco se invertían en el propio Haram al-Sharif o en proyectos que emprendió el emir Tankaz al-Nasiri en Jerusalén, como la madrasa Tankaziyya.

Se trata del zoco más bello de la ciudad y no ha sufrido grandes cambios desde su construcción. Se trata de un espacio rectangular de aproximadamente 95 m de longitud. Incluye dos filas de tiendas, sesenta en total, junto con el *jan* (hospedería) y dos casas de baños. El impresionante portal oriental, que se abre al lado occidental del Haram al-Sharif, es uno de los monumentos mamelucos más importantes de la ciudad.
artist: El sultán mameluco al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun (r. 693-94 / 1294-95, 698-708 / 1299-1309 y 709-741 / 1309-1340) y el emir Tankaz al-Nasiri (m. 741 / 1340), delegado del sultanato en el Bilad al-Sham (la Gran Siria) en los años 712-740 / 1312-1340.

Uno de los artesanos que participó en la construcción del zoco dejó su firma en el tragaluz de una fachada de mocárabes que está en el centro del zoco. Es una inscripción escrita en letra *nasji* mameluca que dice así: “Que Dios se apiade de él, obra de Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Alish”.
keywords: Ablaq; Bab al-Qattanin; tienda; caravanserai; zoco; dovela entrecruzada; arco de descarga; muqarnas.

fr.name: Souk al-Qattanine (marché des marchands de coton).
description:
Orienté est-ouest, le souk al-Qattanine de plan rectangulaire mesure environ 95 m de long. Il contient un caravansérail, deux hammams et deux rangées de 30 échoppes chacun. Sa couverture est en voûte en berceau divisée en 30 sections. Chacune bénéficie d'un jour qui permet à l'air et à la lumière de pénétrer. La pierre de taille utilisée pour la construction était blanche à l'origine, mais a grisé avec le temps. Chaque échoppe est fermée par une porte en bois.  
Le souk possède deux entrées, l'une à l'est, l'autre à l'ouest. L'entrée orientale appelée Bab al-Qattanine (porte des Marchands de coton) ouvre vers le côté ouest du Haram. Réalisée avec un luxe particulier, elle est d'une grande valeur architecturale. Elle consiste en une niche à arc trilobé dans un important retrait surmonté d'un arc brisé et d'une demi-coupole soutenue par cinq rangées de *mouqarnas* de pierre. Le traitement en pierre noire, grise et rouge appareillée en style *ablaq*, est fréquent dans l'architecture islamique de la ville, en particulier dans les bâtiments de la période mamelouke.  
L'entrée occidentale est de plan et de composition architecturale plus simples. Elle présente un portail rectangulaire surmonté d'un important linteau composé de sept pierres à joints à adent sur lequel vient un arc de décharge surmonté d'un oculus. L'ensemble occupe une importante niche qui s'ouvre par un grand arc brisé.  
Le souk al-Qattanine est considéré comme l'un des plus complets et plus beaux souks non seulement de Palestine mais aussi de toute la région de Bilad al-Cham (Grande Syrie). Les revenus du souk allaient au Haram al-Charif et à d'autres travaux lancés à Jérusalem par l'émir Tankaz al-Nasiri, dont la *madrasa* Tankaziyya.

Ce souk est le plus beau marché de la ville. Il n’a pas subi de changements notables depuis sa construction. Le souk est caractérisé par une salle de marché rectangulaire d’environ 95 m de long. Il est encadré sur deux côtés par deux rangs d’échoppes, 60 au total, en plus d’un *khan* (caravansérail) et de deux hammams. Sur le côté est du souk, un imposant portail, considéré comme l’un des plus beaux monuments mamelouks de la ville, s’ouvre sur le côté ouest du Haram al-Charif.
artist: Sultan mamelouk al-Nasir Muhammad bin Qalawun (qui régna à trois reprises : 693-694 H / 1294-1295 J.-C. ; 698-708 H / 1299-1309 J.-C. ; 709-741 H / 1309-1340 J.-C.) et émir Tankaz al-Nasiri (m. 741 H / 1340 J.-C.), représentant du sultan pour Bilad al-Cham (Grande Syrie) en 712-740 H / 1312-1340 J.-C.

La signature de l’un des artisans qui participa à la construction est gravée sur une face en *mouqarnas* de l’ouverture aménagée dans la voûte centrale du souk. Rédigée en écriture *naskhi* mamelouke, elle se lit : “Que Dieu le tienne en sa compassion, œuvre de Muhammad bin Ahmad bin ‘Alich.”
keywords: Ablaq ; Bab al-Qattanine ; boutiques ; caravansérails ; souks ; voussoirs à joints à adents ; arc de décharge

ar.name: القصر ب.
description:
يعتبر القصر ب جزءاً من المجمع الملكي الكبير الواقع إلى الشمال من مدينة الرقة الحالية (الرافقة) الذي أنشأه هارون الرشيد، وقد اختار الرافقة كمقر لإقامته في الفترة بين 180 و192/ 796 و808. يتضمن المجمع سبعة قصور ومقرين للإقامة، وتغطي جميعها مساحة تصل إلى حوالي 10 كم2. تبلغ أبعاد القصر الأعظم بينها، وهو قصر السلام، 350×300م، وقد كان مكان إقامة الخليفة، أما القصور الأخرى التي تمت تسميتها A, B, C, D، والقصران الشرقي والغربي، فيبدو أنها كانت لإقامة عائلة الخليفة والحاشية الملكية. ويذكر المؤرخ الطبري، المتوفى عام 310/ 923، أن زوجة الخليفة زبيدة، وورثته الأمين والمأمون والقاسم والمعتصم، قد أقاموا فيها. كان مقر الإقامة الذي تم توسيعه حديثاً مركزاً للقيادة الحربية، ومركزاً إدارياً للدولة العباسية حيث يتم حفظ ثروة الخليفة، كما ضمت العاصمة الجديدة مجموعة كبيرة من النشاطات الصناعية. وتدل البقايا التي تم العثور عليها خارج السور الشمالي على ورشات إنتاج الفخار والزجاج على نطاق واسع.  
مخطط القصر ب متوازي أضلاع يتجه شمال جنوب، طوله 115م وعرض الجدار الجنوبي 74.6م، وعرض الجدار الشمالي 69.7م. الجدار الخارجي مزود بدعامات دائرية عرضها 1.4م. تقع بوابة القصر التي يبلغ عرضها 17م في الواجهة الشمالية، ويسبقها سور ذو دعامات يحيط بحديقة خارجية.  
تبلغ سماكة السور 1.5م، وقد تم بناؤه من الآجر المجفف بالشمس، وتقويته في بعض المواضع بالآجر المشوي. يفضي المدخل الرئيس إلى الجناح الغربي من القصر الذي كان يشغله موظفو البلاط، وهو يتألف من فسحة سماوية واسعة مبلطة بالآجر المشوي، ومحاطة برواق. وقد تم العثور على العديد من كسر الزخارف الجصية المنقوشة والملونة في هذه المنطقة مما يعطي معلومات عن نظام زخارفه الأساس. تفضي ثلاثة أبواب في الجدار الجنوبي إلى مجموعة من الغرف الرسمية تضم قاعتين، إحداهما مبلطة بالآجر الزجاجي. يضم الجناح الشرقي الذي يمكن الوصول إليه عبر ثلاثة أبواب منفصلة من الأحياء الرسمية المنطقة السكنية، وهي تضم بدورها المطبخ والحمامات ومقراً واسعاً للضيوف مزوداً بفسحة سماوية، ويكمل كلاً من الجناح الرسمي والخاص من القصر حديقة مسورة إلى الجنوب.  
تم إكساء الجدران الخارجية والداخلية للقصر التي كانت مرئية للجمهور بطبقة من الجص الأبيض، كما تمت زخرفة المناطق الرسمية والهامة ولاسيما البوابات بأفاريز من الزخارف الجصية النافرة على شكل أوراق الكرمة بشكل أساس. وعلى الرغم من تشابهها مع النماذج الزخرفية الأموية، إلا أن زخارف الرقة تستلهم مباشرة من النماذج الكلاسيكية لاسيما تلك الموجودة في المدينة الصحراوية تدمر التي تبعد عنها حوالي 180 كم جنوباً.  
تدل القطع المؤرشفة الكثيرة التي يقارب عددها 400 قطعة، والتي تضم كسراً من الزخارف الجصية المنقوشة والملونة، واللوحات الخشبية المحفورة والمذهبة، والقطع الزجاجية، والمجوهرات، على تجهيزات القصر الفخمة.

قرَّر الخليفة العباسي هارون الرشيد (حكم 170- 193 هـ/ 786-809 م) بناء قصر لعائلته ولمساعديه خارج أسوار مدينة الرقة. اختار منطقة بمساحة تقريبية تبلغ 10 كم مربع، من شمال المدينة، وأمر ببناء مجموعة القصور هذه. من هذه القصور اعتبر القصر B من أهم القصور، لما يحتويه من الموجودات الفنية والمعمارية المميزة والفريدة. قُسِّم القصر إلى جزئين، رسمي وخاص, وكلاهما زُوُّد بحدائق. من التصاميم والزخارف الموجودة، كان الجص المحفور، واللوحات الجدارية الجصية، وكذلك اللوحات الجدارية المرسوم على خلفيات من الخشب والسيراميك الفخم، والزجاج، والمجوهرات.
artist: الخليفة هارون الرشيد الذي حكم في الفترة 70-193/ 786-809.
keywords: عمارة قصور.
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

en.name: Palace B.
description:
Palace B is part of the extensive palatial complex to the north of modern-day Raqqa (Rafiqa), erected by Caliph Harun al-Rashid, who chose Rafiqa as his residence from AH 180 to 192 (AD 796 to 808). The complex comprises seven palaces and two residential ensembles covering an area of almost 10 sq km. The most monumental palace of the complex, Qasr al-Salam, which measures 350 m x 300 m, served as the caliph's residence. The other palaces, identified as palaces A, B, C, D, as well as the west and east palaces, probably housed family members and court officials. As historian al-Tabari (d. AH 310 / AD 923) records, the caliph's wife Zubayda, and his heirs, al-Amin, al-Ma'mun, al-Qasim and al-Mu'tasim, all resided there. The newly extended residence was also the army-command centre and the administrative centre of the Abbasid Empire where the caliph's treasuries were safeguarded. The new capital also housed considerable industrial activities. Remains found outside the northern city-wall testify to the existence of pottery- and glass-production workshops.  
The plan of Palace B shows a north–south oriented parallelogram that measures 115 m in length, and which is 74.6 m wide at the southern wall, and 69.7 m wide at the northern wall. The outer walls are articulated by 1.4 m-wide round buttresses. The palace's 17 m-wide entrance is located along the northern façade, preceded by a buttressed enclosure comprising the outer garden.  
The walls are 1.5 m thick and built of sun-dried bricks occasionally strengthened by fired bricks. The main entrance provides access to the western wing of the palace which accommodated the court officials consisting of a spacious courtyard paved with fired bricks and surrounded by a peristyle colonnade. Numerous painted and carved stucco fragments were found in this area, thus providing some information regarding its original decorative program. Three doorways in the south wall lead to a series of official rooms comprising two halls, one of them paved with glass tiles. The eastern section, which can be accessed by three separate doorways in the official's quarters, comprises the residential areas. These contain the kitchen, bathrooms, and a spacious guest house with a courtyard. Both the official and private wings of the palace are completed by an enclosed garden to the south.  
Both the exterior and interior walls of the palace that were in public view were coated with white plaster. The official, prestigious areas, especially the doorways, were decorated with stucco friezes in deep relief consisting primarily of vine ornaments. Despite the resemblance to Umayyad decorative motifs, the motifs from Raqqa rely directly on classical prototypes, specifically those found in the desert city of Palmyra, about 180 km further south.  
An abundant inventory of nearly 400 pieces, including carved and painted stucco fragments, a carved and gilded wooden panel, ceramics, glass objects and jewellery, testify to the sumptuous equipment of this palace.

The 'Abbasid Caliph Harun al-Rashid (r. AH 170–93 / AD 786–809) decided to build a palatial complex for his family and administrative elite outside the walls of Raqqa city. He chose an area of almost 10 sq km to the north of the city and commissioned a complex of seven palaces. Among them, Palace B has yielded many important artistic and architectural finds. Its space is divided into two parts, official and private, both provided with an enclosed garden. Decorative artefacts found include carved and painted stucco and wooden panels as well as luxurious ceramics, glass and jewellery.
keywords: palatial architecture
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

es.name: Palacio B.
description:
El Palacio B forma parte del gran complejo palaciego situado al norte de la actual al-Raqqa y fue construido por el califa Harun al-Rashid, que eligió al-Rafiqa como su residencia entre 180 / 796 y 192 / 808. El complejo comprende siete palacios y dos conjuntos residenciales que abarcan un área de casi 10 km². Qasr al-Salam, el palacio más monumental de todos, mide 350 × 300 m y era la residencia del califa. El resto de los palacios, conocidos como palacios A, B, C y D, así como los palacios Este y Oeste, probablemente fueron la residencia de los miembros de la familia y funcionarios de la corte. Como relata el historiador al-Tabari (m. 310 / 923), Zubayda, mujer del califa, y sus herederos al-Amin, al-Ma’mun, al-Qasim y al-Mu'tasim vivían allí. La residencia, una vez ampliada, albergó también el mando del ejército y el centro administrativo, donde se custodiaban los tesoros del califa. Además, en la nueva capital se desarrolló una importante actividad industrial. Fuera de la muralla norte se han encontrado restos que sugieren la existencia de talleres de producción de cerámica y vidrio.  
La planta del palacio es un paralelogramo orientado de norte a sur que mide 115 m de longitud y tiene 74,6 m de ancho en el muro sur y 69,7 m en el muro norte. El muro exterior está reforzado con contrafuertes semicirculares de 1,4 m de ancho. La entrada del palacio, de 17 m de ancho, está situada en la fachada norte y precedida de un recinto amurallado, también con contrafuertes, que comprende el jardín exterior.  
La muralla, de 1,5 m de espesor, son de ladrillo secado al sol, aunque algunos están reforzados con ladrillos de barro cocido. La entrada principal da acceso al ala oeste del palacio, que acogía a los funcionarios de la corte y contaba con un espacioso patio de suelo de ladrillo cocido, rodeado de un peristilo. En esta zona se encontraron muchos fragmentos de estuco tallado y pintado que proporcionan cierta información sobre la decoración empleada. Las tres entradas del lado sur conducen a una serie de salas oficiales, dos de las cuales son vestíbulos pavimentados con azulejos de vidrio. La sección este, a la que se entra por tres puertas distintas desde las dependencias de los funcionarios, comprende la zona residencial. Aquí se encuentran la cocina, los baños y una espaciosa casa de huéspedes con un patio. Las dos alas del palacio, la oficial y la privada, se completan con sendos jardines interiores en la parte sur.  
Los muros exteriores e interiores del palacio que quedaban a la vista estaban revestidos con escayola. Las zonas oficiales, de protocolo, especialmente las entradas, estaban decoradas con frisos de estuco en altorrelieve adornados principalmente con vides. Pese a su similitud con los motivos decorativos omeyas, la ornamentación de al-Raqqa se inspira directamente en los prototipos clásicos, en concreto en los encontrados en Palmira, ciudad situada en el desierto, unos 180 km al sur.  
Un amplio inventario de casi 400 piezas, entre ellas varios fragmentos de estuco tallado y pintado, un tablero de madera tallada y dorada, objetos de vidrio y joyas, deja constancia de la suntuosidad de este palacio.

El califa abbasí Harun al-Rashid (r. 170-193 / 786-809) decidió construir un complejo palaciego para su familia y la élite administrativa extramuros de la ciudad de al-Raqqa. Eligió una zona de 10 km² al norte de la ciudad y encargó un conjunto de siete palacios. Uno de ellos, el Palacio B, ha brindado importantes hallazgos artísticos y arquitectónicos. Está dividido en dos partes, la oficial y la privada, con sendos jardines interiores. Estaba decorado con estuco tallado y pintado, y paneles de madera, y se han hallado asimismo joyas y lujosos objetos de cerámica y vidrio.
keywords: Arquitectura palaciega
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

fr.name: Palais B.
description:
Le Palais B fait partie du vaste complexe palatial situé au nord de la moderne Raqqa (Rafiqa), érigé par le calife Haroun al-Rachid qui fit de Rafiqa sa résidence de 180 à 192 H / 796-808 J.-C. Le complexe comprend sept palais et deux ensembles résidentiels recouvrant une surface de près de 10 km carrés. Le bâtiment le plus monumental, Qasr al-Salam (350 x 300 m), était la résidence califale. Les autres palais appelés palais A, B, C et D, ainsi que le palais occidental et le palais oriental, étaient probablement réservés aux membres de la famille royale et aux hauts personnages de la cour. Comme le rapporte l'historien al-Tabari (m. 310 H / 923 J.-C.), l'épouse du calife, Zoubayda et ses héritiers, al-Amin, al Mamoun, al-Qasim et al-Moutasim, résidaient tous à Rafiqa. La nouvelle résidence était également le quartier général des armées et le centre administratif de l'empire abbasside où les trésors du calife étaient conservés. La nouvelle capitale abritait par ailleurs des activités industrielles considérables. Des vestiges trouvés devant le rempart nord de la cité confirment la présence d'ateliers de production de poterie et de verrerie.  
Le plan du palais B est en forme de parallélogramme orienté nord-sud de 115 m de long par 74,6 m de large au sud et 69,7 m au nord. Les murs extérieurs sont rythmés par des contreforts circulaires de 1,4 m de diamètre. L'entrée du palais, de 17 m de large, se trouve sur la façade nord, précédée par une enceinte à contreforts entourant le jardin extérieur.  
Les murs de 1,5 m d'épaisseur sont montés en briques crues parfois renforcées par des briques en terre cuite. L'entrée principale donne accès à l'aile ouest réservée aux dignitaires de la cour. On y pénètre par une vaste cour pavée de briques entourée d'un péristyle. De nombreux fragments de stuc peint ou sculpté trouvés dans cette zone fournissent diverses informations sur le programme décoratif d'origine. Trois passages dans le mur sud conduisent à une suite de salles officielles comprenant deux halls dont l'un était pavé de carreaux de verre. La section orientale, à laquelle on a accès par trois passages séparés à partir des quartiers officiels, comprend la partie résidentielle. Les ailes privées et officielles du palais sont agrémentées d'un jardin clos au sud.  
Les murs du palais, aussi bien sur leurs faces extérieures qu'intérieures ouvertes à la vue, étaient recouverts de plâtre blanc. Les parties officielles et prestigieuses, en particulier les entrées de portes, étaient décorées de fresques en stuc sculptées en profond relief consistant essentiellement en ornements inspirés du thème de la vigne. Malgré la ressemblance avec les motifs décoratifs omeyyades, ceux de Raqqa renvoient directement à des prototypes classiques, trouvés par exemple dans le désert à Palmyre, à 180 km plus au sud.  
L'abondant inventaire de près de 400 pièces comprenant des fragments de stuc peint et sculpté, un panneau de bois sculpté et doré, des céramiques, des objets en verre et des bijoux témoigne de la somptuosité des aménagements de ce palais.

Le calife abbasside Haroun al-Rachid (r. 170-193 H / 786-809 J.-C.) décida de construire un complexe palatial pour sa famille et son administration hors de Raqqa. Il choisit un site de près de 10 km carrés au nord de la ville et fit élever un complexe de 7 palais. Parmi eux, le palais B a révélé de nombreux et importants éléments architecturaux et artistiques. Il est divisé en deux parties – officielle et privée –, toutes deux dotées d'un jardin clos. On y a trouvé des panneaux de bois sculpté ou de stuc sculptés et de luxueux objets en céramique et en verre ainsi que des bijoux.
keywords: Architecture palatiale
partner: Ministry of Culture, Directorate General of Museums and Antiquities

de.name: Bernhardisaal (Fürstensaal)
description: Der sich über zwei Geschosse erstreckende Bernhardisaal in der Mitte des westlichen Konventtraktes ist ein architektonisch an sich einfacher rechteckiger Saal, dessen Besonderheit eine rechteckige Deckenöffnung mit umlaufender Balustrade ausmacht, ein „Hypäthralraum“, der eine Öffnung zum Himmel illusioniert. Zum Prunksaal wird der Raum erst durch die Wand- und Deckenmalereien, die die gesamte Fläche füllen. Eine Folge von Szenen aus dem Leben des Ordensgründers, des hl. Bernhard von Clairvaux, gipfelt in der Weihnachtsvision oberhalb der Deckenöffnung.
artist: Johann Martin und Georg Anton Gumpp (Baumeister); Franz Michael Hueber und Anton Zoller (Freskanten)

en.name: Bernhardisaal (Fürstensaal)
description: Architecturally, the Bernhardisaal, extending over two storeys, is a simple rectangular room whose distinguishing feature is a rectangular opening in the ceiling with perimeter balustrade, a “hypaethral space” which gives the illusion of an opening onto heaven. It is the wall and ceiling paintings, covering the entire surface, that first turn the room into a ceremonial hall. A sequence of scenes from the life of the founder of the order, St. Bernhard of Clairvaux, culminates in the Christmas vision above the ceiling opening.
place: Central pavilion of the western monastery wing, the so called “Bernhardibau”, Cistercian Monastery of Stams
artist: Johann Martin Gumpp the elder (1643–1729) and Georg Anton Gumpp (1682–1754); Franz Michael Hueber (?–1746), Anton Zoller (1695–1768)

ar.name: منمنمة مصحف
description:
هذا المصحف المنمنم نسخ في عام 1758 في إيران ومن المحتمل في مدينة أصفهان تحت حكم سلالة عائلة الزند الحاكمة من قبل الخطاط محمد هاشم الأصفهاني. ويوجد صفحة مزدوجة مزخرفة بشكل كثيف بنظام لوني أزرق ، ذهبي وأحمر والذي يعرض النص. وخط النقش الصغير  
يعطي أحكام التجويد بالأحمر بينما توجد وريدات ذهبية تشير لنهاية كل آية. وبلوك النص مؤطر بحدود ذهبية ذات سعيفات معينة الشكل ورصائع برعمية في هوامش تحوي عدد الآيات. بينما النص والتذهيب في هذا الشكل الصغير الشائع تم تشكيله في القرن الثامن والتجليد المطلي بالورنيش / اللكر الذي ما يزال موجودا يمكن أن يعود تاريخه للقرن التاسع عشر وهذا المصحف تم تجليده باستخدام قماش قطني أبيض مخاط مع طباعة باليد لتصميم مزهر بالأحمر والأزرق مثبتة بواسطة مشبك خطافي مزركش / مخرم ذهبي. وعلبة القطن تعطي مؤشر على كيفية حفظ هذه المخطوطات أو تغطيتها لحمايتها خلال السفر.
materials: حبر ، ألوان وذهب على ورق. الخط صغير نقشي 20 سطر على الصفحة.
tags: حبر ، ألوان وذهب على ورق. الخط صغير نقشي 20 سطر على الصفحة.

en.name: Miniature Qur’an
description: This miniature Qur’an was copied in 1758 in Iran, likely in the city of Isfahan under the Zand dynasty, by the scribe Muhammad Hashim al-Isfahani. A densely decorated double page in a blue, gold and red colour scheme introduces the text. The calligraphic small *naskh* script is vocalised in red, while golden rosettes signal the end of each verse. The text block is framed by a gold border with golden diamond-, palmette-, and bud-shaped medallions in the margins containing the verse count. While text and illumination in this popular small format were created in the 18th century, the extant lacquer binding can be dated to the early 19th century. This Qur’an was enfolded in a white sewn cotton cloth with a hand-printed red and blue floral design fastened with a gold filigree hook clasp. The cotton case gives an indication of how these manuscripts might have been stored or how their covers could be protected during travel.
keywords: Calligraphy; illumination; naskh; Qur’an
materials: Ink, colour and gold on paper. Calligraphic small *naskh* script of 20 lines per page.
tags: Ink, colour and gold on paper. Calligraphic small naskh script of 20 lines per page.

en.name: Badshahi Ashurkhana
description:
The Badshahi Ashurkhana is a Shia shrine located near what was known as Khudadad Mahal, which is now called Pathergatti. It was commissioned by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, ruler of Golconda and Hyderabad from 1580–1612, at the same time as he planned the new city of Hyderabad. Construction commenced in 1592 and lasted four years.  
  
The Qutb Shahi rulers, who had Persian roots, built this splendid structure out of a need for a shrine for their Shia subjects on the subcontinent. It is said that during the Qutb Shahi dynasty, when the Sultan visited the shrine to attend *majalis* (religious gatherings), the space would be illuminated with more than 10,000 lamps arranged in rows and the shape of trees.  
  
Badashi Ashurkhana is visited by devotees throughout the year, but especially during *Muharram*, the first month of the Islamic calendar. During this month, *majalis* are held at the shrine to commemorate the martyrdom of Husain, grandson of the Prophet Muhammad, at the Battle of Karbala in 680 AD (10 Muharram in the year 61 AH of the Islamic calendar). Apart from the memorial gathering, the shrine also hosts *jashn*, celebrations of the birthdays of holy personalities.  
  
The main gateway to the monument was constructed under the rule of *Nawab* Mir Nizam Ali Khan (1762–1803). The gate opens into a vast courtyard with a shrine on the left-hand side. Towards the right and opposite the main gate are two other structures, which are decorated with massive *alams*, or battle standards, during *Muharram*. The second entrance to the shrine is surrounded by a garden.  
  
The main hall of the shrine is the oldest portion of the structure, commissioned by Sultan Mohammad Quli Qutub Shah V in 1611. It is divided into three parts, and the walls of the main section are covered in Persian enamelled tile work with arabesque designs and Arabic calligraphy. The eastern and western sections of the halls have walls covered with old photographs and the names of the *Ahl al-Bayt*, the family of the Prophet Muhammad. The walls are also inscribed with the name of the reigning sovereign and the dates of construction for the main hall. The eastern and western sides, which stand on a series of wooden colonnades, were constructed later.  
  
During the Qutb Shahi dynasty, several *alams* made of gold and precious stones were installed in the shrine. Despite the age of the monument, it has been maintained well and is still structurally sound. The beauty and brilliance of the enamel tile work is still evident. The monument belongs to and is maintained by the private estate of the *Nizam*, or ruler of Hyderabad.

en.name: *La Sahrienne: Arab dance for piano*
short_description: The rise of "turkeries" in the 18th century is a good example of the influence of the widespread fascination with the "Orient" on music. In the 19th century, this Orientalism also influenced others art forms, such as painting and photography. Musical motifs started using "oriental" motifs once again in the early 20th century.
artist: Composer: P. Codini; illustrator: A. Morel
keywords: Music; Middle East

fr.name: *La Saharienne: danse arabe pour piano*
short_description: Dès le XVIIIe siècle, le goût pour l'Orient se manifeste dans la musique avec les "turqueries". L'orientalisme touche toutefois davantage au XIXe siècle des arts comme la peinture ou la photographie. Au début du XXe siècle, des motifs musicaux reprennent des motifs d'origine orientale.
keywords: Musique; Orient

ar.name: سجادة لوتو
description: السجاد الذي يظهر هذا التصميم الملفت لأرابيسك نباتي ذو طراز خاص باللون الأصفر على أرضية حمراء يعرف غالبا بسجاد لوتو نسبة للقطعة في مذبح الكنيسة الإيطالية الشهيرة المصنوعة من قبل الرسام الإيطالي في عصر النهضة لورينزو لوتو التي تظهر سجادة مشابهة . وتظهر الأمثلة الأولى على سجاد لوتو حدود مثل هذه المبينة هنا ويعتقد أنها مشتقة من شكل خطي مستقيم للخط الكوفي وهذا النوع من الحدود المتداخلة هو مميز للعديد من السجاد التركي الأول.
dates: القرن العاشر – بداية القرن الحادي عشر هجري /القرن السادس عشر ميلادي
